(#822 did this, broke live streaming, and was reverted #825.) The armed path: - drives a genuine **multi-round** turn through the **real composer** and confirms the loop actually ran multiple rounds (≥1 tool execution / `.agent-thread-node`); - asserts, via a **DOM MutationObserver** on `#chat-history`, that **exactly one** assistant bubble is mounted for the whole turn and it **grows** (net-new `.msg-ai` == 1, added == 1); - asserts **no per-round teardown/re-mount churn** (removed == 0, no hidden per-round holders — this covers the WS `done`-branch discard + N-bubble reconstruction the redo must eliminate); - asserts the preserved invariants: reply/reasoning **channel split** (reasoning stays in `.thinking-section`, never leaks into the public body) and a **single-round** turn still renders as one clean bubble (byte-identity spirit). The key check runs only after the feature is present, so a keyed nightly pre-feature also self-skips cleanly. The sentinel is the codebase's issue-tag convention — the redo carries the literal `#829` tag in `chat.js` (as `#985`/`#830`/`#891`/`#993` all do); absent today. Read failure ⇒ ABSENT (fail-safe: never a false "present", the key is never spent pre-feature). ## No fenced file touched `chat.js`/`chatRenderer.js`/`orwellWs.js`/`ws_routes.py`/`agent_loop.py`/`chat_helpers.py`/`momentPrompts.ts`/`src/engine/**`/`tool_schemas.py`/`registry.ts`/`tests/golden/**` were **read-only inspection only**. Run by the other overseer, keyed: `cd frontend && OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-… python3 scripts/_verify_coalesce_live.py`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Tests** * Added a feature-guarded end-to-end live verification runner for streamed chat interactions. * Automatically self-skips when the required UI artifact isn’t present, avoiding unintended live calls. * When enabled, runs real chat turns through the UI and verifies stable single-bubble assistant rendering across both multi-round and single-round flows. * Captures evidence (screenshots, logs, and detailed verdict/observations) and records results for troubleshooting.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge with low risk. The change is isolated to a new live verification script and is feature-gated before any live model call. No new actionable issues were identified in the current diff. No files require special attention.

T-Rex Logs

author: mingodynasty
body:
Addresses the four items of post-ship feedback on the Playlist Overview changes.

## 1. Hide/Unhide use icons
The visibility column now renders a masked eye icon instead of the Hide/Unhide text links, following the layers-panel convention: **open eye = row visible** (click hides), **struck-out eye = row hidden** (click unhides). Two Material Symbols SVGs are vendored under `assets/icons/` (same Iconify source and format as the existing set), recolored via CSS mask exactly like `local_icon`. The cell keeps an `aria-label` and the existing consequence tooltip.

## 2. Show hidden remembers its toggle
The switch now has Dash `persistence=True` (localStorage), so the management view reopens the way it was left. Verified live: toggle on → full page reload → still on, hidden rows load muted with struck-out eyes.

## 3. Refresh button: busy state, done signal, spam-proof
- The `refresh_rank` callback's `running=` hook drives the button's `loading` spinner for the duration of the fetch; Mantine's loading state also sets `disabled`, so the button cannot be spam-clicked into repeat KovaaK's calls while one refresh is in flight.
- A green toast confirms completion. It uses a fresh id per refresh because `sendNotifications` `show` silently ignores a duplicate id while the previous toast is visible — a fixed id would eat the "done" cue on back-to-back refreshes.
- Failure paths keep their red `dash_logger` toast and skip the green confirmation.
- The handler now guards `n_clicks`, so DashProxy's known initial-load duplicate fire can't force a network refresh or pop a stray toast.

## 4. Type column fits "Benchmark"
`autoSize` can run before the grid's rows arrive, leaving auto-sized columns at their `minWidth` floor — and the 110px floor ellipsized the BENCHMARK pill. The floor is now 140px (pill measures ~92px + quartz cell padding).

## Verification
- All gates green locally: pytest (370 passed), ruff format, ruff check, mypy, compileall.
- Verified live in the running app: eye icons render/toggle/recolor, both SVGs serve 200, persistence survives reload, Benchmark badge fits with no overflow, and the Refresh button held `data-loading`/`disabled` for the full ~10s of a fetch before toasting. The KovaaK's API was returning 503s/timeouts during testing, so the *red* done-toast path is what ran live; the green path is unit-tested and differs only in API health.

author: imrohitagrawal
body:
## Summary

The orchestrator predicted whether the vector retrieval arm degraded **from config alone** (`is_index_embedder_mismatch(configured_identity, index_stamp)`) and used that to gate the answer-cache write. That prediction mis-gated in two opposite directions — both left as debt by #65 (PR #69):

- **#70 (false negative → cached a degraded answer):** a *transient* `EmbedderUnavailable` (Tier-1 outage) degrades the vector arm, but that is not predictable from the index stamp, so the weaker exact+keyword answer was cached and frozen to TTL until the provider recovered.
- **#72 (false positive → needlessly skipped a cacheable answer):** an `exact_lookup` short-circuit returns exact-only evidence **without ever consulting the vector arm** — an embedder-independent, non-degraded answer — yet it was skipped from cache under a config mismatch.

Both issues note the clean fix is the **same plumbing**: report the vector arm's ACTUAL runtime degrade back from `retrieve()` and gate on that.

## The fix (shared root cause → one change)

- `HybridRetriever.retrieve` now returns `RetrievalResult(hits, vector_degrade)` carrying a `VectorDegrade` reason (`none | mismatch | unavailable`), **sourced at the degrade site** in `_safe_vector_retrieve`.
- The orchestrator gates the cache write on `vector_degrade is VectorDegrade.none` and **labels the skip WARN from the reason itself** — `mismatch` → the existing `answer_cache_write_skipped_embedder_mismatch`; transient → new `answer_cache_write_skipped_vector_unavailable`.
- The config-only prediction is removed from the write path; `_retrieve_active_index` no longer resolves the embedder stamp (only version + source hash).

Carrying the reason at its source (rather than a bool re-labeled by a config re-prediction in the orchestrator) removes a non-local invariant flagged in review: the label is now correct by construction, even for an injected `_RetrieverLike` double.

## Not regressed

- **#65:** a genuine Tier-3 mismatch on a non-short-circuit path still skips the write **and** re-emits `vector_retrieval_index_embedder_mismatch` on the next ask (nothing cached → retrieval re-runs).
- **#57/#71:** `_vector_arm_enabled` still delegates to the shared `is_index_embedder_mismatch` predicate (one source of truth).
- The `exact_lookup` **fall-through** (no exact hit) still consults and degrades the vector arm — the boundary of the #72 carve-out is guarded by a dedicated test.
- No schema / migration / public-API / cache-key change; existing cache rows stay valid.

## Test evidence

- **488 passed / 9 skipped** (6 net-new tests over the 482 baseline); `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `pyright app/` all clean.
- New real-hybrid regressions: #70 transient outage (monkeypatched `EmbedderUnavailable`), #72 exact-lookup cached under a mismatch (+ 2nd ask cache hit), #65 mismatch skip, and the exact-lookup fall-through degrade boundary; plus `_safe_vector_retrieve` reason assertions.

## Review

Blast-radius battery (T2→T3): correctness/adversarial, silent-failure, and type-design reviews + a test-coverage pass. Findings addressed: type-design (bool → reason enum; documented `frozen, eq=False` dataclass) and coverage (exact-lookup fall-through; real transient outage) folded into this change. `release-readiness-review` → **SHIP**.

Closes #70
Closes #72

author: n8watkins
body:
## Captains, first-class

Makes creating a control-capable CAPTAIN a real UI action instead of the fragile manual raw-socket dance (spawn `capability:control` → resize → `claude --resume` → `claim_captain` → `move_tile`). Companion to #67, which made the ORCHESTRATOR first-class; this does the same for captains/crew across three slices.

### Depends on #67 (create-orchestrator) — DRAFT until it merges
This branch is **based on `create-orchestrator` (#67)**, not `main`, and builds directly on the surfaces #67 owns (the spawn path, sidebar, Tile.tsx, `commands.rs`, `captain.ts`). It is rebased onto #67's latest tip (through `9fb28f3`, the PR#67 review-round fixes). **Base retargets to `main` once #67 merges.** The three commits here are the only diff over #67.

### 1. UI control-spawn toggle (`feat(spawn)`)
The backend already honored `SpawnOptions.capability` and fired `audit_ui_control_spawn` (item-3) — only the frontend opt-in was missing, so every normally-spawned terminal was stranded at the read tier.
- `types.ts` `SpawnOptions` gains `capability?: "read" | "control"`.
- `SpawnMenu` adds a default-OFF, visibly-distinct **"Control terminal"** toggle (accent-tinted row + shield when armed). A preset picked while armed spawns with `capability:"control"`; otherwise read. Inverted least-privilege preserved — control is always the deliberate opt-in.
- `Canvas.spawn` threads the tier to `spawnTerminal`; a plain shell spawn is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **before/after:** ordinary spawn ⇒ read (pure-work session); toggle armed ⇒ control (full token, audited).

### 2. Captain/crown sync — verify + regression guards (`test(captain)`)
The audit's BUG-2 found controlBridge "mostly syncs correctly." Verified the whole path end-to-end and confirmed it IS correct: backend `captains_sync_apply` broadcast → `adoptCaptainsSnapshot` **preserves `role:"cortana"`** (`controlBridge.ts:129`) → `adoptCaptainsRegistry` adopts the crown and clears a stale one. Added the bypass-would-fail guards that were missing:
- adopting a server-declared cortana this client never set locally (claim from another client / window reload); tracking it via `orchestratorId` only, never as a pinned captain (FleetRole split); crown convergence on a transfer.
- the wire→record boundary preserves `role:"cortana"` into `orchestratorId`.

### 3. Readable ~80-col background floor (`fix(terminal)`)
Client-tracked tile sizing: a **watched** tile fits its real box down to `MIN_SANE_COLS` (a narrow split is legitimate), but an **unwatched/background** tile now refuses to shrink below the ratified readable floor `MIN_READABLE_COLS = 80`, so a freshly created captain/crew tile stays readable before anyone views it (and a captain's `capture-pane` read of it never wraps to garbage).
- `saneFitProposal` gains an optional `minCols` floor; `Terminal.tsx` picks it from `foregroundRef` at the three fit sites (resize / initial-attach / zoom).
- **Floor, don't force:** refusing a sub-80 shrink reuses #65's exact null-guard mechanism, so it can't resurrect the 2-col wedge (floor is 80) or the 220 overshoot (a watched tile still fits exactly; we never grow past the real box). Respects #65's `reassert-window-size-latest` design.

## Tests / gates (rebased on #67 `9fb28f3`)
- `cargo test --lib`: **534 passed, 0 failed** (adds 2 pure `capability_is_control` gate tests).
- `vitest`: **409 passed** across 38 files (adds 14: SpawnMenu toggle ×5, terminalFit readable-floor ×5, captain cortana-adoption ×3, controlBridge wire-role ×1).
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean. `clippy --lib`: no new warnings (the pre-existing control.rs warnings are unchanged; none in the changed code).

## Not covered
- **Click-test / E2E:** like #67, verifying the toggle-armed spawn actually mints a control-token session and that a real control op succeeds from it needs a verify-install of the built app (WSLg). The audit-fires-on-control-spawn path is exercised by the existing item-3 backend wiring; the toggle→`capability:"control"` plumbing is unit-tested but not click-tested here.
- **Cross-client cortana UNMARK:** `adoptCaptainsRegistry` deliberately does NOT clear a still-live crown on a snapshot that merely omits cortana (avoids flapping during a release-then-claim transfer). So a cortana *unmark* driven from another client does not clear the crown on other clients until that terminal dies. Left as-is (documented in-code); out of scope.
- **Flake:** one full-suite run showed a single unrelated intermittent failure (a pre-existing timing flake); 4 subsequent full runs were 409/409. Not caused by these changes (the added tests are deterministic).

author: hariswahidkhan-star
body:
Implements the requested functional improvements. Reuses existing architecture throughout (founding-application flow, `Storage` upload pipeline, `Mailer`, `site_settings`) so nothing is bolted on.

## 1. Registration — Confirm password
Confirm-password field on the sign-up form with client-side match validation, **and** a server-side re-check (`/api/register` → `400 password_mismatch`) so a mismatch can never create an account.

## 2. Country dropdown (single source)
Already a proper list-of-values from the central `frontend/src/data/countries.ts` (sign-up + onboarding), with dial-code auto-fill. The public honorary form ships an inline copy (static HTML can't import the TS module).

## 3. Public certification-routes table
Added the approved **Route / Fee / Exam / Result / who-it's-for** table to the membership "Three routes" section — responsive (mobile horizontal-scroll), on-brand, and linking the new Honorary form.

| Route | Fee | Exam | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard (always on) | Paid | Yes | PCP-AI (earned) |
| Founding (time-boxed) | Free | Yes | PCP-AI (earned) |
| Honorary (board-conferred) | Free | No | Honorary Fellow (PCI) — labelled honorary |

## 4–5. Honorary Route application (separate from student registration) + board review
- **Public form** `backend/wwwroot/honorary-application.html`: personal / professional / qualification details, résumé/CV + optional document uploads, declaration + consent → `POST /api/honorary-application`, shows the reference on success.
- **Backend** `HonoraryApplication.cs`: public submit (validated + stored via `Storage`, `PCI-HONAPP-…` reference) and owner-only list / detail / **document download** / decide. **Approve confers a real, verifiable `PCI-HON` award** via a shared `Honorary.ConferAward(...)` — and never creates any exam/entitlement/credential row.
- **Admin UI** `HonoraryApplications.tsx` (owner-only) → *Access & pricing → Honorary applications*: review, download files, add notes, approve / reject / mark under review.

## 6–8. Reusable notification service + admin config
`Core/Notify.cs` delivers by email (via the provider-agnostic `Mailer`) and records every attempt in a new `notification_history` ledger; `Channel { Email, Sms, InApp }` is the seam for later. Applicant confirmation + board alert on submit, applicant email on decision. Recipient / on-off / subject overrides are **owner-configurable in Admin → Settings** (`notify_admin_email`, `notify_honorary_enabled`, `notify_honorary_ack_subject`, `notify_honorary_admin_subject`) — nothing hardcoded; SMTP stays env-configured.

## 9. Security
`Storage` enforces a MIME allow-list (pdf/jpg/png/webp), a 3 MB cap and magic-byte sniffing (renamed payloads rejected). All inputs trimmed + length-capped server-side; email regex-validated; the public endpoint is rate-limited; admin review is owner-only and downloads are scoped to the parent application.

## 10. Database
New tables (SQLite + MySQL + idempotent `Migrate.cs`): `honorary_applications`, `honorary_application_documents`, `notification_history`, plus the notification settings seeds.

## 11. Tests & docs
- `backend/tests/honorary_application_test.py` — **20 assertions**, wired into CI (SQLite + MySQL jobs): submit + validation, owner-only RBAC, detail + document download, approve → verifiable award, **no exam-shaped rows created**, double-approve 409, notification ledger, confirm-password server check.
- `docs/HONORARY_ROUTE_AND_REGISTRATION.md` documents every file, DB change and the workflow.

## Verification
- Backend + both SPAs build clean.
- Playwright: the public form submits with a file upload end-to-end (reference issued); the sign-up country dropdown + phone render.
- Live API run: submit → review → download the real PDF → approve → `PCI-HON` award publicly verifiable → 3 notification rows.
- smoke 65/65 · integration 148/148 · founding 46/46 · honorary 19/19 · honorary-application 20/20.

**Invariant preserved:** approving an honorary application confers honorary recognition only — it is always labelled honorary and is never the examined PCP-AI credential.

body: # 知识库升级 · P1（统一解析层 + 结构感知切块） 基于 P0（#33）。解决评估中确认的两个问题：**三套并行解析级联互不一致**、**切块破坏文档结构（表格被拦腰截断、标题层级丢失）**。 ## 1. 统一解析层（`services/parsing.py`） 单一入口 `parse_document(content, ext)`，文件上传、URL 导入、专利 PDF 下载、P0 全文获取四条路径全部收口于此（此前 `ingestion.py` / `pdf_downloader.py` 各自维护 markitdown→pypdf 级联，规则不一致）。 **PDF 解析器注册表**（`FORMUMIND_PDF_PARSER` 控制）： | 层级 | 输出质量 | 依赖 | |---|---|---| | marker | 版面感知真 Markdown、表格保真 | 重型可选（`parse_pro` extra） | | MinerU (magic-pdf) | 最高保真、公式/OCR | 重型可选（自装即用） | | MarkItDown | 通用轻量 | `file_ingest` extra（现状默认） | | pypdf | 纯文本兜底 | `file_ingest` extra | `auto`（默认）按最优先探测逐级回退；指定名称则固定首选、仍向下回退。所有层级缺库时静默降级，`ParseResult.parser` 记录实际产出者供溯源。 **网页正文**：`html_to_markdown()` 用 trafilatura 抽正文（去导航/广告/页脚，输出 Markdown、保留表格），回退旧正则剥标签。`ingest_url` 与 P0 web 全文获取共用。 依赖目录/`pyproject` 新增 trafilatura（`file_ingest`）与 marker-pdf（新 `parse_pro` extra），依赖管理 UI 可一键安装。**MinerU 不进一键目录**（安装体积/环境要求苛刻），但装了就会被 auto 层级探测到——与评估结论一致：作为可插拔层引入，不作硬依赖。 ## 2. 结构感知切块（`services/chunking.py`） - `chunk_markdown()`：按 ATX 标题分节并维护**标题路径**，chunk 标题变为 `专利 (p.3) · 实施例 > 实施例 2`——TF-IDF/ColBERT 检索与引用可见文档位置； - **表格与代码块原子化**：永不从行中间截断（超长表格整体成块）——半张配方表对配方抽取毫无价值； - 围栏内的 `# 行` 不误判为标题； - 无结构纯文本**逐字节退化**为旧递归切分器（测试断言两者输出一致），非 Markdown 解析器行为完全不变；旧 `_chunk_text` 保留为签名兼容别名。 ## 验证 - 新增 17 个测试：PDF 层级顺序/固定/逐级回退、`FORMUMIND_PDF_PARSER` 生效、HTML 回退剥标签、标题路径、表格/围栏原子性、围栏内伪标题、纯文本退化一致性、ingest/pdf_downloader 委托、无依赖 Tj 兜底仍可用。 - 兼容性修正：`_chunk_text` 别名补回 `max_depth` 参数（被现有 `test_chunk_max_depth` 抓到）。 - 全量后端：**527 通过**、8 跳过（3 个 pandas 环境失败为 main 已存在）。

author: bluedevilcollectibles
body:
## Summary
# WO ID
**WO-HARNESS-M19-CANARY-REDESIGN-01**

---

## CRITICAL — Ambiguities That Must Be Resolved Before/During Build (Rule 1 + Architect Rule 7)

1. **Canonical FULL spec is not reachable in this worktree.** Verified directly: `docs/board/` does not exist anywhere in this `bdc-harness` worktree (confirmed via `find docs/board -maxdepth 2` returning nothing — not just the two named motion files, the entire directory is absent). The WO text states the FULL spec is authoritative and required reading before starting, and that it carries "the complete file list, exact schema, message templates, and the two board-caught defects." Since `target_repo` for this WO is `bdc-harness` but `SPEC_PATH=github:bluedevilcollectibles/bdc-xo:docs/work-orders/...`, the motions almost certainly live in `bdc-xo`. The builder must either (a) fetch the motion files cross-repo via `gh api repos/bluedevilcollectibles/bdc-xo/contents/docs/board/motions/...` before writing message templates / exact Layer 2 trigger wiring, or (b) proceed on this WO's own Sections 7-12 text only (stated to be a "summary," not the full detail) and flag any place a decision was made without the FULL spec. **Do not guess at message templates or file lists the WO explicitly defers to the FULL spec.** If the FULL spec cannot be fetched, build strictly to what Sections 7-12 specify verbatim and note the gap in the completion manifest.
2. **Migration number collision — VERIFIED.** `ls migrations/` confirms `024_smart_cauldron_reliability.sql` through `028_agent_dispatch.sql` already exist; `024` is taken. **Use `migrations/029_known_bad_bindings.sql`** instead — mechanical fix, not a design change, does not require going back to the board.
3. **Dual schema-write requirement not mentioned in spec — VERIFIED.** Confirmed via `packages/core/src/db/adapters/sqlite.ts`: it contains 19+ inline `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` statements (lines 262-554), including recent additions like `remote_agent_supervisor_incidents`, `agent_dispatch_messages`, `agent_dispatch_workers` — every prior migration that added a table was mirrored here, auto-run on every boot. Confirmed `known_bad_bindings`/`knownBadBindings` currently has **zero** references anywhere in the repo (grep returned no matches), consistent with `PRECHECK_VERDICT=needs-build`. The builder MUST add a matching `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS known_bad_bindings (...)` block to `sqlite.ts` or the table silently won't exist on SQLite-backed dev/test runs.
4. **Layer 2 event-trigger wiring mechanism is underspecified.** Section 8's bullet list names *conditions* but not *where in the codebase* those are detected (GitHub webhook handler? CI step? CLI command?). This is exactly the kind of architectural judgment call that should come from the FULL spec or General, not be invented by the builder. **Recommend:** implement Layer 2 as a small, explicitly-invoked function (`packages/canary-suite/src/probe-runner.ts` exports a `runLayer2TrivialFire(lane)` entry point) plus the fixture workflow YAML, and wire the *trigger detection* (webhook/CI/operator-command call site) as a follow-up WO unless the FULL spec is retrieved and specifies the call site. Do not invent a new GitHub webhook handler or cron-adjacent polling loop to "guess" the trigger — that risks recreating the exact cron mistake M-19 forbids.
5. **WO Class says `CODE` but Section 11/12 requires INFRA-grade runtime evidence** (`docker logs archon-app-1`, deployment to the dev/staging container). Per Rule 14, CODE WOs only require `validate-manifest.sh`; this WO also demands INFRA evidence. Treat this WO as **MIXED** for validation-evidence purposes regardless of its declared Class, and produce both `validate-manifest.sh` output AND the runtime `docker logs`/probe-block evidence in the completion manifest.
6. **Build order / PR strategy.** The WO permits either one PR or stacked PRs, mandating only that Layer 1 merge first. Given the size (5 packages touched, 1 migration, 1 executor hot-path change, 1 new default workflow), **recommend 4 stacked PRs** (Layer 1 -> Layer 3 -> Layer 0 -> Layer 2) onto a shared feature branch chain, each independently reviewable and revertable (Reversibility principle). This is a recommendation, not a hard requirement — flag to General if single-PR is preferred instead.

---

## Files to modify

| File | Layer | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/providers/src/codex/provider.ts` | 1 | Replace local `isModelAccessError` pattern list (verified at line 161, dispatch order verified at lines 244-257: `isModelAccessError` -> `ROLLOUT_MISSING_PATTERNS` -> `AUTH_PATTERNS`) with a call into the new shared `probe-classifier.ts`; keep `classifyCodexError` dispatch shape unchanged so existing retry/failback tests still pass. Must not weaken the existing precedence order or `AUTH_FAILBACK_PATTERNS` (all-must-match) semantics. |
| `packages/workflows/src/dag-executor.ts` | 1 | Extract the provider/model/binding-identity portion of `resolveNodeProviderAndModel` (verified: function starts at line 1205, return block at ~1420-1428 returns `{ provider, model: effectiveModel, options, declaredModelId, personaContextState }`) into the new shared resolution module; `dag-executor.ts` imports and calls it instead of inlining. Persona resolution, capability-warning messaging, and the existing return shape must be preserved byte-for-byte for existing callers (verified 3 call sites at lines ~4301, ~5065, ~5245 including the failover path) and tests. |
| `packages/workflows/src/executor.ts` | 1 | Add the fire-time probe gate call (via the shared resolution module + `fire-time-probe.ts`) before any DAG node dispatch. Must block on structural rejection, warn-and-proceed on transient/unknown, per Section 8 data flow. |
| `packages/canary-suite/src/reducer.ts` | 3 | Demote static-only `passed` verdict (verified current logic at lines 1-45: success path returns `verdict: failed.length > 0 ? author: yueranyuan
body:
## Problem

`evidence_sha_stale` in `boilerplates/presets/simple-gh-sdlc.ts`
required an evidence commit to be **equal** to the PR head sha
(`shaMatches`). That rejects honest multi-commit evidence: an earlier
commit captured at the moment the work actually happened (a baseline
screenshot, a dry-run, an intermediate implementation commit), cited
alongside a `PR:` line naming the eventual head. The only way to pass
today is to fraudulently claim every earlier evidence line was
captured at the final head sha — which it wasn't.

This is a prerequisite for a committed-store workflow that captures
multi-commit evidence trails as work happens, rather than only at the
final merge commit.

## Fix

The rule now accepts any evidence commit reachable as an **ancestor**
of (or equal to) the PR head, via `git merge-base --is-ancestor`
(`isAncestorOfPrHead`). Equality is the degenerate case of ancestry
(a commit is its own ancestor), so this subsumes the old `shaMatches`
equality check while additionally accepting any earlier commit on the
PR branch's own line of history. Fabricated or unreachable shas (not
an ancestor of the head, and not the head itself) still fail closed —
same posture as before.

`isAncestorOfPrHead` needs the project's git root to shell out
against, which a rule's `when` doesn't otherwise see (only the derived
model, not the raw `PresetContextInput`). `loadContext` now stashes
`input.projectRoot` into a module-scoped variable read later by the
rule — a narrow, documented seam, instead of widening the strict
`Context.git` schema for one derived boolean.

## Proof

New test `boilerplates/presets/evidenceShaAncestor.e2e.test.ts` —
black-box e2e against a **real git repo** (not a synthetic `Context`
fixture like the existing unit tests in `simple-gh-sdlc.test.ts`,
which remain green and unaffected — they exercise the
equality-preserving case with no `projectRoot`, so the ancestry check
correctly falls back to the old exact-match behavior):

1. An evidence commit that is an **earlier commit on the PR branch's
   own history** (a true ancestor of the head) passes — no
   `evidence_sha_stale`.
2. A real commit that exists in the repo but sits on an **unrelated
   branch** (not reachable from the PR branch's head) still fires
   `evidence_sha_stale`.
3. A **fabricated/nonexistent** sha still fails, as
   `evidence_commit_not_found` — never silently ancestor-accepted.

```
$ bun test boilerplates/presets/evidenceShaAncestor.e2e.test.ts
 3 pass
 0 fail
 16 expect() calls
Ran 3 tests across 1 file.

$ bun test boilerplates/
 188 pass
 5 skip
 0 fail
 417 expect() calls
Ran 193 tests across 8 files.

$ bun run typecheck && bun run build
(clean)
```

Full-suite run (`bun test`) in progress at PR-open time; will confirm
green in a follow-up comment if anything surprising turns up, but the
touched-surface (`boilerplates/`) suite above is fully green and the
change is additive/narrowing-safe (existing synthetic-context tests
never set `projectRoot`, so they hit the same fallback path as
before).

Not merging — for maintainer/loop review.

author: usirin
body:
Fixes #2658

## What

Adds `pipeline-cli campaign verify-trace <wave-label> [--founder <login>]` — a **fail-closed founder-approval-trace verifier** in the readme-guard/fanout-guard idiom (a pure, IO-free, unit-tested core + a thin Effect bin over `gh api` REST).

The campaign skill is **invoker-agnostic** — a human *or* an agent may run it — so there is no human-at-keyboard guard like `release`'s. The sole authorization that a wave-labeled cluster may become a campaign is a durable, auditable, founder-authored approval marker bound to the wave label, and this verifier **default-DENIES** so that neither an agent nor a human can conjure a campaign the founder never approved.

## The founder-approval trace shape (pinned)

A campaign is authorized only by a **founder-authored comment** — on any issue carrying the wave label — whose **first line** is:

```
campaign-approve: <wave-label> · <ISO-8601-UTC>
```

- **`<wave-label>`** must equal the wave label under verification (binds the approval to *this* cluster — a valid approval of one wave never authorizes another).
- **`<ISO-8601-UTC>`** must be a valid ISO-8601 UTC instant (records *when* approval was granted; auditable after the fact).
- **author** must be the **founder** — identity injected via config (`--founder`, else `$CAMPAIGN_FOUNDER_LOGIN`), never hardcoded (no named identity in a committed artifact).

Emphasis-tolerant leading `**`, case-insensitive keyword, line-one anchored (a mid-body quote never counts). Grounded in the gated-audit-wave play, where findings are returned to the founder for approval *before* anything is filed.

## Exit contract (ADR 0092)

Exit `0` **only** on a present, well-formed, founder-authored, wave-bound trace. Every other input fails closed (non-zero), each covered by a unit test:

| Failure | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `zero-scope` | empty wave label, no founder identity configured, or the label names zero issues |
| `absent` | cluster non-empty but no `campaign-approve:` marker |
| `malformed` | a marker exists but is malformed or bound to a different wave |
| `non-founder-author` | a well-formed, wave-bound marker exists but no author is the founder |

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The trace shape is pinned as a checkable, auditable artifact bound to the wave label, documented in the tool surface (command docblock + tool `README.md`).
- [x] `campaign verify-trace` (readme-guard idiom: pure core + thin Effect bin) returns pass only for a present, well-formed, founder-authored trace.
- [x] Fails closed (non-zero) on a missing trace, a malformed trace, a non-founder author, and zero scope — each covered by a unit test.
- [x] The pure core is unit-tested over fixtures without spawning `gh` (`campaign-trace.unit.test.ts`, 22 tests).

## Files

- `packages/pipeline-cli/src/tools/campaign/campaign-trace.ts` — the pure IO-free core (marker grammar + default-deny decision + report)
- `packages/pipeline-cli/src/tools/campaign/campaign-trace.unit.test.ts` — 22 unit tests, the four fail-closed paths covered exhaustively
- `packages/pipeline-cli/src/tools/campaign/github.ts` — the `gh api` REST boundary (gathers the wave-labeled cluster + its comments)
- `packages/pipeline-cli/src/tools/campaign/command.ts` — the CLI wiring
- `packages/pipeline-cli/src/tools/campaign/README.md` — the tool surface documenting the trace shape
- `packages/pipeline-cli/src/registry.ts` — registers the `campaign` command

## Local checks

- `pnpm typecheck` — clean (28/28 workspace projects)
- `pnpm lint:worktree` — clean
- unit tests — 22/22 pass

author: claude[bot]
body:
## Summary

Implement Fiduccia-Mattheyses / Kernighan-Lin style local refinement over a Partition. The refinement module evaluates single-vertex moves and pair swaps, recomputing gain after every move to iteratively improve cut cost. Pair moves resolve 2-cycles by construction; combined with single-vertex moves they also resolve longer cycles.

## Decisions made

- **Used `external - internal` for gain formula** (not `internal - external`).
  Reason: Aligns with standard KL convention where positive gain indicates improvement.

- **Stored best_swap as (i, j, part_a, part_b, gain) tuple**.
  Reason: Simplifies deterministic tie-breaking; can compare full tuples directly.

- **Added `Partition::from_assignment(pub(crate))` helper to partition.rs**.
  Reason: Minimal additive API per spec; enables mutable partition construction in refinement loops.

- **Used enumerate().skip() over range loops**.
  Reason: Clippy compliance; more idiomatic Rust iteration.

## Test plan

- [x] 2-cycle (swap) resolves: entities A/B with strong soft edge co-locate after refinement
- [x] 3-cycle resolves: triangle of soft edges reduces cut cost beyond what 2-cycle alone achieves
- [x] Never worsens: random-ish partition never increases cut cost after refinement
- [x] Hard edge respected: entities with Hard edges never separated by refinement
- [x] Capacity respected: refinement never exceeds partition capacity
- [x] Determinism: refining same input twice produces identical output
- [x] Idempotent convergence: refining already-optimal partition preserves cost

All tests in `refinement::tests` pass. `cargo clippy -D warnings` clean. `cargo fmt --all` applied.

Refs #247

author: sandonemaki
body:
## Summary

`QueryStmt.One` (the prepared-statement query path) leaks the `sql.Rows` —
and with `database/sql`, the pool connection holding them — on **every call**.

`One` passes the rows from `stmt.QueryContext` to `scan.OneFromRows`, which by
contract does not close caller-owned rows (`scan.One` does, `scan.OneFromRows`
does not), and `One` never closes them itself:

```go
rows, err := s.stmt.QueryContext(ctx, args...)
if err != nil {
    return t, err
}

t, err = scan.OneFromRows(ctx, s.mapper, rows)   // rows never closed
```

Because `One` reads a single row and never exhausts the result set,
`database/sql` cannot auto-release the connection. Each call permanently
holds one pool connection; a service using a prepared `One` in a request
handler exhausts the pool and PostgreSQL starts rejecting connections:

```
pq: sorry, too many clients already (53300)
```

This reproduces on every released version (verified on v0.42.0 and main)
against a real PostgreSQL 17 with a plain `bob.PrepareQueryx(...).One(...)`
loop.

## Changes

- `QueryStmt.One`: close the rows as soon as `scan.OneFromRows` returns
  (before the extra loaders run, matching the ordering of the non-prepared
  exec path where `scan.One` closes rows before `bob`'s loaders execute).
  A close error is returned if scanning itself succeeded.
- `QueryStmt.All`: the happy path exhausts the rows so `database/sql`
  auto-releases the connection, but a scan error mid-iteration leaked them —
  now closed explicitly on every path.
- `QueryStmt.Cursor`: rows ownership moves to the returned cursor, but when
  `scan.CursorFromRows` itself fails the rows leaked — now closed on that
  error path.
- `stmt_test.go` (new): regression tests using a fake `Preparer`/`Rows` that
  record whether `Close` was called — happy path, `sql.ErrNoRows` path,
  `All` happy path and `All` scan-error path. All four fail without this fix.

## Testing

- The four new regression tests fail on current main and pass with the fix.
- End-to-end: on a `MaxOpenConns(1)` pool, 10 consecutive `One` calls block
  forever without the fix (the leaked connection is never returned) and pass
  with it.
- `go test .` / `go vet .` pass.

## 概要

従業員マスタ（CustomUser化）・担当スケジュール・出退勤記録を追加。
Slack連携（Socket Modeワーカー）が前提とするモデル群はこのPRで揃う。

## 追加機能

- **employeesアプリ新設**
  - `Employee`（AbstractUser継承）を `AUTH_USER_MODEL` に設定。将来のログイン機能の土台
  - フィールド: Slack ID（メンバーID）・フリガナ・電話番号・在籍フラグ
  - スタッフ一覧・新規登録・更新・削除画面（サイドバー「スタッフ一覧」から）
- **担当スケジュール**（`Assignment`: 従業員×利用者×日付）
  - 日付ごとの割当て一覧・追加・削除。同一割当ての重複防止つき
  - Slackの日報プルダウン生成用クエリを想定した設計（docs/slack_handover.md 7章参照）
- **出退勤記録**（`Attendance`）

`AUTH_USER_MODEL` 変更のため**既存DBのリセットが必要**（モックデータのみ確認済みの前提）:

```bash
docker compose down -v        # DBボリューム削除

docker compose exec web python manage.py migrate
docker compose exec web python manage.py createsuperuser
```

## Resumen

### 1. Llamadas de video 1:1 (reemplaza el botón de pánico)
Botón 📹 en el header de cada chat 1:1 (no en el chat familiar — solo entre dos personas). Cualquier invitado puede llamar a Kiomi y viceversa:

- Señalización vía Firebase Realtime Database (`calls/{par de usuarios}`): oferta/respuesta SDP + intercambio de candidatos ICE.
- Solo STUN gratuito de Google (sin servidor TURN, que tiene costo) — funciona bien en la misma WiFi y en muchas redes móviles, pero puede fallar en combinaciones de red más restrictivas. Documentado en el README.
- Pantalla completa de llamada: saliente, entrante (timbre sintetizado + vibración en Android), y activa (video local en miniatura + remoto, mutear micrófono, apagar cámara, colgar).
- Nueva Cloud Function `onIncomingCall` que avisa por push cuando entra una llamada, para que suene con la app cerrada.
- Queda un registro en el chat («📹 Llamada de video · 2:15», perdida/rechazada/cancelada), como WhatsApp.
- Se quita todo el código del botón de pánico (ya reemplazado).

### 2. Pestañas Kiomi / Familia para invitados
Antes había un solo botón que alternaba el texto. Ahora son dos pestañas fijas y visibles a la vez, cada una con su propia bolita roja de no-leídos — así el invitado ve de un vistazo cuál tiene mensajes nuevos antes de entrar, sin tener que cambiar de pestaña para averiguarlo.

## Plan de pruebas

- [x] Verificado con Firebase simulado + cámara/micrófono falsos reales de Chromium (no mockeados — negociación WebRTC real de extremo a extremo): botón de llamada visible solo en 1:1; iniciar llamada genera una oferta SDP real y muestra la pantalla saliente; el otro lado detecta la llamada entrante con el nombre correcto y puede contestar (genera respuesta SDP real); ambos lados terminan en la pantalla "activa"; colgar corta la llamada y deja exactamente **un** registro en el chat (se encontró y corrigió un bug real de duplicado); cero errores de consola en ambos lados.
- [x] Pestañas con bolita roja verificadas: solo se cuenta como no-leído lo que el invitado no está viendo activamente.
- [ ] Falta probar en dispositivos reales — en particular, confirmar que la llamada conecta en la combinación de redes real de la familia (WiFi vs. datos móviles) dado que solo se usa STUN.

author: jenner-analytics
body:
[Jenneranalytics.com](https://jenneranalytics.com) provides an API that runs SAS code, with support for more than 200 SAS procedures. You can also use it with AI assistants in a collaborative workspace. It's available for Mac on the Apple App Store, and by license for Windows and Linux.

We support the larger community by
(1) increasing access to SAS-compatible systems,
(2) by providing test coverage and a test coverage framework to public SAS repos in order to encourage the use of best practices in software engineering.

Your 01_libname_setting.sas runs on Jenner unmodified — this PR adds a small compatibility bundle so you can see for yourself. It's the test we wrote for your package, shared in case it's useful, and was assembled with AI assistance as is most code in modern businesses today.

The `%condition` macro in `01_libname_setting.sas` is a clean piece of design: one macro, called thirteen times (Cancer, heart, renal, stroke, alzheimer, cirrhosis, frailty, lung_failure, neurodegenerative, both diabetes tiers, hiv_aids, dme), each call pulling a differently-named sheet out of the same disease-codes workbook and dropping a ready-to-use `A_<category>` code list into the macro symbol table via `PROC SQL SELECT INTO`. That's a lot cleaner than the alternative of hand-writing thirteen near-identical import blocks, and the pediatric ICD-10-CM/PCS lists further down the same file (neuro, cardio, respiratory, renal, gastro, hemo, metabolic, congenital, malignancy, prematurity) look like real clinical-coding curation rather than boilerplate.

`jenner-check/` in this PR holds four small bundles built from four different files in this repo — the condition-code macro above, the DME claims filter from `02_condition.sas`, the enrollment/age-bucketing and expenditure logic from `04_enrollment.sas`, and the survey-contents-and-merge pipeline from `SC_P01.sas` — each paired with mock data standing in for the network claims/survey extracts, plus the captured log and listing from a passing run:

```
jenner-check/
├── run_jenner.sh
├── README.md
├── t001_condition_macro/
├── t002_condi_macro/
├── t003_enrollment_macro/
└── t004_survey_merge/
```

To check it yourself: check out this PR's branch and run from the repo root —

```bash
gh pr checkout <PR_NUMBER>
curl -sS --data-binary @jenner-check/t001_condition_macro/script.sas https://api.jenneranalytics.com/v1/quick
```

or `cd jenner-check && ./run_jenner.sh --all` to re-run all four and verify them against the pinned results. The hosted API is free to try, no signup — full API reference: [the docs](https://docs.jenneranalytics.com/api/).

The runner uploads only a bundle's SAS source text (the two-line autoexec plus script.sas) to api.jenneranalytics.com, where it runs and returns the log and listing — it does not read or upload any data files, so anything sitting next to a script stays on your machine, and nothing is sent unless you run a command yourself.

Merge it, close it, or ignore it — no response expected, and we won't open further PRs in this repo. To opt out for good, drop `no-more-prs` in a comment here or open an issue titled `jenner-check: opt out`.

author: arrington-collab
body:
## Slice 3 — Spanish-first crew comms

Crew and canvass reps get messages in their own language. From `docs/superpowers/specs/prompts-wow-features.md`.

> **Stacked on #185** (branched off the 1a branch so the migration numbers correctly and it reuses the inbound-SMS entry). The diff shows 1a's commits until #185 merges. **Migrations 0075 + 0076.**

### A survey finding that shaped scope
The spec assumes rich crew-facing messaging exists; in reality the only crew-**recipient** message today is the **weather-move crew notice** (`notifyWeatherMove`) — the homeowner-"crew" touches actually go to the homeowner. So this slice delivers the full language machinery + localizes the one real crew message, and scopes the rest as documented follows (below).

### What's built
- **Migration 0075** — `language` ('en'|'es', default 'en') on `crew` + `canvass_rep`. **0076** — `crew_id` + `language` on `communication` (so crew sends are attributable for the invariant).
- **Pure i18n core** (`@savvy/core/crew-language`): `parseLanguageFlip` (accent-insensitive ESPAÑOL/ENGLISH), `languageFlipConfirmation` (confirms in the NEW language), `selectTemplateKey` (base vs `.es` Library variant), `translateWithFallback` (English passthrough; **fail-soft to flagged English** on gateway error — never silence).
- **Self-serve flip** — a crew member texting "ESPAÑOL"/"ENGLISH" flips their crew's language and gets a confirmation in the new language (inbound-SMS short-circuit, `crewByMemberPhone`).
- **Team admin** — English/Español toggle per crew in Crews settings (`setCrewLanguageAction`).
- **Localized crew message** — the weather-move crew notice renders in the crew's language via the cheap gateway capability, fail-soft to English, stamping `crew_id`+`language` on the `communication`.
- **Evidence** — `comms.crew_language` (UNBOUND, window-scoped): a crew communication whose stamped language differs from the crew's current preference fails. Red/green tested.

### Tests (all green)
- Pure core (vitest): `parseLanguageFlip` / `languageFlipConfirmation` / `selectTemplateKey` / `translateWithFallback` (incl. fail-soft) — 8 cases.
- Evidence `comms.crew_language` red/green.
- DB integration (live PG): language get/set + `crewByMemberPhone` + canvass rep — 2 cases.
- `weather-reschedule` unaffected (en passthrough) — 5 cases.
- Full `pnpm typecheck` (7/7) + `pnpm lint` (0 errors).

### Documented follows (need net-new crew-messaging surface / pipeline)
- Localize the **other** crew message types (schedule/day-before/material/punch/safety) — most don't have a crew-recipient send today; they need building first, then `selectTemplateKey`/`translateWithFallback` applied (the machinery is ready).
- **Inbound Spanish memo pipeline** (transcribe+translate crew memos, English fields + original preserved) — hooks onto the existing memo pipeline.
- Persist the translation-failure **flag** (currently fail-soft sends English; the `failed` bool isn't stored).

Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/` (foundation-first increment).

author: melvincarvalho
body:
Rebuilds lwsd on the jspod recipe — a thin daemon that spawns JSS (>=0.0.219) with an `lws` protocol plugin — replacing the old lws-server basis and hand-rolled passkey/token auth.

## What it implements

Every current w3c/lws-protocol editor's draft that a storage server can conform to:

- **lws10-core** — CRUD, conditional PUT (428/412), merge-patch content PATCH, container representations (`application/lws+json` + conneg incl. `ld+json;profile`), link-based pagination, RFC 9264 linksets, storage description discovery, `Depth: infinity`, Range requests, RFC 9457 errors, optional 507 quota.
- **lws10-searchindex** — TypeIndex + TypeSearch with the full CNF filter (GET+POST), Link-header type derivation, strict 400/415 errors, authorization-filtered results.
- **lws10-notifications** — webhook subscriptions, Activity Streams 2.0 envelopes, RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures (ES256, key published in the storage description).
- **Authorization** — 401 challenges, access request/grant endpoints, a real ODRL Access Profile engine (actions/assignee/target/constraints) driving read + write.
- **Authn suites** — did:key (Ed25519 + P-256) and CID (subject-dereference) self-issued JWTs.

Not implementable storage-side: OpenID/SAML suites and the OAuth token-exchange flow (need an external authorization server).

## Tests

`npm test` orchestrates four batteries on scratch ports — **72 checks** (51 features + 6 did:key + 3 CID + 12 ODRL grants), all passing.

## Findings

[CONFORMANCE.md](CONFORMANCE.md) documents 14 findings (C1-C14) where the spec and the JSS plugin API interact — including the dot-segment/`.meta` collision (C1), the lack of a CLI plugin config channel (C6), and the CID suite's mandatory outbound subject-dereference as an SSRF surface (C14).

author: omerm14
body:
## What changed
Three internal `integrations` lookups fetched by `id` alone, violating CLAUDE.md's top invariant (every server-side query must scope by `user_id`, since the server uses the service-role key and bypasses RLS). Not an active leak today — in every call site the `id` was already ownership-verified earlier in the same request/job — but any future reuse of these patterns without re-verifying ownership would become a real IDOR.

- `server/services/syncProcessor.js` — `isCancelRequested(integrationId)` now takes a second `userId` param and adds `.eq('user_id', userId)`. Both call sites (`syncGmail`, `syncGreenInvoice`) already have `userId` in scope and now pass it through. Exported for testability, matching the existing `isDuplicate`/`parseAmount` pattern in the same file.
- `server/routes/integrations.js` — `processSyncJob`'s integration lookup now adds `.eq('user_id', job.user_id)` (the job row was already fetched scoped by `req.user.id`, so `job.user_id` is trustworthy).
- `server/routes/cron.js` — the stale sync-job resume path's integration lookup now adds `.eq('user_id', job.user_id)` for the same reason.

Out of scope (per ticket): the WhatsApp webhook's `integrations` queries in `server/routes/webhook.js` are intentionally left untouched — that endpoint has no JWT/user context by design (HMAC-verified, phone-based routing).

No behavior change for legitimate calls — the id/user_id pairing already held in every current call site, so this is purely a scoping tightening.

## How to verify (<1 min)
```
npm test   # 22 files / 118 tests pass, including 3 new cases in tests/integrationsScoping.test.js
npm run build   # succeeds
```
The new tests exercise the real modules (via the repo's established require.cache-seeding mock pattern, see tests/plans.test.js / tests/errorLeak.test.js) and assert each fixed query's `.eq()` calls include both `id` and `user_id`.

## Tradeoffs
None functionally. `isCancelRequested`'s signature gained a second parameter — both call sites updated in the same file.

## Flags
No billing/auth/migration impact — hardening/defense-in-depth only, not a fix for a currently-exploitable bug.

author: augustas11
body:
## What

Wave C **item 6** — SPEC-024 **v0.2**: the provider-local prefix-cache **isolation baseline** (§11–§16), reconciled to shipped code, plus the coordinated cross-spec amendments that ratify the shipped provider-visible derived `conversation_key` under an explicit privacy posture.

**Bundled amendments (one coordinated change):**
- **SPEC-024 v0.2** — new §11–§16: cache-key/reuse invariant (FR-CI1–4a), cross-account namespacing (FR-CI5–7), non-leakage threat model (FR-CI8–10a), coordinator cross-check (FR-CI11–14), ingest paths, acceptance criteria.
- **SPEC-004 v0.3.2** — FR-SR-2 provider-visibility carve-out (the coordinator MAY forward the derived opaque `conversation_key` to the provider for prefix caching).
- **SPEC-006 v0.9.8** — §1.3 survivability invariant (b) narrowed; lifecycle + disclosure reconciled.
- **SPEC-008 v0.4.1** — §2.2 invariant (b) narrowed; §6.6/§10.6 document the shipped `inference_request_plaintext` encrypted envelope.

**Spec-only. No code change** — this documents shipped Swift-provider + Go-coordinator + gateway behavior; the code is the live cross-repo interop contract.

## The design decision (H1 → option (a))

The shipped prefix cache **sends the derived `conv:` key to the provider** (provider-local KV caching needs a stable per-conversation key), which tensioned the prior SPEC-004/006/008 invariant that the provider cannot see `conv:`. **Operator decision (2026-07-12): option (a) — ratify the shipped design.** The provider learns a **stable opaque per-conversation identifier** (the cross-turn correlation sticky affinity already grants) but **never** the raw buyer tag or `account_id` (one-way HMAC), and captured network frames carry no raw account/tag (Pillar B survivability intact).

## Honest residuals (tracked MUST-close, not papered over)

The audit pushed the corpus to state option (a)'s consequences honestly rather than overclaim:
- **Provider retention is not buyer-purgeable.** `DELETE /v1/sticky` purges only the coordinator sticky map; the provider-local KV is deterministic-keyed and can be re-populated by post-delete normal routing to the same provider — its only dependable bound is the provider's own TTL/LRU (reuse *eligibility*, not guaranteed physical erasure). Recorded as a §1.3 lifecycle residual + §13/FR-CI10a disclosure-completeness item.
- **Disclosure completeness.** The base sticky-affinity disclosure ships and is hard-required; the option-(a) extensions (provider receipt/retention, cross-provider linkability) are a tracked MUST-close disclosure item.
- **Shipped-code gaps documented for follow-up:** FR-CI11a (queued-routing `sticky_result` provenance on the slot-queue path), FR-CI13 (sticky read-path account compare), plus test-coverage gaps in §16.

These are billing-attribution / disclosure-completeness items — **not** cross-account isolation breaches (the account-scoped HMAC holds throughout).

## Audit

7-round codex 3-lane loop (code / security / architect via `omc ask codex`), converged to **0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH / 0 MEDIUM on all three lanes** (code lane passed at R3; security + architect at R7). The loop caught several issues a lighter review would have shipped wrong — most notably the encrypted-envelope byte contract (§6.6/§10.6 said ciphertext = bare `body`, shipped = JSON envelope with `conversation_key`), and an overstated buyer-deletion control that had to be corrected to the honest residual above. All LOW hygiene nits resolved.

## What

author: adityavg13
body:
Profiling FSZero cold indexing showed ~2 min of 100% CPU with the top of stack in `fts5NextMethod` (748/902 samples) inside `delete_file_children` executing `DELETE FROM lines_fts WHERE file_id=?1`.

Root cause:
- `lines_fts` is an FTS5 virtual table with `file_id UNINDEXED`, so per-file deletes scanned the entire FTS table: O(N^2) during cold bulk builds.
- `symbols`, `callers`, `imports`, and `semantic_chunks` had no indexes on `file_id`, making per-file deletes table scans.
- `lines_trigram` is external-content over `lines`, so it must be deleted before `lines` rows disappear.

Change:
- Collect `rowid`s from `lines` first.
- Delete `lines_trigram` and `lines_fts` rows by `rowid` in 500-row chunks (avoiding the FTS5 scan and parameter limits).
- Delete the remaining ordinary tables by indexed `file_id`.
- Add `file_id` indexes on `symbols`, `callers`, `imports`, `semantic_chunks`, and bump `SCHEMA_VERSION` to 5 so existing stores pick them up.
- Add targeted tests for stale FTS/trigram rows, per-table deletion, and linear re-upsert performance.

Before: cold bulk builds O(N^2) due to FTS5 full-table scans per file.
After: per-file deletes are O(lines-in-file) for the FTS tables and indexed for the rest.

author: mmatook
body:
## Problem

The last three **Build & Release** runs failed (starting 2026-07-10). All three
share one root cause and none actually reach the blocklist build/validation —
the **Clippy** step aborts first:

```
error: this `match` expression can be replaced with `?`
   --> src/parser.rs:151:20
error: could not compile `dns-blocklist-compiler` (lib) due to 1 previous error
##[error]Process completed with exit code 101.
```

The release workflow installs a fresh **stable** toolchain daily. A newer clippy
(rust ≥1.97) tightened `clippy::question_mark`, which now fires on the
`match body_after_comment { Some(b) => ..., None => return None }` block in
`extract_expected_entry_count`. Because the job runs `clippy -- -D warnings`, the
lint becomes a hard error. CI (`ci.yml`) hasn't caught it because it only runs on
push/PR, and there have been no pushes since the toolchain drifted.

## Fix

Replace the `match` with the idiomatic `?` on the `Option`, exactly as clippy
suggests. The semantics are unchanged: the first non-comment line ends the header
block and returns `None`.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check` ✅
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` ✅ (no issues)
- `cargo test` ✅ (93 passed, 2 ignored)

author: jlengelbrecht
body:
## Summary

Adds the reusable building block that lets the release and dev-latest signing jobs fetch Android signing material from **1Password at runtime**, so no keystore or signing password is ever stored in GitHub. This is the block those jobs will consume; the jobs themselves are not part of this change.

## What's here

- **`.github/actions/op-load-signing-secrets`** — composite action.
  - Input `keystore: release | debug`.
  - Installs the 1Password CLI (`install-cli-action`, pinned), resolves the signing passwords and key aliases into **masked env vars** via `load-secrets-action`, and materializes the keystore **file attachment** to `$RUNNER_TEMP` (`chmod 600`) with `op read` — `load-secrets-action` cannot resolve a file attachment, so the CLI handles the keystore.
  - Exports the exact env-var names `app/build.gradle.kts` already reads (`RELEASE_KEYSTORE_FILE`/`_PASSWORD`, `RELEASE_KEY_ALIAS`/`_PASSWORD`, and the `DEBUG_*` equivalents) plus a non-secret `keystore-path` output, so the signing jobs consume it with **no renaming**.
- **`.github/workflows/secrets-plumbing-check.yml`** — `workflow_dispatch` smoke test that authenticates with the service-account token and resolves **only** the non-sensitive `canary` field, printing `1Password plumbing OK`. Never touches a keystore or password.
- **`docs/dev/signing-and-secrets.md`** — documents the model (all signing material in 1Password vault `github`, item `android-signing`; the only GitHub secret is `ANDROID_ACTIONS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`, mapped to `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN`), the file-attachment-vs-text-field split, and a copy-paste consumer snippet. Added to `docs/dev/_meta.json`.

## Secret handling

- No keystore, password, alias, or token byte appears in the diff — only `op://` references.
- Keystores are written to `$RUNNER_TEMP` (`chmod 600`) and never echoed; passwords and aliases live only in masked env vars; the sole action output is the non-secret keystore path.
- Both third-party actions are SHA-pinned with version comments (`install-cli-action` `v4.0.0`, `load-secrets-action` `v4.0.1`).

## CI

Docs/CI-only change — the **Android Gate** passes via its skip path (nothing under `app/`, `gradle/`, etc. is touched). The plumbing check is `workflow_dispatch` only and becomes dispatchable once this workflow reaches the default branch.

body:
## Summary

clerk can now pre-fill answers from a global defaults file, so you stop re-typing the same values (author name, org, license, Python version, …) on every project you generate.

## What's new

- Reads a user-owned `~/.config/clerk/defaults.yml` and pre-fills matching questions as **soft defaults** — you can still change any value at the prompt.
- Path is overridable via the `CLERK_DEFAULTS_PATH` environment variable.
- Works across single-template and multi-template generation; each layer only receives the defaults relevant to its own questions.
- Falls back to copier's native `settings.yml` `defaults:` (best-effort) when clerk's own file doesn't supply a value.
- **Secret questions are never pre-filled** from the defaults file.

## Behaviour notes

- No defaults file → no change in behaviour (silent first-run state).
- A malformed defaults file, or a `CLERK_DEFAULTS_PATH` pointing at a file that doesn't exist, fails fast with a clear error naming the path.
- Precedence: an explicit run-spec answer always wins over a default.

## Verification

`uv run pytest` — 255 passed, 1 skipped · `uv run mypy` — clean · `ruff check/format` — clean.

## Spec Context

Implements spec 004 (global per-module defaults). Governed by ADR-0005 (`user_defaults=` injection). Q-004a resolved to **YAML** (`defaults.yml`) — the codebase-consistent choice (PyYAML already a dependency; matches ADR-0005's filename, so no ADR rename); planning artifacts reconciled TOML→YAML in this branch. Q-004b best-effort settings fold; Q-004c explicit-missing-path raises; Q-004d hidden-key exclusion = SHOULD. Post-review fix: renamed a stale `toml_defaults` parameter to `clerk_defaults`.

body:
## Summary

`main` is currently broken: `:openbank-ledger-service:compileTestKotlin` fails, blocking any test
run for the whole module.

Root cause is a semantic merge conflict between two PRs that each passed CI independently but
never saw each other's change:
- PR #888 (`feat(ledger): add operator replay endpoint...`), merged 08:11:49, added
  `appendOutbox(messages: List<OutboxMessage>): Int` to the `JournalRepository` interface
  (`LedgerPorts.kt`).
- PR #836 (`test(fx,ledger,balance): property tests for FX margin, idempotency, projection
  order`), merged 08:16:35 — five minutes later — added
  `LedgerServiceIdempotencyPropertyTest.kt` with a hand-written `InMemoryJournalRepository` fake
  that predates #888's interface addition.

Neither PR's own CI run ever saw the other's diff. Together on `main`, the fake no longer
satisfies the interface it implements.

## Fix

`appendOutbox` is only called by `ReplayBookedChangesService`, never by
`LedgerService.postJournal` (the path this property test exercises) — so the fix follows this
same fake's existing pattern for its other not-exercised members (`saveReversal`,
`trialBalance`, `subLedgerBalances`, `controlAccountTieOut`):

```kotlin
override suspend fun appendOutbox(messages: List<OutboxMessage>): Int = error("not exercised by postJournal")
```

## Verification

Reproduced and fixed against a clean **detached checkout of `origin/main`** (not a stale local
branch — per this repo's own documented "stale checkout" pitfall):
- Before the fix: `compileTestKotlin` fails with `Class 'InMemoryJournalRepository' is not
  abstract and does not implement abstract member: suspend fun appendOutbox(...)`.
- After the fix: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`.
- Full `:openbank-ledger-service:test`: 198/198, 0 failures/errors.
- `ktlintCheck` + `detekt`: clean.
- Also re-ran the other 5 property-test files added by the same PR #836
  (`JournalEntryPropertyTest`, `MoneyPropertyTest`, `BalancePropertyTest`,
  `BalanceProjectionOrderPropertyTest`, `FxConversionMathPropertyTest`) — all pass, confirming
  issue #469's full scope (ledger double-entry, Money arithmetic, FX conversion, balance
  projection, idempotency) is genuinely covered end-to-end once this fix lands.

Test-only change — no `src/main/**` touched, no version bump needed.

Refs #469 — the failure this fixes is in #469's own coverage work; not closing here since this PR
only unbreaks the build, it doesn't change the scope of #469 itself.

- Semver via changesets with explicit **0.x semantics**: pre-1.0, **minor** = behavior-changing/breaking (allowed, but called out in the changeset text); **patch** = fixes/internal/no observable change.
- **1.0 condition**: a usable core (import, browse, organize) whose data model and primary surface we're prepared to keep stable.
- Convention: behavior-changing PRs include a changeset; docs/tooling-only PRs may skip. **No CI hard-gate** (image-trail's default) — the PR template prompts; revisit if changesets get forgotten.

**Tooling:**

- `@changesets/cli@2.31.0` (exact pin) + `.changeset/` init (default config, `baseBranch: main`).
- Scripts: `changeset`, `changeset:version` (plain `changeset version`; the ADR documents the sync-hook slot for a future second version-bearing file, mirroring image-trail's `sync-manifest-version.mjs`).
- PR template gains a **Changeset** section with a checkbox, linking ADR-0002 for the 0.x semantics.
- AGENTS.md records the convention (same-PR maintenance rule): changesets for behavior changes, `CHANGELOG.md` is generated, never hand-edited.

## Verification (exit criteria)

- [x] ADR exists in the wiki and is linked from the PR template's changeset prompt
- [x] Flow probed end-to-end: a test changeset + `npm run changeset:version` bumped 0.1.0 → 0.1.1 and wrote `CHANGELOG.md` correctly (probe reverted — no changelog committed until a real behavior change)
- [x] PR template asks whether a changeset is included/needed
- [x] Full lint + format gates pass

author: amoifr
body:
Closes #89.

@stof spotted that the supported Sass options were missing the deprecation-related ones, and suspected #67 (repeated options) would need solving first. Good news: that part is already done — #37 taught `SassBuilder` to expand array values into repeated flags, which `load_path` already relies on. So this is just wiring up what's missing:

| Config | Sass flag | |
|---|---|---|
| `verbose` | `--verbose` | boolean |
| `fatal_deprecation` | `--fatal-deprecation` | repeatable |
| `future_deprecation` | `--future-deprecation` | repeatable |
| `silence_deprecation` | `--silence-deprecation` | repeatable |

```yaml
symfonycasts_sass:
    sass_options:
        fatal_deprecation: ['import']
        silence_deprecation: ['color-functions']
```

One caveat worth flagging: `--silence-deprecation` only exists since **Dart Sass 1.74.0**, while the binary this bundle downloads is pinned to 1.69.7. The other three work fine on the pinned binary (`--future-deprecation` works there even though `sass --help` doesn't advertise it — verified 🕵️). Every option defaults to `null` and is only emitted when set, so nothing changes for existing users; the docs note the version requirement.

Tests cover both the CLI flag expansion and a functional build: opting into the `import` deprecation early warns, and marking it fatal turns it into a build error. I also fixed the `$sassOptions` docblocks, which still claimed `bool|string` while `load_path` has been passing arrays since #37.

Thanks for the bundle! 🙏

author: sachiniyer
body:
**Review-only design artifact — do NOT merge.** Plan for Phase 3 of the #1592 multi-backend epic.

## Goal
Make the daemon client API reachable over the network (TLS TCP) with a **single bearer token = full access, single-owner** (Sachin-LOCKED: no mTLS/OIDC/per-user). Loopback + SSH-tunnel stays the zero-config default; the token is for direct TCP + the future web client. This phase is **small** because Phase 2 pre-built every auth seam as a no-op — the token gate drops in without reshaping a single route, handler, or wire message.

Full doc: `docs/design/phase3-tcp-auth.md`.

## Resolved decisions (recommendations)
1. **Listener model** — keep the unix socket (local trust, no auth) *and* add a TLS TCP listener; **both serve the same mux**, differing only in the per-listener auth gate. One config key `listen_addr`, **off by default**.
2. **TLS cert** — daemon **self-generates** a self-signed cert on first TCP-enable (client pins the SHA-256 fingerprint, TOFU); `tls_cert`/`tls_key` override for a CA/Let's-Encrypt cert. TLS mandatory on TCP.
3. **Token lifecycle** — 32-byte random, af-home `daemon-token` (0600), **auto-generated on first TCP-enable**, printed on start + `af token show`; `af token rotate` to replace; `crypto/subtle` constant-time compare, fail-closed.
4. **withAuth fill-in** — unix peer always authorized (unchanged); TCP peer must present a valid bearer token (REST header / WS `?access_token=`) or **401** (which also aborts the WS handshake, since `withAuth` wraps the mux before the upgrade). One gate param on the existing middleware.
5. **CORS** — replace permissive `*` with a `cors_allowed_origins` allow-list, **empty/off by default**; exact-match origin echo.
6. **Client side** — `--daemon-url` / `--token` / `--tls-fingerprint` (+ `AF_DAEMON_*` env); unset ⇒ local unix socket unchanged. `apiclient.NewRemote` threads the token on every REST call + WS dial; the Phase-2 `stream-info` URL indirection already hands back remote `wss://` URLs.

## PR sequence (least-risky-first, each shippable, clean-break)
- **PR1 — auth material *(dark)*:** self-signed cert + token library + `af token show|rotate` + the 4 config keys. No listener, no wire change. Risk LOW.
- **PR2 — `withAuth` enforcement + CORS allow-list *(dark)*:** constant-time compare + 401 path; unix gate stays off ⇒ local behavior byte-identical. Risk LOW–MED.
- **PR3 — TLS TCP listener:** bind on `listen_addr` (off by default), same mux + token gate, self-gen/override cert, enable-banner. Risk MED (network surface, gated behind opt-in).
- **PR4 — client remote target:** `NewRemote` + token threading + flag/env resolver at the 4 client-construction sites; default local path unchanged. Risk MED.
- **PR5 — docs + hardening:** enable→connect→rotate walkthrough, SSH-tunnel-vs-TCP guidance, README/`af --help`. Risk LOW.

Every PR: build/gofmt/lint/deadcode/file-length clean, `make test-container` green, selftest 25/25, plus a real TCP+TLS+token loopback round-trip. Load-bearing/user-facing bits flagged: config-key names, `af token` shape, client flag names, network-port + token-in-log (auth *model* is locked).

## Sets up later phases
- **Phase 4:** remote/container backends expose their own authed `wss://` via the existing `stream-info` URL; the client dials them with the PR4 token plumbing — no new transport.
- **Phase 5:** the browser seams (`?access_token=` query + `cors_allowed_origins`) are both filled here; the web client just sets its origin + carries the token.

body:
## Problème

Rechercher « L'âme idéale » dans la recherche calendrier renvoyait « Aucun résultat », alors que le film existe (tt35526093). Diagnostic sur la base réelle : **le film est déjà dans `calendar_entries`, sous son titre anglais « You Found Me »**. Deux défauts se combinaient :

1. `/calendar/search` n'interrogeait que les providers externes et **supprimait silencieusement** tout résultat dont l'`imdb_id` était déjà dans le calendrier (`filter_existing_entries`) — TMDB trouvait bien le film via son titre français, puis le résultat était jeté.
2. La table locale n'était jamais consultée par cette recherche, et son matching de titre était sensible aux accents (« Ame ideale » ≠ « Âme idéale ») et au type d'apostrophe (’ vs ').

## Correctifs

- **`/calendar/search`** (`merge_calendar_search_results`) : les correspondances locales sont listées en premier (avec leurs drapeaux téléchargé/liste d'intérêt) ; les résultats providers déjà connus du calendrier sont repliés dans leur entrée locale ; toute entrée connue est marquée `in_calendar`.
- **Interface web** : les cartes de résultats affichent des badges « Déjà au calendrier » / « Téléchargé » / « Dans la liste d'intérêt » au lieu d'un bouton « Importer » inutile ; le bouton liste d'intérêt n'apparaît que si l'entrée n'y est pas déjà.
- **`CalendarEntriesRepository#normalize_text`** : comparaison de titres insensible aux accents (décomposition Unicode + suppression des diacritiques) et aux apostrophes typographiques (’ ʼ ` → ').

## Tests

- `test/daemon_routes_test.rb` : +3 tests sur le merge (dédoublonnage local/provider, repli d'un hit provider connu sous un autre titre vers l'entrée locale, filtre année).
- `test/app/calendar_entries_repository_test.rb` : +1 test (recherche « L'ame ideale » avec apostrophe typographique → trouve « L'Âme idéale »).
- Suite complète : identique à la baseline (échecs préexistants d'environnement uniquement).

## Après merge

Redémarrer le démon sur l'hôte (pas de rechargement à chaud). Note : l'entrée tt35526093 gardera son titre anglais « You Found Me » en base tant que le feed TMDB ne l'a pas rafraîchie (le fix « titre original » de la PR #850 s'applique aux entrées ré-hydratées).

## 개요

스킬 스튜디오 **Phase 3** — Phase 2(PR #293)가 "가짜 데이터 금지 원칙"으로 범위 밖에 뒀던 4개 항목을 **실측 데이터 기반**으로 구현합니다.

스펙: `docs/design-docs/skill-studio-phase3-benchmark-cost-spec.md`

### 확정 결정 (사용자)
- **D1 A/B 실행**: 싱글턴 모델 콜 2-arm — 케이스당 with-arm + without-arm + grader 3콜 (풀 에이전트 런 아님)
- **D2 휴먼 피드백**: 케이스별 판정(agree/disagree) + 스킬 단위(up/down) 둘 다. **표시 전용**(pass_rate/health 미반영)
- **D3 usage 귀속**: 실측만 — 평가 런 실 LLM 토큰/비용(전량 스킬 귀속) + 채팅 `execute_in_skill` 성공 실행 횟수. "스킬 연결 대화의 전체 비용"은 다중 스킬 중복·무관 턴 왜곡으로 제외

## 주요 변경

**백엔드**
- **마이그레이션 m70** — `skill_usage_events`(스킬 축 usage 원장), `skill_evaluation_runs.usage`(실측 rollup), `skill_feedbacks` / `skill_evaluation_case_feedbacks`
- **실측 A/B 벤치마크 러너(llm-2)** — 케이스당 with/without arm을 실제 실행해 채점(기존 러너의 baseline "추정"을 실측으로 교체). `baseline_comparison=false`면 2콜로 절감. arm별 wall-clock/토큰 실측 → benchmark `measured:true`
- **비용 실회계** — 모델 단가 기반 estimate + 평가 런 실 LLM 토큰/비용 기록. 단가 없는 모델은 cost NULL("모름 ≠ 무료")
- **버전별 통과율 API**(`GET .../evaluations/version-stats`) + **휴먼 피드백 API**(케이스/스킬, CSRF + enumeration-safe)
- 채팅 `execute_in_skill` **성공 시** 스킬 축 실행 카운트 귀속

**프론트엔드**
- 평가 탭: A/B 벤치마크 바(실측/추정 배지), 실측 사용량·비용, 버전별 통과율 추이, usage 카드, 케이스/스킬 피드백 UI
- 히스토리 탭 리비전 통과율 배지

## 검증

- backend **2761** pytest(serial, `SKILL_EVALUATION_ENABLED=true`) + ruff
- frontend **vitest 1305** + tsc + eslint + build + lint:i18n + lint:design-system
- mock E2E + **라이브 캡처 투어 8장**(throwaway 스택, scripted 모델로 실제 평가 런 2버전 실행)
- origin/main(Stage 3 god 모듈 분할) 머지 후 전 계층 재검증 — 충돌·의미적 회귀 없음

## 적대 리뷰 (5라운드, 발견 0 수렴)

R1(5) → R2(2) → R3(8) → R4(4) → R5(3) — 누적 22건 수정. 라운드마다 직전 수정 델타를 1순위 재검증("수정 배치가 다음 라운드의 표적"). 주요 수확:
- baseline_comparison 미전달로 estimate/summary 과대 보고 → 전 경로 스레딩
- run 타임아웃(고정 180s)이 llm-2 케이스당 3콜과 미조합 → 워크로드 비례 스케일(정상 크기 평가셋 mid-run 타임아웃 + $0 회계 방지)
- chat_execution이 실패 스크립트도 카운트 → 스펙대로 성공(exit 0) 게이트
- priced 모델 no-metadata → "0 토큰" 위장 → "미측정" 표기
- 피드백 코멘트 유실, 케이스 드래프트 런 간 누출, 벤치마크 델타 이중 렌더 등

**의도적 defer(문서화)**: 피드백 upsert IntegrityError 하드닝(UI 가드 + message_feedback 관례 — 두 경로 함께 후속), timeout/cancel 시 부분 usage 미기록(과금 정책)

## 백로그

`baseline_comparison` UI 토글(백엔드/E2E 준비됨), 케이스 피드백 집계 run 응답 동봉, 피드백→health/pass_rate 반영, 다중 스킬 usage 대시보드

author: wanxiankai
body:
# Summary

Closes #2976.

This fixes generic CSS font family names on Apple platforms. Previously, values like `fontFamily="serif"` were passed directly to React Native's `RCTFont` helper. `RCTFont` does not resolve CSS generic family keywords such as `serif`, so iOS reported the family as unrecognized and fell back to the default system sans-serif font.

The Apple text glyph path now resolves generic family keywords before calling `RCTFont updateFont`:

- `serif` -> `Georgia`
- `sans-serif` -> `System`
- `monospace` -> `Menlo`
- `cursive` -> `Snell Roundhand`
- `fantasy` -> `Papyrus`

I also added a common test screen reproducing the issue with a default system text line and a `fontFamily="serif"` line.

## Test Plan

Commands run locally:

- `yarn lint` ✅
- `yarn tsc` ✅
- `git diff --check` ✅

### What's required for testing (prerequisites)?

An iOS simulator or device running the example app.

### What are the steps to reproduce (after prerequisites)?

1. Open the common test app.
2. Render `Test2976`.
3. Confirm the first SVG text line uses the default system sans-serif font.
4. Confirm the second SVG text line with `fontFamily="serif"` renders with a serif font instead of falling back to the default system font.

## Compatibility

| OS      | Implemented |
| ------- | :---------: |
| iOS     |      ✅      |
| MacOS   |      ✅      |
| Android |      ❌      |
| Web     |      ❌      |

Android and Web are not changed by this PR; the issue was reported for iOS and the fix is in the Apple text implementation.

## Checklist

- [ ] I have tested this on a device and a simulator
- [ ] I added documentation in `README.md`
- [ ] I updated the typed files (typescript)
- [ ] I added a test for the API in the `__tests__` folder

author: chenchaoyi
body:
feat(usage): usage-watch — token accounting, layered thresholds, early warnings

Implements openspec/changes/usage-watch (approved #373). Deterministic, zero
LLM calls, cgo-free — the digest layer's cost model.

- internal/usage: per-session accounting from the agent's own log. Cumulative
  out/in tokens ride a PERSISTENT byte-offset counter (state/usage/<session>) —
  the first-ever scan pays once (measured 21s across a 47M-token 11-session
  fleet), then every call is incremental (0.36s). Live context = the last
  message's input+cache tokens; window is EVIDENCE-inferred (smallest tier
  ≥ observed: 200k/1M — dogfood showed model names don't encode long-context;
  usage.json `window` overrides). Rate = output tokens/min over a 10-min tail
  window.
- Layered thresholds per agent type (~/.config/gtmux/usage.json): ctxWarn
  (default 0.8) / sessionOutWarn (20M — tuned to this fleet's real long
  sessions) / typeRatePerMinWarn (30k) + global horizonMin (30). Pure
  Evaluate() PROJECTS current + rate × horizon → warns with an ETA before the
  wall ("ctx→80% in ~9m").
- Surfacing: `gtmux usage [--json]` (per-session + per-type rollup, the type
  layer judged on the summed rate) · GET /api/usage (bearer-gated, additive) ·
  digest rows gain tok/ctx/rate/usage_warn · agents --json gains the additive
  amber `usage_warn` modifier (read from the marker — the radar stays cheap).
- Warnings: the hook evaluates on EVERY lifecycle event (tool-call-driven ≈
  near-real-time during real burn; the silent-generation gap is the recorded
  P2 serve-tick refinement), maintains the usagewarn/<pane> marker, and types
  ONE `[gtmux] usage·warn <loc> — <detail>` per layer into a live HQ pane
  (marker doubles as dedup; hqNudge config honored; self-exclusion held).

Dogfooded live: real fleet totals/ctx/rates rendered sanely (85%/94% sessions
flagged); with a forced-low threshold the warn marker appeared and HQ received
`[gtmux] usage·warn MP:0.0 (%6) — ctx 60%` exactly once, and the supervisor's
own breach did NOT self-nudge.

Tests: scan/tail parsing, incremental counters, window inference, Evaluate
table (breach + projection + quiet), TypeRateWarn, layerOf dedup, GET
/api/usage 401/200/503. make check green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

## Summary
Drei Verbesserungen nach Spieltest-Feedback:

1. **„Weiter" → „Zocken" + eigene Signalfarbe.** Statt des bisherigen neutralen Iris/Blau bekommt der Weiterwürfeln-Knopf eine Bernstein-Farbe – klar unterscheidbar vom grünen „Sichern"-Knopf, damit man die riskante Entscheidung nicht aus Versehen mit der sicheren verwechselt (neue `--color-amber-*` Tokens, analog zu Mint/Koralle/Iris).
2. **Niete-Banner statt sofortigem Weiterschalten.** Eine Niete löst nicht mehr sofort und stillschweigend die nächste Person aus. Stattdessen erscheint ein großes Banner („X hat sich ausgezockt!" + verlorene Punkte) mit explizitem „Nächster Spieler"-Knopf – der Verlust bleibt kurz sichtbar. Die eigentliche Zug-Auflösung läuft erst beim Bestätigen.
3. **Keine Überlagerung von Feier und Übergabe mehr.** Die „X ist dran"-Einblendung überlagerte sich bisher mit der Konfetti-Feier bei besonderen Würfen (Pasch, Straße, heiße Würfel), da beide gleichzeitig als Vollbild-Overlay ausgelöst wurden. Die Übergabe wartet jetzt, bis die Feier abgeklungen ist.

## Test plan
- [x] `tsc -b` und `npm test` (65 Tests) grün
- [x] Per Playwright (iPad quer): Zocken-Button zeigt Bernstein-Verlauf statt Iris, Text „Zocken"

- [x] Doppel-Pasch-Feier ausgelöst und verifiziert: „IST DRAN" erscheint **nicht** gleichzeitig mit der Konfetti-Feier, sondern sauber verzögert danach

author: lancetipton
body:
## Summary
- `endpointTestApi.ts`'s fetch had no `AbortSignal`, so testing an endpoint (Endpoint drawer's "Send" button) against a slow/unreachable external API left the request hanging indefinitely — `useEndpointTest`'s `setLoading(true)` is only cleared once `testEndpoint()` settles, so the Send button stuck loading forever with no way to cancel besides a full page reload.
- Added `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(30_000)` to the fetch call. On timeout, the abort is caught distinctly (checking `err.name === 'TimeoutError'`, since `DOMException` is not `instanceof Error` in Node) and surfaced as a clear `Request timed out after 30s` error through the existing `TEndpointTestRes.error` path, so `useEndpointTest`'s existing error-display renders it like any other failure — no changes needed to `useEndpointTest.ts` itself.

## Test plan
- [x] New test in `endpointTestApi.test.ts` (`request timeout` describe block): asserts `AbortSignal.timeout` is called with `30_000`, and a fake-timer test (stubs `AbortSignal.timeout` to route through vitest's fake clock, mocks `fetch` to hang until the injected signal aborts, then `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(30_000)`) confirms `testEndpoint`/`execute` resolves with `error.message === 'Request timed out after 30s'` — no real 30s wait.
- [x] `pnpm --filter @tdsk/admin types` — clean.
- [x] `pnpm --filter @tdsk/admin test` — full suite green: **71 test files passed, 681 tests passed** (includes existing `useEndpointTest.test.ts` and `testEndpoint.test.ts`, both passing unchanged).

Nothing to flag for the reviewer beyond the `DOMException` vs `instanceof Error` gotcha noted above — worth double-checking the timeout-branch test still passes if you re-run it, since that's the one non-obvious part of this fix.
