body:
## Summary
- Third and final item from the refreshed roadmap's "Next" tier: guided curriculum / lesson paths, sequencing the existing mission catalog into an instructor-assignable syllabus.
- An instructor sequences the existing mission catalog (`Mission` enum) into an ordered, named path (e.g. "Options 101") for a cohort. Students see a locked syllabus rather than a loose scenario picker — each step unlocks once the previous step's mission is completed.
- **Design note, documented directly in `CurriculumController`'s Javadoc**: progress (complete/unlocked) is always computed against the *viewing user's own* accounts. An instructor viewing a curriculum sees their own progress against it, same as a student — there's no separate per-student breakdown here (that's what the existing instructor grading tools are for). This endpoint's instructor-facing action is authoring/publishing the path, not monitoring individual students.
- **Backend**: new `curricula` / `curriculum_steps` tables (`V8__curricula.sql`); a new `CurriculumController` at `/api/cohorts/{id}/curricula` (instructor-only create with mission-code validation against the real enum, member-or-instructor read).
- **Frontend**: a "Curricula" panel in the Classroom tab with an instructor-only builder (click missions in the order they should be completed) and a per-curriculum checklist (🔒 locked / 🎯 unlocked / ✅ complete) for whoever is viewing. The picker mirrors the backend's `Mission` enum as a small hardcoded catalog — title/description/xp stay defined once, server-side.

## Test plan
- [x] `mvn test` — 66/66 backend tests pass, including 4 new `CurriculumTest` cases (instructor-only create authorization, member-can-read authorization, invalid mission code rejected with 400, steps unlocking in order as the student completes missions).
- [x] Frontend `typecheck` / `vitest` / `webpack build` all clean.
- [x] New Playwright E2E spec (`curricula.spec.ts`) — a two-browser-context flow: instructor publishes a 2-step curriculum, student joins and completes the first mission, the student's own Classroom view shows the first step complete and the second unlocked. Caught a real bug during development (the initial version checked the instructor's view instead of the student's, which doesn't reflect the student's progress per the design above) — fixed and re-verified. Run repeated (3x) with no flakes.
- [x] Full E2E suite run — all green except one pre-existing, already-documented flake in `fx.spec.ts` (unrelated to this change).
- [x] Independent re-verification in a separate `git worktree` at the exact pushed commit — backend `mvn test`, frontend typecheck/vitest/build all clean.

author: devail1
body:
## What & why

chela's Telegram inbound forwarded **every** `/command` straight to Claude Code via `send_tmux`, so there were no bridge-level commands and no `/` autocomplete in Telegram. This ports ccbot's slash-commands into the `chela telegram` bridge.

- **`/screenshot`** and **`/esc`** are now intercepted at the bridge (never typed into the agent's prompt). Every **other** `/command` (Claude-native `/clear`, `/model`, …) still forwards exactly as before.
- Both resolve the target window through a shared `router.resolve()` — the same `chat_id` + topic→window gate (`BindingRegistry.window_for_thread`) as a routed message — and reply into the **same** forum topic.

## How

- **inbound.py** — `TopicRouter`/`RegistryRouter` grow a pure `resolve(chat_id, topic_id)` (the gating half of `route`, now shared). `build_application` registers `CommandHandler`s for `screenshot`/`esc` **before** the catch-all `MessageHandler(filters.TEXT)` (PTB runs one handler per group, so bridge commands are intercepted and never forwarded), and publishes them via `set_my_commands` in a `post_init` hook → the `/` menu autocompletes.
- **`/esc`** → `messenger.send_escape(window_id)` sends a bare tmux `Escape` (interrupt Claude) — *not* the `send_tmux` text path.
- **`/screenshot`** → `messenger.capture_pane(window_id, ansi=True)` (read-only `capture-pane -e -p`) → `telegram/screenshot.py::text_to_image` renders a dark-background **PNG** (ANSI 16/256/RGB parser ported from ccbot, MIT — see NOTICE) sent as a photo. Degrades to a monospaced text snapshot if Pillow isn't installed. Reuses the **already-bundled JetBrains Mono** (SIL OFL 1.1) — no new font binary.
- **pyproject** — `Pillow>=10.0` added to the `[telegram]` extra (+ `uv.lock`).

## Safety / boundaries

- `capture-pane` is read-only — no tmux teardown (the crash that once hit ccbot). No secrets/tokens surfaced; commands stay silent for the wrong chat / unbound topic.
- No new absolute paths, chat ids, or private names. Routing/registry/outbound/`parser.py`/`reconcile.py` contracts untouched.

## Tests

`router.resolve` gating (both routers), `messenger.capture_pane`/`send_escape`, `to_code_block` code-fence escaping, and the PNG renderer (non-empty PNG magic for plain/ANSI/empty input, ANSI parsed not drawn literally). All against stubs, no live Telegram.

- `uv run ruff check chela tests` ✅
- `uv run pytest -q` → **247 passed** ✅

## Summary

**Phase 1 backend** for real push (`feat/push` — the last item in the plan). Every event that already creates an in-app notification (likes, comments, friend requests/accepts, mentions) now **also fans out an FCM push**, by extending the existing `NotificationEmitter` seam — so message text stays single-sourced and every type pushes for free.

**Off `main`.** Backend gates the Flutter Android PR → merge + **deploy before** `feat/push` Flutter.

### Endpoints (`/api/push`)
| Method | Path | Body |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/tokens` | `{token, platform}` → register (upsert) |
| DELETE | `/tokens/{token}` | unregister (logout / refresh cleanup) |

### Design
- **`device_tokens`** collection keyed by the FCM token (globally unique) → re-registering a device that switched accounts reassigns its `uid`. Send to a user = `whereEqualTo("uid", …)`.
- **`PushSender`** seam + **`FcmPushSender`**: multicast **notification + data** (`data = {type, targetType, targetId}` for deep-linking) via `firebase-admin`'s `FirebaseMessaging`; **reactively prunes** tokens FCM reports `UNREGISTERED`/`INVALID_ARGUMENT` (no scheduled job). Best-effort — failures logged, never break the notification flow.
- `NotificationFeedService.emit` calls `pushSender` after persisting, with a **no-op-default constructor** so existing tests are untouched. Self-actions don't push (same guard as in-app).
- **No new dependency** — `firebase-admin` was already present.

## Test plan
- [x] `./mvnw test` — **135 green**, BUILD SUCCESS.
  - `DeviceTokenServiceTest` (6): upsert, reassign-on-reregister, unregister, empty-reject, unknown-user.
  - `PushControllerTest` (4): auth gating, register captures uid+token, empty-token 400, unregister.
  - `NotificationFeedServiceTest` (+2): emit pushes with correct message + deep-link data; self-action doesn't push.
  - `FcmPushSender`'s live FCM call is external SDK — covered by manual/integration, not unit tests.
- [ ] Manual (post-deploy): register a token, trigger a like/mention → device receives a push whose tap-data carries the deep-link.

## Next
Phase 1 Flutter (Android): `firebase_messaging` + `PushService` (register on login, foreground local-notification, cold-start deep-link) + navigatorKey + manifest channel. **Phase 2 (iOS APNs)** is a short config PR blocked only on Apple artifacts — checklist coming after Phase 1.

body: ## Summary Fixes `@ExternalType` generated adapters so their cached `MethodHandle`s are isolated by the resolved application class. A single extension can now safely serve applications, web modules, or plugins that define the same external class name in different classloaders. This PR also: - adds virtual and static dispatch regression coverage across two isolated application classloaders; - corrects the live-attach integration test to wait for the two lines its probe actually emits; - updates the extension guides to describe the classloader-safe cache; and - archives the original implementation plan under `internal/superpowers/plans`, marked for the current consolidated `io.btrace` layout. ## Root Cause Generated adapters previously kept one static `MethodHandle` per method. The first application classloader to resolve an adapter method populated that field. Calls using a same-named class from another application classloader could then fail type checks or dispatch through the wrong loader. ## Validation - `./gradlew --no-daemon :btrace-core:test --tests io.btrace.extension.processor.ExternalTypeProcessorTest` - `./gradlew --no-daemon :btrace-extensions:btrace-ext-test:build` - `./gradlew --no-daemon -Pintegration :integration-tests:test --tests tests.ExternalTypeAdapterIntegrationTest` - `./gradlew --no-daemon :btrace-core:spotlessCheck :integration-tests:spotlessCheck` - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/btraceio/btrace/860)

## Why

Root cause of the live "Something went wrong" crash on opening any staff file: a React component (`StaffTrackRecordPanel`) referenced `role` without receiving it as a prop. **Vite/esbuild treats an undeclared identifier as a global and builds cleanly**, so the bug shipped despite a passing `npm run build`, then threw `ReferenceError` at render → app-wide ErrorBoundary fallback.

(The code fix already merged in #154; this adds the process guardrail so it can't recur.)

## Rule added
For every frontend change: a variable read from an outer scope must be destructured in the component's props **and passed at every call site** (grep them), and run eslint `no-undef` on changed `.jsx` before committing — never trust the build alone for JSX.

author: avila-fe
body:
# IaC: Deploy AWS EC2 + RDS via Terraform e pipeline CI/CD

## Contexto

Esta fase adiciona toda a infraestrutura como código (IaC) necessária para provisionar e opiar o sistema na AWS dentro do free tier, além de corrigir problemas no pipeline e no deploy local Kubernetes.

---

## Alterações

### `terraform/ec2/` — novo módulo EC2 free tier

Substitui a abordagem EKS (custosa) por **EC2 t3.micro + RDS db.t3.micro**, ambos elegíveis ao AWS Free Tier (750 h/mês no primeiro ano).

**`main.tf`**
- Backend S3 com configuração parcial: `key` fixo em `ec2/terraform.tfstate`, `bucket` injetado via `-backend-config` no `terraform init` para não expor o nome no código
- `data "aws_ami"` busca automaticamente a AMI mais recente do Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (Canonical)
- `aws_security_group.app` — libera `:8080` (Spring Boot) e `:22` (SSH)
- `aws_security_group.rds` — PostgreSQL `:5432` acessível apenas pelo SG da EC2
- `aws_db_instance.postgres` — RDS PostgreSQL 16, `db.t3.micro`, 20 GB gp2, sem Multi-AZ, sem Performance Insights (free tier)
- `aws_instance.app` — EC2 `t3.micro` com `user_data` que instala Docker e sobe o container; depende do RDS para garantir que o banco esteja disponível antes do bootstrap

**`user_data.sh.tpl`**
- Instala `docker.io`, habilita o serviço
- Aguarda 30 s para o RDS aceitar conexões
- Executa `docker run` com todas as variáveis de ambiente injetadas via `templatefile` (sem hardcode de segredos)
- `--restart unless-stopped` garante que o container reinicia automaticamente se a EC2 for reiniciada

**`variables.tf`**
- `aws_region`, `db_name`, `db_user`, `db_password`, `jwt_secret`, `app_image`
- Variáveis sensíveis marcadas com `sensitive = true`

**`outputs.tf`**
- `app_url` — URL pública com IP da EC2 (exibida no final do job CI/CD)
- `ec2_public_ip` — IP da instância
- `rds_endpoint` — endpoint do RDS (sensitive)

---

### `terraform/main.tf` — correção de timeout no Kind

Adicionado `wait_for_rollout = false` no recurso `kubectl_manifest.postgres`:

```hcl
resource "kubectl_manifest" "postgres" {
  for_each         = var.use_aws ? {} : data.kubectl_path_documents.postgres.manifests
  yaml_body        = each.value
  wait_for_rollout = false  # evita timeout no Kind

  depends_on = [
    kubectl_manifest.postgres_configmap,
    kubectl_manifest.postgres_secret,
  ]
}
```

Sem essa flag, o Terraform aguardava indefinidamente o pod do Postgres ficar `Ready` no cluster Kind efêmero do GitHub Actions, causando timeout de 10 minutos.

---

### `.github/workflows/pipeline.yml` — novos jobs e correção de condicionais

**Correção: `secrets` não é permitido em `if:` de job**

GitHub Actions não permite o contexto `secrets` em condições de job por razões de segurança. A solução foi usar o contexto `vars` (variáveis de repositório, não secrets):

```yaml
# Antes (inválido — erro no workflow):
if: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID == '' }}

# Depois (correto):
terraform-local:
  if: vars.USE_AWS != 'true'

terraform-ec2:
  if: vars.USE_AWS == 'true'
```

A variável `USE_AWS` é configurada em **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables** no repositório GitHub.

**Novo job `terraform-ec2`**

Substitui o antigo job `terraform-aws` (EKS). Roda quando `USE_AWS == 'true'`:

1. Configura credenciais AWS via `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4`
2. `terraform init` com `-backend-config="bucket=${{ secrets.TF_STATE_BUCKET }}"` — bucket do state passado como secret, não hardcoded
3. `terraform apply` injetando `db_user`, `db_password`, `jwt_secret` e `app_image` com a tag versionada gerada no job `docker-build-push`
4. Exibe a URL da aplicação no output do job

A tag versionada (`v<version>-build.<run_id>`) força a recriação da EC2 a cada build porque o `user_data` muda, garantindo que a instância sempre sobe com a imagem mais recente.

---

## Secrets necessários no GitHub

| Secret | Descrição |
|--------|-----------|
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | Chave de acesso IAM |
| `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | Chave secreta IAM |
| `AWS_REGION` | Região (ex: `us-east-1`) |
| `TF_STATE_BUCKET` | Nome do bucket S3 para o Terraform state |
| `DB_USER` | Usuário do banco |
| `DB_PASSWORD` | Senha do banco |
| `JWT_SECRET` | Segredo JWT da aplicação |
| `DOCKER_USERNAME` | Usuário Docker Hub |
| `DOCKER_HUB_TOKEN` | Token Docker Hub |

## Variável de repositório

| Variável | Valor | Efeito |
|----------|-------|--------|
| `USE_AWS` | `true` | Roda `terraform-ec2` (deploy na AWS) |
| `USE_AWS` | qualquer outro valor ou ausente | Roda `terraform-local` (Kind local) |

---

## Como usar

**Deploy na AWS (via pipeline):**
```bash
# Configurar USE_AWS=true em Settings → Variables
git commit --allow-empty -m "chore: deploy AWS"
git push
# Acompanhar o job terraform-ec2 → output "App URL"
# Aguardar ~3 min após o pipeline para o user_data terminar
```

**Deploy na AWS (manual):**
```bash
cd terraform/ec2
terraform init -backend-config="bucket=<nome-do-bucket>"
terraform apply -auto-approve \
  -var="db_user=..." \
  -var="db_password=..." \
  -var="jwt_secret=..." \
  -var="app_image=favilafrr/os-management:latest"
```

**Destruir:**
```bash
cd terraform/ec2
terraform init -backend-config="bucket=<nome-do-bucket>"
terraform destroy -auto-approve
```

author: trustscoreagent
body:
## Problem
The `Deploy Production` run for the phase-C merge failed at **Verify (5 min)**:

```
ERROR: (gcloud.run.services.describe) unrecognized arguments:
  --filter (did you mean '--flatten'?)
  status.traffic.tag=canary
```

`gcloud run services describe` has **no `--filter`** flag (that's a `list`-only flag). The command exited 2, and because the step runs under `bash -e`, Verify aborted **before** the health-check loop. The auto-rollback lives *inside* that loop, so it never fired either — the deploy just left a 5% canary in place.

## Impact (already handled manually)
The canary revision (`00004-quw`) was healthy — I verified its tagged URL directly (`/health` 200, `/swagger/v1/swagger.json` 200, `/v1/score` 200) and promoted it to 100%. Prod is fully on the new revision now. This PR fixes the workflow so the **next** deploy verifies and promotes automatically.

## Fix
Pull the traffic array as JSON and select the canary target's per-tag URL with `jq` (preinstalled on GitHub ubuntu runners):

```bash
URL=$(gcloud run services describe "$SERVICE_NAME" --region "$GCP_REGION" \
  --format 'json(status.traffic)' \
  | jq -r '.status.traffic[] | select(.tag == "canary") | .url')
```

Verified the JSON shape (`.status.traffic[].{tag,url}`) against the live service.

author: os-zhuang
body:
## What

Proposed **ADR-0056** — the design for consolidating permission-set editing into Studio (Option B, the agreed direction). Epic: #2398.

## Why

A permission set (`sys_permission_set`) has **two** editing surfaces over the **same** record:
- **Setup** renders it as six raw-JSON `Field.textarea` columns (`object_permissions`, `field_permissions`, `system_permissions`, `row_level_security`, `tab_permissions`, `admin_scope`).
- **Studio** has a structured `PermissionMatrixEditor` — but only for `objects` + `fields`.

Raw JSON authorization metadata is invisible to the ADR-0090 explain engine + publish linter, unvalidated at author time, duplicated (objects/fields authorable in both surfaces), and a silent-incident footgun (ADR-0049).

## Decision (Option B)

Permission **editing** → Studio (structured editors). Setup keeps **user management** + permission-set **assignment**. Exception: `system_permissions` (includes `studio.access`) stays in Setup as a structured `sys_capability` multi-select — granting who-may-enter-Studio is an operator act.

| `sys_permission_set` column | target editor | home |
|---|---|---|
| object/field_permissions | `PermissionMatrixEditor` (exists) | Studio |
| system_permissions | `sys_capability` multi-select (new) | **Setup** |
| admin_scope / row_level_security / tab_permissions | new structured editors | Studio |

## Status

**Proposed — design-review PR.** Open questions (RLS editor depth, deep-link UX/scope, legacy-JSON backward-compat) are listed in the ADR for reviewer input. Implementation is phased **P1–P5** in #2398; **P2** (capability picker) starts in a companion PR.

author: qingminlong
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running built-in file search helpers could have an oversized GitHub release metadata success response fully buffered when OpenClaw needs to download fd or ripgrep.

## Why This Change Was Made

The helper installer already bounds archive downloads and cancels release-check error bodies. This change applies the existing bounded response reader to the release metadata success body before JSON parsing, keeping the fix local to the tool installer without changing helper selection, archive download limits, or config behavior.

## User Impact

Helper auto-installation now keeps GitHub release metadata reads under a fixed byte cap before parsing, so a bad release metadata response cannot bypass the bounded IO used by the rest of the helper download path.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: current head `876354a6bc69c375b3c751f0bdc4731937a68535` exercises the real fd helper auto-install path after the bounded release metadata read change. In an isolated `OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR`, `getToolPath("fd")` returned `null`, OpenClaw downloaded fd through `ensureTool("fd")`, installed it under the agent bin directory, and the installed binary ran successfully.
- Commands / artifacts:
  - `node --import <repo>/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs --input-type=module -` with a repo-local proof script importing `src/agents/utils/tools-manager.ts` and calling `ensureTool("fd", false)` after setting an isolated `OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR` and a `PATH` without fd/fdfind.
  - `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD -- src/agents/utils/tools-manager.ts src/agents/utils/tools-manager.test.ts`
- Observed result:

```text
[proof] head=876354a6bc69c375b3c751f0bdc4731937a68535
[proof] isolated OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR=<OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR>
[proof] PATH=D:\soft-programs\nodejs;C:\WINDOWS\System32
[proof] before getToolPath("fd")=null
fd not found. Downloading...
fd installed to <OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR>\bin\fd.exe
[proof] ensureTool("fd") returned <OPENCLAW_AGENT_DIR>\bin\fd.exe
[proof] installed exists=true
[proof] installed under agent bin=true
[proof] fd --version status=0
[proof] fd --version stdout=fd 10.4.2
```

- `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD -- src/agents/utils/tools-manager.ts src/agents/utils/tools-manager.test.ts` passed with no whitespace errors.

author: ginderjeremiah
body:
## Summary

#1851 correctly made `AbandonBattle` apply the 5s post-battle cooldown when an abandon resolves an outcome, and `BattleService.StartBattle` anchors the replacement battle's `BattleStartTime` to that cooldown's expiry. But the `NewEnemy` response contract was never updated: `NewEnemyModel` already had a `Cooldown` field, but the enemy-bearing response only ever populated `EnemyInstance` + `ZoneId`. The client presented the new enemy immediately, so after any idle loss/draw the client's battle timeline ran ~5s ahead of the server's.

## Failure scenario this fixes

1. Idle loss → client calls `NewEnemy` (the idle loop never sends `BattleLost`; that's boss-only).
2. Server books the loss, sets `EnemyCooldown = now+5s`, anchors the replacement battle at that expiry — but returned the enemy with no cooldown/offset.
3. Client fought immediately; its honest `DefeatEnemy` claim arrived ~5s − rtt **before** the server-computed completion → rejected by the `ClaimedBeforeBattleCouldFinish` anti-cheat gate (warning logged), triggering a full `resyncPlayerAndInventory`.
4. In a losing streak (idling in a too-hard zone) this repeated on every loss: extra round trips, hand-backs, refights, and warning-log noise burying genuine tamper signals.

## Changes

- **`Game.Api/Sockets/Commands/NewEnemy.cs`**: populates `NewEnemyModel.Cooldown` whenever `PlayerState.EnemyCooldown` is still in the future after `StartBattle` returns — which is exactly (and only) when this call's own abandon just incurred the post-battle cooldown.
- **`UI/src/lib/engine/battle/enemy-manager.ts`**: when a `NewEnemy` response bundles both an enemy and a positive cooldown, the fetch loop now waits it out via `battleEngine.startLoading` (the same mechanism the `DefeatEnemy`/`BattleLost` cooldown/prefetch flow already uses) before presenting the enemy, re-checking the stop/supersession guards after the wait.
- **`docs/backend-battle.md`**: closes the gap between the documented server-side anchor and what the response contract now actually carries.

## Tests

- `Game.Api.Tests/Integration/NewEnemySocketTests.cs`: new integration test — starts a battle, backdates it so the next `NewEnemy`'s abandon resolves an outcome, and asserts the response carries both the fresh `EnemyInstance` and a positive `Cooldown` bounded by the 5s post-battle cooldown.
- `UI/src/tests/lib/engine/battle/enemy-manager.test.ts`: new cases pinning that a bundled positive cooldown is waited out via `battleEngine.startLoading` before the enemy is presented, and that a cooldown-free response (a genuinely fresh spawn) is presented immediately with no wait.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet build` — solution builds clean, 0 warnings.
- [x] `dotnet test` — full backend suite passes: 3081/3081.
- [x] `npm run check` (svelte-check) — 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean.
- [x] `npm run test:unit:ci` — full suite passes: 3626/3626.

Closes #1881

author: souliane
body:
Closes the privacy-seam coverage gap from the final holistic review: forge writers that post colleague-visible content without routing through the scanned leak/send-proxy seam. Each finding was audit-surfaced (its adversarial verify never ran), so each was first VERIFIED against current code, then fixed with an anti-vacuous regression test observed RED before the fix.

## The seam

Two routers existed:

- `route_forge_write` (`core/send_proxy.py`) — the correct chokepoint: public-repo leak gate (`scan_outbound_text`) **and** the #117 send-proxy audit/allowlist/redaction.
- `route_forge_send` (`cli/review/send_routing.py`) — send-proxy audit **only, no leak scan**.

The fix unifies on the scanned chokepoint so no content-bearing forge write can reach a colleague surface unscanned.

## CC-4 (root) — two divergent routers → one scanned chokepoint

**Verified real.** `route_forge_send` called `route_send` only — no `scan_outbound_text`. A caller on that path skipped the public-repo leak gate every other forge writer runs. It is the root enabler of CC-1/CC-2.

**Fix.** `route_forge_send` now delegates to `route_forge_write`, converting a raised `OutboundBlockedError` into the existing `(note, refusal)` contract. `t3 review` is GitLab-only, so the forge is pinned to GitLab for the probe/audit channel. Its single caller (`ReviewService.post_comment`) is unchanged. Empty note stays a no-op (no scan, no audit). The chokepoint-parity test now pins `send_routing` to the stronger `route_forge_write` seam.

**RED before:** against the old `route_send`-only router, `test_leaking_comment_to_a_public_repo_is_refused_before_the_wire` failed (no refusal — leak not scanned) and `test_empty_note_is_a_noop_passthrough_with_no_audit` failed (old path audited even an empty note). GREEN after.

## CC-1 (HIGH) — `t3 pr post-test-plan` posted unscanned

**Verified real.** `post_test_plan` (and its deprecated `post-evidence` alias) built `note_body` and posted it via `host.post_pr_comment` / `update_pr_comment` with no leak scan — laxer than the MCP / ticket / test-plan-body writers.

**Fix.** The composed body routes through `route_forge_write` BEFORE consuming the on-behalf approval, so a leaking body is refused (nothing posted) and every post is audited. The CI project path is a bare slug, so the forge is left unqualified — the leak gate fails CLOSED (scans) on an unknown host rather than skipping.

**RED before:** with the scrub removed, all three tests failed — a body containing a banned token posted `{'id': 1}` raw instead of returning an error. GREEN after; the leaking body returns `privacy gate refused` and `post_pr_comment` is never called (alias too).

## CC-2 (MEDIUM) — `close_dead_issue` posted unscanned

**Verified real.** `close_dead_issue` passed its audit comment straight to `host.close_issue`, while the MCP `<forge>_issue_close` twin scrubs the identical op via `route_forge_write`.

**Fix.** The close comment routes through `route_forge_write` (repo from `host.repo_for_issue_url`, forge from `forge_from_url`), matching the MCP twin, via a small helper so the handler stays within the return-count bar. A leak/blocked verdict — or any scrub failure — SKIPs the close (best-effort: never raise, never post unscanned).

**RED before:** with the scrub removed, `test_leaking_close_comment_to_a_public_repo_is_refused_and_close_skipped` failed (the leaking comment was posted, close not skipped) and `test_clean_close_comment_writes_a_send_audit_row` failed (no audit row). GREEN after.

## CC-3 (MEDIUM) — structural pin for the NEXT forge writer

**Verified real.** The chokepoint tests covered only enumerated fixed callers; a new forge writer could reach a raw backend forge-write method undetected (CC-1/CC-2 prove it).

**How it works.** A new registry entry `forge-comment-write-seam` in `quality/chokepoints.yaml` drives the existing AST checker (`scripts/hooks/check_chokepoints.py`): it walks `src/` and FAILS when any body-bearing forge-write method — `post_pr_comment`, `update_pr_comment`, `post_issue_comment`, `update_issue_comment`, `close_issue`, `create_issue`, `update_issue` — is called from a module outside `allowed_modules`. `allowed_modules` is exactly the set verified to scrub via `route_forge_write` first (plus the backend primitive layer and the reply-transport `_enforce_privacy` + `_route_reply` twin). The next bypass is caught at CI, not in an audit.

**Anti-vacuous.** New checker tests flag a bypass module (`close_issue` / `post_pr_comment` / `create_issue` outside the seam → exit 1) and pass a scrubbing module (exit 0); a self-maintenance test pins the full method set so a new protocol method must be added here too. Demonstrated RED: with the registry entry removed, the flag-tests returned 0 (not flagged) and the self-maintenance test raised. GREEN with the entry.

## Verification

- Each regression test observed RED before its fix, GREEN after.
- Targeted tree-wide gates GREEN under `-n auto` (210 passed) and `-n 0` (286 passed, 3 pre-existing xfails) — send-proxy/routing, pr command, mechanical-loop, `tests/quality/test_chokepoints.py` + `test_import_contracts.py`, `tests/conformance/`, module-health.
- `uv run ruff check` clean; `makemigrations --check` no-op (no model changes).
- All pre-commit + pre-push leak/quality gates passed (banned-terms, gitleaks, no-overlay-leak, chokepoint, #685 public-push gate) — no `--no-verify`.

Draft — do not merge.


---

## Cold-review HOLD resolution (round 2)

### BLOCKER (fixed) — `ticket create-sub` posted title/body/labels unscanned
Verified real: `create_sub` sent the child `title`/`body`/`labels` straight to `host.create_sub_issue` → the backend `create_issue` RAW, with no leak scan — while its sibling `comment` in the same file and the MCP `issue_create` twin both scrub. Fixed by routing title/body/each-label through `route_forge_write` before the create (mirroring `comment` exactly). Registered `create_sub_issue` in the `forge-comment-write-seam` chokepoint. RED-before: with the scrub removed, a leaking title/label posted the child raw and wrote no audit row; all three `TicketCreateSubRoutesThroughSeam` tests fail pre-fix, pass after.

### Completeness guard made genuinely exhaustive
The old guard only asserted the hardcoded method names existed on the protocol — it never enumerated the protocol, which is exactly why `create_sub_issue` slipped through green. The guard now ENUMERATES `CodeHostBackend` and derives "body-bearing" from each method's signature (a `body`/`title`/`comment`/`labels`/`description` param), asserting every such method is registered. RED-before proof: dropping `create_sub_issue` from both the registry and the set (simulating the original bug) — the old check would have passed, the enumeration reports `unregistered=['create_sub_issue']`.

### `create_pr` description — VERIFIED COVERED (no code change)
Traced all three `create_pr` call sites; the PR description body is scanned before it can reach a public forge:
- `fast_push.py` (`ForgeClient.create_pr`): the body/title IS the commit message, and `LeakGateScan` scans that exact `message_text` (banned-terms + overlay-leak + secret-scan, via `by_path[_MESSAGE_PATH]`) before the push+create — it uses `--no-verify` precisely because it self-scans.
- `ship.py` / `_ensure_pr.py` (`CodeHostBackend.create_pr`): the title/description are built from the branch's own commit message (`git.last_commit_message` / `_branch_own_commit_message`), pushed via the normal `git.push` (not `--no-verify`), so the #685 pre-push gate scans those commits. A leak in the body would be blocked at push → no PR.
- `tasks.py:359` is a docstring, not a call site.

`create_pr(spec)` carries its body in a `PullRequestSpec` object (no body-shaped param), so the enumeration guard correctly leaves it out of scope. Per the reviewer's "if genuinely covered, don't add redundant scanning," no code change. Transparent residual note: the non-commit injections into the `CodeHostBack

author: omkhar
body:
## Summary

The `docker-desktop-launch-smoke` certification scenario (the `macos/arm64` `local_compat/docker-desktop/compat` boundary cert) fails on any host that has real Codex auth staged at `~/.codex` — i.e. every real local-operator-certification machine, which is the exact target for a compat-boundary certification.

Root cause: the scenario's `inspect_target_state` and `doctor_target` functions invoked `scripts/workcell --inspect` / `--doctor` with **neither** `--injection-policy` **nor** `--no-default-injection-policy`, so they fell back to the default injection policy. That resolves `codex_auth` to the host `~/.codex`, and `resolve_credential_sources` then fails closed:

```
credentials.codex_auth must not point inside host provider/auth state: /Users/.../.codex
resolve_credential_sources exited 1
```

The guard is correct — it refuses to use host provider auth as a session credential source. The bug is that the diagnostic pre-checks resolve credentials at all. The scenario's own launch steps already exercise real credential injection with the fixture policy; the `--inspect`/`--doctor` steps only assert **target-state** fields (`profile`, `target_state_dir`, `target_kind`, assurance class, support-matrix rows) — nothing about credentials.

Fix: add `--no-default-injection-policy` to the two diagnostic calls, matching the sibling `aws-ec2-ssm-launch-smoke` and `gcp-vm-launch-smoke` certification scenarios, which already use exactly that flag on their `--doctor` pre-check. This keeps the diagnostics credential-free and makes the cert runnable on any host regardless of staged provider auth, with no assertion coverage loss.

## Validation

- **Reproduced** the failure on this MacBook (real `~/.codex` present), then confirmed `--no-default-injection-policy` on `--inspect`/`--doctor` returns `rc=0` and still emits every asserted target-state field.
- **Certified the compat boundary end-to-end**: `tests/scenarios/shared/test-docker-desktop-launch-smoke.sh` now passes against real Docker Desktop (`29.5.3`) on `macos/arm64` — `Docker Desktop provider launch smoke scenario passed`.
- `go test ./...`, shellcheck, and `scripts/pre-merge.sh --profile pr-parity` all green.

This is a STEP-D compat-boundary certification deliverable: the `local_compat/docker-desktop/compat` boundary is now empirically certified on the maintainer host (the `local_vm/colima/strict` boundary was certified separately via `agent-launch-smoke`).

author: thechefcharles
body:
**Punch-list Tier 1 #4.**

`leave_group` deleted the caller's membership and the group (if now empty), but never touched `groups.owner_id`. When the **owner** left a group that still had members, `owner_id` kept pointing at the departed non-member — and every management RPC (`rename_group`, `remove_group_member`, `respond_join_request`) gates on `owner_id = uid`. Result: the remaining members could never rename, kick, or approve join requests again.

## Fix
On owner-leave with members remaining, hand ownership to the **oldest remaining member** (`ORDER BY joined_at, user_id`). Empty-group deletion is unchanged.

## Verification (BEGIN/ROLLBACK)
Group with owner + M1 (older) + M2:
- Owner leaves → `owner_id` becomes **M1** ✅
- M2 then M1 leave → group **deleted** ✅

author: kdroidfilter
body:
Closes #304

## Problem

The native library cache was shared across versions (`<cacheDir>/<platform>/lib.so` + a `.fingerprint` file next to it). Between fingerprint validation and `System.load`, another running application using a different version of the same library could replace the extracted file — the loaded library no longer matched the validated fingerprint.

## Fix

The cache is now content-addressed, as suggested in the issue: the fingerprint is part of the extraction path.

```
<cacheDir>/<platform>/<fingerprint>/<lib>
```

Different versions never share a file, which eliminates the race by construction:

- `.fingerprint` files and the validate/write logic are gone — if the file exists in its content-addressed directory, it is the right one. An existing file is never replaced.
- Concurrent extraction of the *same* version stays harmless (same bytes): if the atomic move loses the race, the existing target is loaded; the temp-copy fallback for locked files on Windows is preserved.
- Sidecars (e.g. `WebView2Loader.dll`) live in the same directory as the main library (required by the dynamic linker), and their fingerprints are included in the directory key, so the race is eliminated for them too.
- Fingerprint format changes from `crc:size` to `crc-size` (`:` is illegal in Windows file names).
- Dev-mode bonus: with `file:` URLs the fingerprint is size+mtime, so every rebuild gets a fresh directory — the stale-cache issue that build scripts worked around by clearing the cache disappears.

Old flat cache files from previous versions are left in place (benign, OS-cleanable cache directory); no purge logic added.

## Tests

`NativeLibraryLoaderTest`: distinct path-safe fingerprints for distinct content, existing files never replaced, extraction when target is missing. `:core-runtime:test`, `detekt` and `ktlintCheck` pass.

author: tranhoangnguyen03
body:
## Summary

- preserve private Pi settings permissions during runtime duplicate repair
- centralize shared persona parsing, schema policy, and answer extraction
- add strict TypeScript boundary checks and broader syntax discovery
- expand consult, setup, package, and real Pi RPC release coverage
- correct the supported `pi-subagents` floor to the published 0.34.0 release
- remove the unsupported `resultDelivery` request field
- keep bridge timeout promises alive in headless Node processes
- pin CI actions, add a prepublish test gate, and document the initial npm/GitHub release sequence

## Why

A whole-repository code and design audit found one security-sensitive file-mode regression, several duplicated policy/normalization paths, weakly typed extension boundaries, and release-confidence gaps. The release review also exposed an incorrect dependency requirement for a nonexistent `pi-subagents` 0.35.0 version.

The settings issue came from replacing a private settings file through a temporary file created with default permissions. The dependency issue came from documenting and enforcing an unverified future capability instead of the published slash-bridge contract. The final Node 22 CI failure exposed request timers that were unreferenced while callers still awaited their Promises, allowing a headless process to exit before reporting a missing or stalled bridge.

## User impact

There is no intended workflow change. Runtime repair now preserves private permissions, the supported dependency matches the real published package, bridge failures reliably surface in headless sessions, and release checks cover the packaged extension more directly.

## Verification

- `npm ci`
- `npm test` — 123 tests passed, including real Pi RPC smoke
- `npm audit --omit=dev` — 0 vulnerabilities
- `npm pack --dry-run --json`
- `npm publish --dry-run --access public` — prepublish tests passed
- `git diff --check`
- GitHub Actions on Node 22.19 and 24 — passed for push and pull-request events
- manual provider-backed consult and roundtable smoke with `pi-subagents` 0.34.0 — passed

author: yzxoi
body:
## 需求与摘要

Closes #33.
Closes #39.
Closes #44.
Closes #51.

在 #50 的统一等级基础上完成论坛 staging 可交付闭环：每日签到与真实活跃度、可恢复等级评估、密码优先的友好认证、持久安全邮件、私有 OSS → 私有 Delivery → 签名 CDN 媒体链路、管理员媒体治理与 reconciliation，以及 main/PR 隔离的版本化部署流程。

本 PR 按当前业务目标实现功能，不照搬 issue 中已不适合现状的内部框架。例如密码重置在撤销旧 session 后返回唯一新 session；Redis/CAPTCHA 不可用时敏感入口 fail closed；PR Preview 保持 provider-free。

## 产品行为与不变量

- 首页右上角是每日签到；上海自然日幂等，展示连续/累计天数并跨午夜自动刷新。
- 活跃度由发帖、评论、点赞、签到四项版本化权重计算；点赞按日封顶。管理员可修改权重/阈值，等级自动评估每次最多升一级。
- 等级 evaluator 使用持久 cursor、50-account batch、lease heartbeat、账号失败隔离、指数退避与 8 次 dead-letter；坏账号不阻塞后续账号。
- 登录默认密码，也保留邮箱验证码与注册；set/change/reset 原子替换 session。未知账号、无密码与错误凭据使用中性响应；验证码先预检再执行有界 Argon2，最终事务重验并一次性消费。
- 密码 set/change/reset 和管理员邀请在业务事务写 Identity email job；worker 租约、重试、dead-letter 与安全事件均持久化，不保存邮件正文、验证码或 provider response。
- Ingest/Delivery bucket 均 private 且分离。只接受静态 JPEG/PNG/WebP；服务端有界解码、去 metadata、生成三个 immutable WebP 变体，发布后只返回 300 秒 Type-A CDN URL。
- 普通 moderator 不能自审；当前最高角色 ADMIN 仅可在 recent-auth、显式确认、理由和 preview evidence 下自审本人媒体。另一 ADMIN 仍不可被审核。
- block/delete 顺序为 CDN purge 完成 → Delivery delete → Ingest delete。过期 processing worker 的晚到写会重新武装 cleanup，不会复活公开状态。
- PR Preview 不读取生产 OSS/CDN secret；所有 PR close（含 merged）都清理 preview。Main 在停旧 backend 前执行真实 STS、不可覆盖、Delivery、签名 CDN 与 purge preflight。
- Credit ledger、签名与 Web2.5 合规边界不变。

## 影响矩阵

- [x] 产品行为或 Web UI
- [x] `contract/openapi.yaml` 与 Web 生成类型
- [x] PostgreSQL migration、backfill 或兼容窗口
- [x] 身份、授权、PII、隐私、保留或审计
- [ ] 积分合规、签名、防重放或 ledger 完整性（未修改 credit 行为）
- [x] Media/OSS、cache、counter、notification 或 background job
- [x] 依赖、配置、CI、部署或外部 provider

新 runtime dependency 仅为 `image 0.25.5` 的静态 JPEG/PNG/WebP decode/encode 路径；直接相关 crates 为 MIT/Apache-2.0（zune-jpeg 另含 Zlib），未引入外部网络服务依赖。

## 文档影响

已同步 canonical product/architecture/security/operations 文档，重点包括：

- `docs/product/activity-scoring.md`
- `docs/product/identity-and-access.md`
- `docs/product/content-media-and-discovery.md`
- `docs/product/trust-safety-and-administration.md`
- `docs/product/current-state-and-roadmap.md`
- `docs/operations/media-storage.md`
- `docs/operations/deployment-and-previews.md`
- `docs/operations/email-delivery.md`
- `docs/security/authorization-and-audit.md`
- `docs/security/privacy-and-data-lifecycle.md`

## 验证

- [x] `python3 scripts/check_docs.py`
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [x] Fresh PostgreSQL：migration 1 → 63 全部成功
- [x] Fresh PostgreSQL + Redis：`cargo test --all -- --nocapture --test-threads=1` 全工作区通过
- [x] Web OpenAPI generation 幂等
- [x] Web Vitest：55 files / 116 tests
- [x] Web lint / typecheck / production build
- [x] Deploy unittest：27 tests
- [x] ShellCheck、`bash -n`、Ruff lint/format、5 个 GitHub YAML parse
- [x] 已知 secret pattern 扫描无命中
- [ ] 真实 Alibaba provider smoke：只能由 main staging deploy 使用 Environment secrets 执行，PR Preview 有意 provider-free
- [x] PR Preview deploy + HTTP smoke：frontend、`/settings` deep link、health、ready；GitHub runner private-port 负向探针

## Migration、部署与回滚

- `0060_activity_check_ins.sql`：签到事实、四项 score projection、trust cooldown/evaluation run。
- `0061_media_delivery.sql`：publication/variant/processing/purge/delete/reconciliation 状态机与完整性 trigger。
- `0062_identity_security_delivery.sql`：credential-version reset、security events、durable email jobs。
- `0063_trust_evaluation_recovery.sql`：持久 cursor、backoff/dead 与逐账号 failure inventory。

四个 migration 均 forward-only。新 backend 一旦启动并可能执行 migration，失败时不得重启旧 backend；保留现场并 roll forward。Frontend release 可独立回滚。

Main staging 合并前需要按 runbook 配齐两个 private bucket、Ingest upload role/backend caller、Delivery worker、CDN Type-A 双 key、CDN purge identity、path-level prevent-overwrite rule、GitHub `main-staging` Environment，以及服务器 `EMAIL_ENCRYPTION_STRICT=true`、active version 与两项独立 32-byte hex email encryption key。缺项或权限过宽/不可验证时部署 fail closed。

## Preview 与证据

Preview：`http://20.205.27.178:8080/pr-50/`。Actions run [`29193126957`](https://github.com/YourTongji/YourTJ-Platform/actions/runs/29193126957) 已通过；站外 smoke 验证主页、`/settings` deep link、health、ready 均为 200，GitHub runner 验证 15050/16050 不可直连。服务器 Docker/`ss` 同时确认 frontend/backend 只监听 `127.0.0.1`。本地自动化另覆盖桌面/窄屏首页、跨上海午夜、密码/register/reset、安全设置、媒体上传/过期 URL 恢复、管理员审核/reconciliation 与 deployment fake-provider journeys。

## 已知限制与 Review 重点

- #35 保留：refresh/access 仍在 localStorage；HttpOnly refresh cookie、CSRF 与跨标签同步需独立迁移。
- #40 保留：JWT `kid`/多 key 验证与 signing-key rotation 尚未交付。
- 普通管理员逐账号 capability delegation 仍是 Planned；当前持久 `admin` 承担 ADMIN 语义，不能把静态 `mod` 包装为已完成的委派管理员。
- Profile/search 等 legacy avatar DTO 尚未全部统一为 typed expiry；主要 Web consumer 已用 4 分钟 refetch + image-error recovery，后续仍应收敛 contract。
- PR Preview 没有 TTL scheduler，依靠所有 PR close cleanup；失败时按 runbook inventory/手工清理。
- Web build 仍有既有 `oss-vendor` chunk-size warning，不影响构建。
- Reviewer 请重点检查 migration forward-only cutover、ADMIN 自审边界、provider prevent-overwrite release gate、late-write cleanup rearm、email encryption main gate 与 auth enumeration/Argon2 限流。

author: sainathr19
body:
Adds Solana as the third chain kind, built on **surfpool**, at feature parity with the EVM and Starknet stacks. A Solana chain (`solana-1` on `:8899`) now boots by default alongside the two Anvil chains and the Starknet chain. Built up as one commit per capability.

## What's included

- **Boot** — `SolanaEngine` (surfpool `1.4.0`) with deterministic, funded dev accounts (keypairs from documented `sha256("wharfnet-solana-dev-<i>")` seeds); `getHealth` readiness probe; unified `status`/manifest.
- **Chain control** — `wharfnet solana mine | increase-time | warp | pause-clock | resume-clock` over surfpool's `surfnet_*` cheat JSON-RPC.
- **SPL test tokens** — USDC/WBTC at fixed deterministic mint addresses, seeded onto the dev accounts via cheatcodes at boot (a new post-boot engine hook — surfpool has no program to deploy).
- **Faucet** — `wharfnet faucet solana <addr>` funds native SOL (`requestAirdrop`) and tops up SPL tokens (additive, no key needed).
- **Persistence** — `up --resume` / `up --reset` keep or discard a chain's state via surfpool's `--db`/`--surfnet-id` SQLite surfnet, matching the EVM/Starknet chains.
- **Forking** — `fork_url` boots a copy-on-read fork of a live network (surfpool `--rpc-url`); no `fork_block` (surfpool has no fork-at-slot).
- **Studio explorer** — surfpool's built-in Studio UI, on by default (skipped by `--bare`), published on the RPC port + 10000. Adds a generic `Engine::extra_host_ports()` so an engine can declare ports beyond its RPC one, folded into the cross-chain collision check.
- **WebSocket RPC** — surfpool's WS endpoint published on the RPC port + 1 (Solana's convention), so subscriptions and `confirmTransaction` work from the host. Always on; advertised via a new `ws` field in the manifest.

## Testing

Each capability has unit coverage plus a docker-backed e2e that boots a real surfpool chain (health, funded accounts, seeded tokens, faucet top-ups surviving `down`/`up --resume`, forking a live origin, the Studio page, and a real WebSocket upgrade + `slotSubscribe`). E2e tests self-skip without Docker. Full suite green, clippy + fmt clean.

Remaining follow-up: "weird" Token-2022 test tokens (transfer-fee, interest-bearing) — deferred as not feasible via surfpool cheatcodes.

body:
## Summary

Re-opened against `main`: #3 was merged into its stacked base branch (`feat/xhigh-and-custom-model-providers`) rather than `main`, so the cursor provider never landed there. This PR carries the same two commits, including the usage extraction added after live verification.

Adds `runner.provider: cursor`, driving Cursor CLI (`cursor-agent`) in headless print mode, mirroring the `claude-code` provider:

- **Command**: `cursor-agent -p --output-format stream-json [--model <name>] [--force] <prompt>`; `dangerouslySkipPermissions: true` maps to `--force` (which also grants workspace trust — `cursor-agent` refuses headless runs in untrusted directories without it; documented).
- **Resume**: `--resume <chatId>`; session ids captured from stream-json `session_id` and persisted for pause/resume.

author: rusdad
body:
### Motivation
- Hover/picking was inaccurate because the code relied on Three.js `Raycaster.params.Line.threshold` in world units, which yields a hit region that varies with camera distance and angle. 
- Click selection was lost because `OrbitControls.start` was treated as a drag sentinel, which caused pointer state to be cleared and `pointerup` to be ignored. 
- The picking controller duplicated canonical selection state, preventing later synchronization from the source panel and blocking repeat callbacks.

### Description
- Replaced world-space raycaster line threshold with screen-space picking: render segments are projected to NDC, converted to CSS-pixel canvas coordinates and scored with `distancePointToSegment2D`, selecting the closest segment within `6` CSS px; math helpers live in `public/nc/NcPickingMath.js` and projection/traversal is in `public/nc/NcPickingController.js` (`pickFromPointerEvent`).
- Reworked pointer interaction to use an explicit pointer-state (`createPointerInteractionState`) where `pointerdown` stores `pointerId`/`clientX`/`clientY`, `pointermove` sets `didDrag` when movement > `5` CSS px, and `pointerup` treats the event as a click only when `didDrag === false`; removed dependence on `OrbitControls.start/end` and instead listen to `change` to recompute hover after camera changes.
- Removed local `selectedSegmentId` from the picking controller so `NcSelectionController` remains the canonical owner of selection, and the picker now emits `onSelectSegmentChange` for clicks (including explicit `null` when clicking empty space) without blocking repeat callbacks.
- Added `test/nc-interaction.test.mjs` with unit tests for `distancePointToSegment2D`, `ndcToCssPixels`, screen-space closest-segment selection, click/drag threshold logic, and selection semantics, and wired it into `npm test` by updating `package.json`.

### Testing
- Ran `npm test` which executes `node test/overlap-union.test.js && node test/top-regions.test.js && node test/nc-parser.test.mjs && node test/nc-interaction.test.mjs`, and the full suite passed with exit code `0` (output: OK messages for overlap-union, top-regions, NC parser and NC interaction helpers). 
- The new `test/nc-interaction.test.mjs` verifies horizontal/vertical/diagonal distance math, picking chooses the nearest screen-space segment and respects the 6px threshold, click/drag classification at 5px, and that OrbitControls start does not cancel clicks. 
- Tests produce Node warnings about typeless ES modules but these are informational only and do not affect pass/fail of the test suite.

author: jasmine-nguyen
body:
## What

Cold-launching the app already signed in (the Face ID unlock path, `EXPO_PUBLIC_AUTH_BIOMETRIC_ENABLED=true` + a stored session) crashed Release builds to the home screen in under a second.

## Root cause (confirmed live on device with trace logging)

`AuthGate` rendered `<Redirect>` **in place of** its children — the root `<Stack>` at `app/_layout.tsx:79`. Unmounting the Stack resets navigation to the index route, so the gate saw `authed + onIndex` again and re-redirected:

```
[gate] status=authed segments=[]                   → target=/(tabs)/budgets
[gate] status=authed segments=["(tabs)","budgets"] → target=null
[gate] status=authed segments=[]                   → target=/(tabs)/budgets   ← reset by the remount
```

~50 nested updates → "Maximum update depth exceeded" → RCTFatal kills the Release app.

## Fix

The redirect now renders inside an opaque absolute-fill cover **on top of** the still-mounted children (unconditional wrapper — moving the children's tree position would remount the Stack and reintroduce the bug). The cover doubles as the privacy/touch shield while the redirect lands: opaque `C.bg`, explicit zIndex above the in-gate floating headers, default pointerEvents blocks touches.

Also fixes the same loop reached via the background→Face-ID resume path.

## Tests

- **New** `authGateRedirectLoop.screen.test.tsx` — deterministic replay of the device loop (reactive segments store; Redirect completes navigation in an effect; child models the Stack-remount reset). Proven red on the pre-fix code.
- **New** `authGateTransitions.screen.test.tsx` — dynamic edges: sign-out from a deep route, authed→anon flip while the redirect is in flight, AppState background→active lock/unlock convergence, late navReady release, StrictMode double effects. All proven red on revert (plus a surgical `pointerEvents` mutation caught by exactly one test).
- Static suites flipped: children stay mounted + cover present during redirects; cover absent on pass-through; cover style pinned.
- 26 gate tests + 634 logic tests green · tsc clean · sharded coverage 97.5% (floor 30%).

Board: WHIT-265 · Follow-ups filed: WHIT-266 (lock screen loses your place), overlays-above-cover, Face ID silent read-through.

body:
## Audit module — closes AC-017/018/019/020 (INV-005)

Implements the immutable, hash-chained audit trail as **literal AC-017**: every governed state change emits an enriched `AuditEvent` in the **same transaction** as the module write (NFR-042), readable + verifiable by the Auditor. Delivered as five GO-gated stages (PR0–PR4) on one branch, squash-merge intended.

### Decisions (both Accepted)
- **ADR-0026** (amends ADR-0009) — audit enrichment, hash-versioning (v1 byte-preserved so history still verifies; v2 via `HashVersion`), same-transaction atomicity.
- **ADR-0027** — audit-read RBAC = {Auditor, Chairman, Secretary}; **Administrator excluded** on SoD-5 grounds (supersedes the FR-153 role clause).

### What's in it
- **PR1 — infra:** enriched versioned `AuditEvent` + `Audit_Enrich` migration; before/after scalar-delta capture (`AuditCaptureInterceptor` + request-scoped buffer, keyed by `PublicId`); widened `IAuditSink.EmitEnrichedAsync`; **same-transaction unit-of-work** over one shared `DbConnection` (avoids MSDTC) with lazy ambient-tx begin + `TransactionBehavior` commit/rollback.
- **PR2 — emit sites:** all governed state-change sites across 9 modules migrated to `EmitEnrichedAsync` (subjectType = CLR aggregate name). Verified populated end-to-end on real SQL.
- **PR3 — read/verify API:** `GET /api/audit` (filter/paginate, newest-first) + `GET /api/audit/verify` (chain scan), gated by `Policies.AuditRead`. RBAC proven on both routes (Auditor/Chairman/Secretary→200, Member/Reviewer/**Administrator**→403, no-token→401).
- **PR4 — /audit UI:** read-only register built to `ACMP Lists & Registers.dc.html` (INV-014); FE RBAC aligned to the API policy; i18n EN+AR. Live pixel-VR PASS (EN-light + AR-dark/RTL).
- **PR1 boot fix:** `PersistSecurityInfo=true` on the shared connection — a shared open `SqlConnection` masked its password, so EF's fresh-DB `master` connection failed `sa` login (18456). Guarded by a Docker-free regression test.
- **Build:** `Dockerfile.backend` — single shared build stage (compile once for api+worker) replacing the dual `Dockerfile.api`/`Dockerfile.worker`.

### Gates (local)
BE Domain 188 / Arch 41 / App 806 / Integration 25 / Api 203 · coverage **99.66%** (no file <95%) · `dotnet format` clean (only the generated `Audit_Enrich` migration, CI-clean on Linux) · i18n 1521 parity · **Keystone 7/7 critical gates OK**.

### Test plan
- [ ] CI green (the push-time full-stack e2e is the only place all 11 contexts boot on the shared connection end-to-end — the class of bug the PR1 fix addresses).
- [ ] Operator: production live-confirm of the `/audit` register against real data.

author: greluc
body:
## What & why

Prod mail alerts (`TargetDown` / `DeployHealthRestartFailing`, container restart storm) were caused by the **ingest** gateway hitting its `pids: 2048` cgroup cap and crashing with `pthread_create failed (EAGAIN)` (native-thread OOM) at ~17h uptime — **not** heap, and **not** a JVM thread leak.

### Root cause (confirmed on the live container)

The container runs the JVM as PID 1 (`exec java`), which does not reap orphaned children. The 30s Docker HEALTHCHECK uses BusyBox `wget --no-check-certificate https://…`, and BusyBox `wget` forks an `ssl_client` TLS helper it does not wait on; on exit it reparents to PID 1 and lingers as a `<defunct>` zombie. One accumulates per probe until the pid cap is exhausted, at which point the JVM can no longer create an OS thread.

Live evidence (`/proc` on the running ingest at ~6h uptime):

- JVM threads: **36** (healthy — this is why `JvmThreadsHigh` never fired)
- total processes: **716**, of which **712 × `(ssl_client) Z`**
- cgroup pids: **750 / 2048**, climbing ~1 per 30s

All three JVM apps (backend/frontend/ingest) share the same wget-HTTPS probe, so all three were latently affected; ingest just had the longest continuous uptime and crashed first.

## Fix

`init: true` on the `x-backend` / `x-frontend` / `x-ingest` compose templates → Docker runs its bundled **tini** as PID 1, which reaps the orphaned `ssl_client` processes. tini needs no capability, is compatible with `no-new-privileges` + `cap_drop:[ALL]`, and still `exec`s the JVM and forwards signals (graceful shutdown / `stop_grace_period` unchanged). Keycloak (bash `/dev/tcp`), Postgres (`pg_isready`) and Redis (`redis-cli`) fork no TLS helper and are unaffected.

## Changes

- `docker-compose.yml` — `init: true` on the three JVM app templates (+ rationale comment)
- `docs/specs/deployment-delivery.md` — new **REQ-OPS-019** (PID-1 zombie reaping)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — Unreleased/Fixed entry

## Verification

- `docker compose config` validates (anchors/merge OK).
- Post-deploy: `docker exec ingest sh -c 'cat /proc/1/comm'` reads `tini`, and the `(ssl_client) Z` count stays flat instead of climbing.

## Reviewer notes

- Reaches prod via the config-bundle promotion (REQ-OPS-004); `deploy.sh` recreates the app containers on the config-digest change. Not a `networks:`/stateful-infra change, so it is an ordinary rolling apply.
- No ADR (standard reaper, not architecturally significant); no unit test (compose invariants follow the REQ-OPS-014 file+review precedent).
- **Follow-up (separate):** this incident was invisible to every pre-crash alert because `JvmThreadsHigh` only counts JVM threads. A `ContainerPidsHigh` cgroup-pids alert (needs cAdvisor `process` metrics enabled) is tracked separately.

author: itsyoga
body:
Implements the approved change `add-apfs-backend` (archived), with the four review corrections applied verbatim to the spec before implementation.

## What ships

- **`backend/apfs.rs`** — `clonefile(2)` snapshot at run, command against the real tree, pruned two-way stat-walk diff (porcelain **bytes unchanged**), O(1) commit. All rootless.
- **Parent-anchored undo, three explicit branches** (safety spec, flagged section): parent verified by dev/ino + canonical target path; then (a) target exists & not a symlink → atomic `RENAME_SWAP` (a replaced target is just another command change — restored normally); (b) target deleted → rename-into-parent; (c) target is a symlink → refuse. A restored-marker makes a crash between swap and cleanup unable to re-swap the damage back.
- **Session lookup `$PWD` fallback** — found during testing: with cwd-keyed lookup, branches (b)/(c) were unreachable (getcwd fails in a deleted cwd). Lookup now falls back to the shell's logical `$PWD`; spec'd (`session`: "Session lookup by logical path fallback").
- **Per-volume state roots** — `<mount>/.oops/state`, registered in an **atomically written** `volumes.json`; containment/gc operate over exactly the registered set; foreign `.oops` dirs never grant deletion rights; unmounted volumes skipped.
- **Triple-gated destructive tests** — explicit `XDG_STATE_HOME` override + self-created tempdirs + `OOPS_TEST_DESTRUCTIVE=1` (set only by `make test-apfs`).
- **README guarantee matrix** — interception vs snapshot-restore side by side, incl. the cloud-sync propagation warning and the mtime-heuristic gap.

## Verification

- macOS host: 12 integration scenarios green, incl. all three restore branches, parent-identity refusal, stale-snapshot refusal, fail-closed on unusable state root; byte-identical restores verified by tree manifests.
- `make bench-apfs`: **undo 6ms** on a 10k-file tree (target < 100ms).

body: ## Goal Make TradeSim more profit-oriented: fewer bad trades, smarter strategy switches, portfolio-level risk control. ## What's new in v26 ### Strategy selection (biggest lever) - **Backtest gate** — auto-tactics and trader-copy only switch if proposed strategy beats current on last ~200 candles by `AUTO_TACTICS_BACKTEST_MIN_EDGE` pp vs hold - Connects the existing backtest module to live decisions (was UI-only before) ### Entry quality - **Regime filter** — blocks DCA/Grid/RSI buys in bear market (below SMA + falling momentum) - **RSI** — computed from 1m candle closes, not every tick - **Scalper** — TP from entry price; minimum edge covers fees+slippage ### Risk management - **Portfolio drawdown halt** at `PORTFOLIO_MAX_DRAWDOWN_PCT` (default 12%): brain emergency halt + blocks new buys via `risk_gate` - **Strategy-aware brain** — pause/reduce/halt adjusts grid/momentum/scalper params, not only DCA ### Learning stability - Optimizer min trades: 5 (was 2) - Shadow Lab: eval every 5 min, promote after 8 trades; clones **not** reset on tactic switch ### Ops - No duplicate per-market REST poll when FeedHub multiplex is active - Mirror sync includes fees; paper→exchange errors shown in UI toast - LIVE/DEMO feed indicator in header ## Config (.env) ``` AUTO_TACTICS_BACKTEST_ENABLED=true AUTO_TACTICS_BACKTEST_MIN_EDGE=0.5 PORTFOLIO_MAX_DRAWDOWN_PCT=12 REGIME_FILTER_ENABLED=true SHADOW_MIN_TRADES_PROMOTE=8 ``` ## Tests 71 passing (8 new v26 tests) ## Upgrade (Windows) ```powershell git pull origin cursor/tradesim-v26-profit-2631 python main.py # Ctrl+Shift+R in browser → v26 Profit badge ```

author: imzodev
body:
## Summary

Fixes the mobile-only bug where the sticky header (with the hamburger menu) scrolls out of view when a chat auto-scrolls to the latest message.

## Root cause

ChatView used bottomRef.scrollIntoView() for the auto-scroll effect. scrollIntoView walks up the ancestor chain looking for a scrollable container. On mobile, the chat container (flex-1 overflow-y-auto) is nested inside <main class=overflow-hidden>. The browser falls back to scrolling the document, dragging the sticky header (which lives outside the chat container) off-screen.

## Fix

Replace both scrollIntoView calls with explicit scrollContainerRef.scrollTo(...). Only scrolls the chat container — no ancestor walking, no document fallback, no header drag.

## Tests

New tests assert scrollTo is called on the chat container and scrollIntoView is never called. setup.test.ts mocks Element.prototype.scrollTo for jsdom.

- ChatView.test.tsx: 9/9 (was 7/7)
- Full web suite: 356 passed, 3 skipped

## Manual verification

Bug only reproduces on mobile. Please confirm in Chrome DevTools device toolbar (≤ 768px):

1. Open chat, select a session from sidebar.
2. Chat scrolls to latest message AND header stays visible.

Before: header disappears. After: header stays put.

author: jimeh
body:
## Summary

Configured command working directories are validated while building the action
plan, but file operations run before commands and can change the live path. A
symlink operation could therefore turn a previously missing in-worktree cwd into
a link to the root checkout and let the command run outside the worktree.

This change:

- re-resolves each command cwd and the worktree boundary immediately before
  spawning the process
- rejects live cwd escapes through the existing command-start failure path,
  preserving `allow_failure` behavior
- shares component-safe boundary checks between planning and execution
- makes force replacement select Windows' directory removal API for directory
  symlinks, so the portable regression reaches command enforcement without
  modifying the linked directory target
- adds focused core coverage and a real linked-worktree regression for the
  symlink escape
- clarifies the runtime contract and updates the spec version to 1.15.1

This remains a trusted-config bootstrap tool, not a process sandbox; the check is
performed as late as the portable process API permits.

## Testing

- `mise run check`
- focused core and linked-worktree CLI regressions
- Windows cross-target `treeboot-core` compile check
- `mise run coverage:missing` (99.84% line coverage in `commands.rs`; 92.92%
  workspace line coverage)

body:
Two problems — **one of them introduced by the previous change.**

## 1. Wrong lyrics (my bug, from #18)

The variant search interleaved duration-free attempts with duration-checked ones:

```
raw title    + duration      <- verified
raw title    + no duration   <- unconstrained, on a MESSY title
cleaned title + duration     <- verified, but never reached
```

So an unconstrained match on a raw, messy title could beat a duration-verified match on a tidied one. And an unconstrained match is only as good as the title it was handed.

**Every duration-checked attempt now runs before any unconstrained one.** A duration hit is the same recording, and it is always preferred.

## 2. Lyrics running ahead — the official-video intro

Providers only accept a duration match within **±2 seconds**. An official video with a long intro is never within 2s of its own recording, so it falls through to the **album cut** — whose lyrics are *correct* but timed from where the album track starts, i.e. **after the video's intro**. The lyrics then run ahead by roughly the intro length, for the entire song.

LrcLib knows the duration of the recording it matched — it simply was never asked. Now it reports it, we compare it with what is playing, and when the difference is real we offer it as a correction in the sync controls:

```
[-0.5s]  [0.0s]  [+0.5s]  [Align -18.0s]
```

**Offered, not applied.** The extra runtime is only *probably* an intro — it could be an outro, and shifting the lyrics would then make them worse. So the ear decides.

The button appears only when the gap is ≥ 4s **and** the track has no offset of its own, so a song already in sync, or already nudged by hand, is left alone.

## Verified

Across the same twelve library tracks, every match now lines up within a second — so nothing is offered where nothing is wrong:

```
Naresauna maya      video=174s lyrics=174s  in sync
The Box             video=197s lyrics=197s  in sync
Self Aware          video=181s lyrics=180s  in sync
Nepali Ho by 1974 AD video=334s lyrics=333s in sync
```

The drift only fires on **official video** uploads, which is precisely the reported case.

**Known limitation:** KuGou does not report a duration, so no correction can be offered for lyrics that come from it.

body:
## What

Adds a `go-activity` capability that reports **what the spec-kitty-go binary did** during agent sessions, read from Claude Code / OpenCode / Codex transcripts.

The stock pipeline is shaped for the Python Spec Kitty surface and its typed channel dispatch drops the Claude Code `type:"attachment"` hook events that carry spec-kitty-go's governance verdicts. This reads them first-class:

- **Governance decisions** — `ADMIT`/`DENY`/`DECISION_REQUIRED`/`ERROR` verdicts, per the exact `spec-kitty hook run` contract (stdout token authoritative; exit 0/1/3, 2=usage), with DENY/DECISION **reasons** extracted.
- **Governed-action correlation** — each verdict linked via `toolUseID` to the exact tool call it gated.
- **Pre/Post pairing**, **hook-hot-path latency** (min/p50/p95/max), and **derived ledger accounting** (admission-decision appends per the hook contract; ledger.db is out-of-band).
- **Direct go-verb usage** (`hook/review/space/ledger/seal/governance/config` + `witness-sidecar`), attributed conservatively vs the Python CLI that shares the `spec-kitty` binary name.

## Surfaces

- `spec-kitty-analyzer go-activity [paths|--mission|--recent]` (human + `--json`)
- `query --include go` adds a `spec_kitty_go` section; `analyze` prints a one-line governance summary.

## Tests

New `internal/gogov` package with unit coverage (verdict contract incl. exit-code fallback, deny/decision reasons, toolUseID correlation, Pre/Post pairing, ledger accounting, CLI verb gating) + a query-section test. Full suite + `go vet` green. Verified against a real dogfood session (3 governed PreToolUse hooks, all ADMIT, 37–49ms).

## Status

Experimental branch dedicated to spec-kitty-go analysis. **Merge at maintainer discretion** — opened for visibility/review, not necessarily immediate merge.

author: sras2024
body:
…andons + three misreporting ratings

The audit's Recommended Repairs page showed Fetcher FAIL, Checklist + citation bridge FAIL, Repair orchestrator FAIL, and Strict QA + Monthly report WARN. Root-caused each; most were diagnostic-semantics bugs (the rating measured the wrong thing) plus one genuine behavioural dead-end.

Repair orchestrator (FAIL — genuine):
- EXTRACT_FAILED plans re-extract the SAME stored read, which is deterministic: a field missing once is missing every attempt. The handler used to return ok:false and retry, burning all maxAttempts and ABANDONING — the dominant driver of the FAIL. It now resolves such a plan terminally in ONE attempt: reject the stuck artifact so it leaves the funnel (covering host-scoped plans whose artifact previously lingered at EXTRACTED forever) and defer the alternate source to discovery. Curated-built types (GUIDE / MARIAN_TITLE) short-circuit like PARISH.
- filePlan no longer re-files a (kind, failedEntity) that ABANDONED within a 7-day cooldown, so a proven dead-end can't re-flood the rolling window with fresh maxAttempts cycles.

Fetcher (FAIL — diagnostic semantics): the rate counted benign policy rejections (unapproved host, login wall, binary/PDF, JS-only shell the dynamic fetcher couldn't render) as transport failures, so it read red whenever discovery surfaced off-registry/dynamic candidates. It now measures transport health — genuine network/HTTP/timeout failures on approved hosts only; policy rejections (the fetcher correctly refusing junk) are excluded from the denominator.

Checklist + citation bridge (FAIL — diagnostic semantics): was bridged / ALL-artifacts-ever, so historical REJECTED junk pinned it red forever. Now backlog-based: the only artifacts the bridge still owes are those at CHECKLIST_READY with no checklistItemId; an empty backlog is caught-up (pass), a growing one is a genuine stall.

Strict QA (WARN — diagnostic semantics): an artifact QA correctly caught as junk and then terminally REJECTED is QA working, so it is excluded from the pass-rate denominator rather than counted as a QA failure; small windows no longer hard-fail. The remaining honest signal (viable artifacts genuinely awaiting repair) now clears as the fixed repair orchestrator resolves them.

Monthly report (WARN): already fixed (recurring check + missed-month catch-up); the marker is simply absent until the now-alive worker runs a pass, at which point June's report catches up and the rating clears. No code change needed.

Tests: 10 new (EXTRACT_FAILED terminal resolution incl. curated short-circuit; filePlan abandon cooldown; and the three rating fixes driven through the public runAdminWorkerDiagnostics with a where-aware mock, each proving the old FAIL/WARN input now reads correctly). Full suite 2880 passed, 1 skipped; typecheck, lint, prettier, production build clean.

author: fhwang
body:
## Summary

Narrative (`clinical-pdf`) ingestion now **requires** LLM extraction. If the analysis cannot be derived — for any reason — the ingest fails with nothing persisted:

- **Missing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`** fails immediately with a new `Error::ExtractorNotConfigured` whose message names the fix ("set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY on the server and re-run the ingest").
- **LLM outage** behaves as before: 3 bounded in-band retries, then the ingest fails.

The text-only degradation path (`extraction_status: "skipped_no_extractor"`) is removed. In practice the in-band status was too easy to miss: a server missing the key silently ingested half-indexed documents — searchable text but no codings, no title, no date — and only an attentive interactive caller would notice. One rule is simpler and safer.

Removing the degraded path also deletes the special-case "preserve prior verified state on degraded re-ingest" branch — a failed ingest never touches the index, so prior state is safe by construction.

Unchanged:

- Total *verification* failure still applies as an empty extraction (`"applied"`, zero codings, reasons in `rejected`).
- `rebuild_index` still replays both stores keyless — existing text-only documents ingested before this change survive rebuilds, and re-ingesting them once a key is configured upgrades them in place.

## Holdout revision (signed bless commit)

The blessed `degraded_reingest_preserves_verified_extraction` contract froze the old text-only behavior and is replaced by two stronger contracts:

- `keyless_ingest_fails_cleanly_with_nothing_persisted` — the error names the missing key; zero FTS hits; `rebuild_index` finds nothing archived.
- `keyless_reingest_fails_and_preserves_verified_extraction` — a keyless re-ingest of already-indexed bytes fails, and all prior codings, title, and date survive intact.

## Test plan

- [x] TDD: new core + server tests written first and watched fail against the old behavior
- [x] `just check` green (fmt, clippy, tests, sqlx offline check, deny, machete, holdout-verify post-bless)
- [x] Full holdout suite passes, including the mock-LLM narrative contracts

author: farkasmark
body:
Closes #50. The per-flavor platform libs (`hull build --flavor`) had no SBOM of their own — only `hull.sbom` (full) and `libhull.sbom` (no-runtime) shipped. This adds the SBOM analogue of `hull build --flavor`.

## What's here

- **`hull sbom --flavor=<full|server-only|client-only|pure-compute>`** — reports the dependency set that flavor's platform lib links, generated from any (full) hull binary (no per-flavor hull build needed — same mechanism as `--subject=libhull`). A new `needs_http` flag on `HlSbomEntry` marks Keel + mbedTLS; `pure-compute` drops them (`HL_ENABLE_HTTP=0` unlinks both). Subject renamed `hull (<flavor>)`, binary hash omitted (the SBOM describes a flavor lib, not the running binary). `full` / `server-only` / `client-only` link the same vendored set as the binary.
- **`release.yml`** generates `libhull_platform-<flavor>.sbom.{json,cdx,spdx}` for the three published flavors and folds them into the Ed25519-signed `hull.sha256`, so a `hull platform install <flavor>` consumer gets a signed bill of materials for the lib they linked.
- **`test_sbom`** — `needs_http` flags match policy; unknown flavor rejected; pure-compute drops the HTTP deps + renames subject + shrinks the set.
- README note under Build Flavors.

## Validation

- `make test` 51/0 (`test_sbom` 24/24, incl. 3 new).
- scan-build clean on the `--flavor` parsing.
- All formats scope correctly; **default output unchanged**; `release.yml` valid YAML.

## Notes

- The **release.yml half is untestable locally** (tag-only); the `--flavor` filter itself is fully validated + unit-tested.
- **Narrowness (documented):** only `pure-compute` actually differs at the vendored-dependency level; `server-only`/`client-only` equal the full set (they differ in which cap *code* compiles, not which vendored lib). The three per-flavor SBOMs are published for symmetry so every `hull platform install <flavor>` has a named, signed SBOM.

author: moshgrossman
body:
## Summary

Field report: setup tried to re-download Python even though 3.13.1 was already installed. `Get-Python` probed candidates with `2>$null`, but under Windows PowerShell 5.1 with `$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'`, redirecting a native command's stderr converts any stderr text into a terminating error — so the probe could throw, get swallowed by its `catch`, and report an installed Python as missing.

## Changes

- Probe candidate interpreters without stderr redirection; judge success by exit code (a failing candidate's stderr just prints)
- Probe the `py` launcher, `python` on PATH, **and** the standard install directories (`Program Files\Python3*`, `LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Python\Python3*`) directly, in case the console's PATH is stale
- Print what was probed and why each candidate was rejected, so future field reports are self-diagnosing

## Test plan

- [x] Parse-checked with pwsh 7.4.17: 0 errors, including under a simulated CP-1252 misread
- [x] Probe helper exercised against a real interpreter (returns its `sys.executable`), a failing executable (returns null, no throw), and a missing path (returns null, no throw)
- [ ] End-to-end on the Windows machine — this unblocks that run

## Security implications

None — detection logic only; no new inputs or subprocess shapes.

## Database changes

- [x] No schema changes

## Documentation

- [ ] No doc changes needed

Follow-up to #2 and #3.

body:
## Summary

The deep review found three schema↔runtime parity gaps with no guarding test — a future refactor could silently re-introduce the dead-ref class the arc's drift-guards exist to prevent:

- **Nested `labels[].color` now drift-guarded.** The GitPr guard iterated `pullRequests[]` item keys but only spot-checked `labels[0].name`; `labels[].color` had no parity check. The nested `labels[]` item shape is now run through the same "every declared key is a real emitted key" assertion, so a `LabelRef` rename can't leave a schema-declared `labels[].color` resolving to null.
- **`x-dynamic-output` hint now guarded.** It had no test at all — renaming an output key while leaving the hint (or vice-versa) would ship green and make every drilled `body.*` / `json.*` path resolve to null. A new contract test asserts every `x-dynamic-output` hint (HTTP `body`, LLM `json`) names a **real declared output property** (pairs with each node's own output test, which pins the runtime key).
- **`acceptance.kind` enum completeness.** It listed 4 of the built graders; `CitationsResolve` is a real, authorable kind (`CitationsResolveGrader` ships, `PlannerSchema` permits it) that was missing, so the picker didn't offer it as a suggested value. Added to both plan nodes. `DiffMatch` stays omitted as genuinely unbuilt.

author: naxy9
body:
## What

A late (<24h) student cancellation under a partial-refund policy now captures the
retained part of the hold for the tutor and lets the provider release the rest to the
student in the same partial capture. Previously this branch was a no-op and left the
hold in place.

## How

`request_partial_capture` mirrors the completion capture flow (`request_capture`):

- `reconcile_booking_payment`'s partial branch pins the retained amount
  (`amount − refund`) from the policy's refund and enqueues the provider call after
  commit, like every other provider call.
- The `capture_partial_payment` Celery task settles a still-held payment whose booking
  the student cancelled: `provider.capture(amount=retained)` captures the retained part
  and releases the remainder in one call, then `capture_and_credit` (reused unchanged)
  credits the tutor exactly once.
- Guards mirror the full capture: still `held`, booking `cancelled_by_student`, provider
  id present. The shared `capture-{id}` idempotency key cannot collide — a booking is
  either completed or cancelled, never both.

## Tests

Rewrote the boundary test (now asserts capture + tutor credit) and added coverage for a
0% policy (full capture, nothing released), idempotency, the booking-status guard, a
missing provider id, provider-failure propagation, and the string→Decimal task boundary.

Full suite: 356 passed, 16 skipped (PostgreSQL-only, run in CI). ruff + black clean, no
migrations.

## Known follow-up

The retained amount is carried only in the Celery message, not persisted — if the broker
drops it, the hold is stranded in `held` with no way to recover the penalty (the payment
amount holds the full price, and the cancellation policy must not be recomputed). Flagged
with a `FIXME` in `reconcile_booking_payment`; to be closed by a separate change that
persists the retained amount alongside the cancellation.
