author: neweustrategies
body:
## Cel

Przebudowa systemu liczenia czasu czytania wpisu od zera: parametryzowany algorytm liczący **PL i EN symultanicznie (niezależnie, z własnych treści)**, panel ustawień w adminie z sekcją super-admina, i pełna synchronizacja z widokiem publicznym — to, co ustawione w panelu, natychmiast rzutuje na wpisy.

Jeden commit ponad `main` (gałąź przestawiona na świeży main po scaleniu #9). Bramki po rebase: tsc bez nowych błędów, **pełny vitest 1431 przechodzi / 5 pominiętych**, lint 0 błędów.

## Algorytm (`src/lib/readingTime.ts`)

```
minuty = słowa/wpm(język) + obrazy(krzywa head/tail) + kod/(wpm × mnożnik)
```

- **PL i EN liczone niezależnie** — każda wersja językowa z własnej treści (`content_pl`/`content_en` + bloki/builder + excerpt) i własnego wpm (domyślnie 220/238),
- krzywa obrazów à la Medium (pierwsze N × head-sekundy, kolejne × tail), bloki `<pre>/<code>` czytane wolniej (mnożnik),
- konfigurowalne **minimum** i **tryb zaokrąglania** (round/ceil/floor),
- `computeBilingualReadingStats()` — wynik PL+EN naraz (podglądy),
- `resolveReadMinutes()` — semantyka publiczna: globalny włącznik → ręczne `posts.read_minutes` jako **override redakcji** (puste = automat) → automat; brak treści → brak etykiety,
- ustawienia w `site_settings["reading_time"]` (zod, walidacja zakresów); `estimateReadingMinutes` zachowany jako zgodny wrapper.

## Panel `/admin/reading-time`

- **admin:** włącznik globalny, wpm PL / wpm EN, minimum minut, tryb zaokrąglania, reset do domyślnych;
- **super admin:** dodatkowo parametry zaawansowane (sekundy na obraz head/tail, próg N, mnożnik kodu) — sekcja niewidoczna dla zwykłego admina;
- **podgląd na żywo PL i EN symultanicznie** liczony na niezapisanym drafcie (edytowalne próbki treści PL/EN + liczba obrazów), z składem wyniku (minuty + liczba słów);
- zapis waliduje schemat i **inwaliduje zbiorczy cache `site_settings`** — publiczny widok przelicza się bez przeładowania;
- pozycja w nawigacji AdminShell (sekcja wyglądu/treści) i w palecie ⌘K.

## Synchronizacja z widokiem publicznym (jedno źródło prawdy)

- `$.tsx` liczy `readMinutes` **raz** (treść aktywnego języka + ustawienia + override) i podaje do: meta przy tytule (`PostOverlayMeta`), paska quick-view, widżetu odsłuchu **oraz JSON-LD/SEO** (`readingTimeMin`). Dotąd UI pokazywało surowe `read_minutes` z DB, a SEO liczyło osobno hardkodem — wartości mogły się rozjeżdżać.
- Blok builderowy `reading-time` (`PostUtilityViews`) przechodzi z hardkodu `wpm=220` na ustawienia; jawne `wpm` ustawione na bloku w CMS pozostaje override'em pojedynczego widgetu; `enabled=false` chowa blok.
- **Edytor postów:** pole `read_minutes` z placeholderem „auto" i hintem **„Auto: PL X min · EN Y min"** liczonym na żywo z treści formularza tym samym rdzeniem — redaktor widzi obie wersje, zanim zdecyduje się nadpisać.

## Testy

16 nowych przypadków rdzenia: wpm per język (symultanicznie), tryby zaokrąglania, minimum, krzywa obrazów (HTML + doc), mnożnik kodu, override redakcji, `enabled=false`, walidacja schematu.

## Uwaga techniczna

`routeTree.gen.ts` zaktualizowany ręcznie w formacie generatora (w tym środowisku vite nie startuje — prywatne pakiety `@lovable.dev` są niedostępne); pierwszy lokalny `dev`/`build` zweryfikuje/przepisze go automatycznie.

author: mairat
body:
Advances the DOM/CSS promotion backlog ([`htmlbridge-remaining-work-roadmap.md`](docs/roadmap/htmlbridge-remaining-work-roadmap.md) §2) with three independent, `Broiler.Cli.Tests`-verified slices, plus roadmap-accuracy fixes.

**Submodule:** bumps the `Broiler.CSS` pointer to Broiler-Platform/Broiler.CSS#21 (the `GetSparseComputedStyle` + `CssStyleScopeBuilder` commit). That PR must merge (or the pointer be re-bumped to its merged SHA) for CI to build — the bridge changes here consume those new APIs.

## What changed

### 2.1 — additive canonical sparse computed-style projection
The submodule adds `CssStyleEngine.GetSparseComputedStyle`: the computed-style pipeline **without** the initial-value backfill, so an undeclared non-inherited property reads back absent — the null-for-undeclared contract the bridge's `GetComputedProps` consumers rely on. Here (main-repo): two internal `*ForParity` accessors + a **differential parity test** that measures how faithfully the canonical projection reproduces `GetComputedProps` and pins the reconciliation delta to four documented classes. Purely additive — **no call-site changes**.

The literal ~98-site `GetComputedProps → GetSparseComputedStyle` cutover was **attempted and confirmed NOT a clean drop-in** — delegating produced 4 regressions (zoom-serialization of inherited/scroll-margin props + two `scrollIntoView` cases), exactly the predicted inheritance/value-resolution delta — so it was reverted and remains deferred behind the WPT gate (documented in §2.1).

### P2 — stylesheet scope assembly via `CssStyleScopeBuilder`
Routes `DomBridge.GetSyncedScopedEngine` through the new canonical `CssStyleScopeBuilder` (submodule). Beyond the promotion, this **fixes a real bug**: the old path concatenated every collected `<style>`/`<link>` sheet into one blob and applied it unconditionally, ignoring per-element `media` — so `<style media="print">` wrongly took effect on screen. The builder gates each source on its media attribute, preserves origin/document order, and parses each source as its own sheet. Pinned by `StyleScopeMediaTests`.

### 2.3 — live per-property `CSSStyleDeclaration` setter validation
The per-property setters (`el.style.X = …`, `setProperty(…)`, the rule-side twins) wrote raw values with **no validation**, while the attribute/`cssText` path already dropped invalid declarations via the shared `CssDeclarationValidator`. So `el.style.color = "bogus"` *stored* the invalid value. All six setter sites now gate through a shared `DomBridge.IsAcceptableInlineValue` helper: invalid values are ignored (prior value kept), matching the attribute path and CSSOM error handling; custom (`--*`) and unknown properties still pass; `!important` is validated on the stripped value. 10 `CssStyleDeclarationValidationTests`.

### Docs
Updates the five htmlbridge roadmap docs — records the three slices, and corrects stale "not merged" language in four docs now that the facade-removal stack (#1359) merged to `main`.

## Reviewer notes
- **Behavior changes** (P2 media gating, 2.3 invalid-value rejection) are spec-aligned but observable; they additionally want the **full WPT css/cssom + Acid + pixel** gate at merge.
- Nuance found in 2.3: the IDL `SetValue` stores the value in two places (ERS map + a JS property the getter reads first), so the gate returns early on invalid to skip `base.SetValue`; `el.style.cssFloat=` is a pre-existing dead path (defensive gate only).

## Verification
Regression-free across the CSS.Dom, CSSOM, computed-style, inline-style, scope, and Acid3 clusters; all residual failures confirmed **pre-existing at clean HEAD** (`:root`/`:lang`, HttpClient reflection, Acid3 render/score/image environmental, `Border_Shorthand`, the zoom-serialization environmental trio).

First of the seven PRs in [`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-11-starter-hardening-design.md`](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-11-starter-hardening-design.md).

A 6-agent audit of *"what breaks when you start a **new** product from this starter"* found ~25 issues that collapse into **three root causes** — each a **missing gate**, not a missing fix:

1. **The reverse direction is never exercised.** The repo is only ever dogfooded `apps/web → packages/*` (extraction). Nobody has run it backwards (scaffold → remove → deploy).
2. **Fail-open defaults** — "if you don't know about it, it passes."
3. **Doc drift has no gate.**

So the governing principle here is **Fix + Gate**: no fix lands without an automated check that fails if it regresses, and **every new gate was proven to go RED** before it was accepted.

## What was broken, and what now catches it

| Fix | Gate |
| --- | --- |
| `engines.node` said `>=20`, but `packageManager: pnpm@11.3.0` needs `>=22.13`. CI already excluded Node 20 *and its comment said why* — nothing propagated that to the manifests, **including the one published to npm**. | New `scripts/repo-invariants.test.mjs` derives the floor from the pinned pnpm major and cross-checks the CLI manifest + the CI matrix. |
| The app generator pinned TypeScript `5.9.2` (workspace: `6.0.3`); `packages/eslint-config` alone floated on a caret — and typescript-eslint caps support at `<6.1.0`, so the next TS minor would have silently pushed it onto an unsupported compiler. | Same suite, generalized: walks **every** workspace and **every** generator template. |
| The Dockerfile copied **16 of 21** workspace manifests, so `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` could not resolve the graph — **the image did not build at all**. It rotted for three weeks because CI never built it (`docker` appeared 0 times under `.github/`). | Static manifest diff (deps-stage-scoped, comment- and destination-aware) **+ a `docker` job that builds the image, runs it, and curls `/api/health`** — the `runner` stage is now exercised too, not just `deps`/`builder`. |
| **Generated PWA apps were dead HTML in production.** The generator's root layout was sync → static prerender → **no CSP nonce** → the app's own `'strict-dynamic'` blocked all 13 of its scripts → zero hydration. `pnpm dev` hid it completely; only a production build showed it. Both real apps already had the fix — only the template drifted. | `scaffold-smoke` job: scaffolds **both** variants (PWA **and** the default non-PWA), runs `check-types`/`lint`/`build` on each, and asserts every `<script>` in the PWA build carries the nonce. Measured: **13/13 un-nonced → 0/12**. |
| `isDistributedRateLimitEnabled()` — the exact detector for the serverless rate-limit hole — was defined, exported, and **never called**. The in-memory limiter is per-instance, so the effective limit is `limit × instances`, and the instance count *grows with the attack*. | Unit tests: warns once, production only. Wired at the `createRateLimiter` factory, so all 7 call sites across both apps are covered. |
| `@repo/ui` declared a `hooks` alias it never exported — `shadcn add sidebar` would die on `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`. And shadcn switched its default primitive to **Base UI** in July 2026, so the bare `shadcn add` this package's own rules prescribed would mix Base UI into a Radix system. | Contract test probing **Node's real resolver** (`import.meta.resolve`), both bare and one-segment-deeper. `-b radix` is now mandatory in `packages/ui/CLAUDE.md`. |
| The dev CSP emitted a nonce **and** `'unsafe-inline'` on `style-src`. Per spec, a nonce makes the browser **ignore** `'unsafe-inline'` — so the relaxation was a no-op and the dev console took ~56 violations per page load. The code comment already conceded it was "contradictory". | `csp.test.ts` pins **both** modes by exact directive equality (the first attempt at this guard was illusory — it only rejected one token order — and was caught in review). **Production is byte-identical**, proven by the zero-violation e2e. |
| `pnpm gen` printed literal Handlebars (`--filter={{ dashCase name }}`); the default port collided with `apps/admin`; and two docs — including `.claude/skills/add-mvp/SKILL.md`, which **an agent executes** — taught a headless form that **hangs without a TTY**. | Messages built from the answers. And `turbo/generators/config.ts` — previously type-checked by **nothing** (no root tsconfig, not a workspace member) — is now in `pnpm check-types`, proven RED under an injected type error. |

## Two gates the PR added against itself

Found by review, after the fixes were already in:

- **`pnpm gen app` would have turned a downstream user's `pnpm test` red** — the new Dockerfile invariant requires a COPY line for every workspace, and a freshly scaffolded app has none. The generator now tells you the exact line to add, and the invariant's failure message prints it verbatim. *(The PR had recreated the very trap it exists to close.)*
- **The invariant suite's own workspace walk was fail-open** — it hardcoded `["apps", "packages"]`, so adding a third glob to `pnpm-workspace.yaml` would have silently un-covered both the Docker and TypeScript gates. Now asserted.

## Verification

Every gate was proven to go **red** against the defect it targets before the fix made it green — including the Dockerfile rule against a commented-out COPY, a COPY in the wrong stage, and a COPY to the wrong destination (all three of which the first version passed).

Local: `lint` 19/19 · `check-types` 19/19 + generator · `build` 3/3 · `test` 17 turbo + 16 node:test · **e2e 56 (web) + 7 (admin) passed**.

> ⚠️ **`docker build` could not be run locally** (no Docker on the dev machine). The new `docker` job is its only proof — **read that job's log before merging.**

author: stephen-nazieh
body:
Fixes the "Book button not fetching" report — both the student flow (already patched by #928's `ENSURE_TABLES_SQL`) and, per follow-up, the **tutor** flow and the underlying migration pipeline.

## 1. Systemic: unfreeze the migration journal (`0069`–`0072`)

**Root cause (proven).** The drizzle journal was frozen at idx `68`, so the deploy's `migrate()` silently ignored `drizzle/0069`–`0072`. Their columns/tables never reached prod, and the booking routes 500 on them: `db.query.oneOnOneBookingRequest.findFirst/findMany` and `.insert().returning()` emit **every** schema column — including `0070`'s `rescheduleProposed*`. I reproduced this against Postgres with the real query builder:

| Query (real route code) | Correct schema | Prod pre-fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| Student status / existing-request check | ✅ | ❌ 500 | ✅ |
| Student create booking (`insert.returning`) | ✅ | ❌ 500 | ✅ |
| **Tutor** received-requests list | ✅ | ❌ 500 | ✅ |

So the tutor's dashboard (incoming requests) was broken by the same cause.

**Fix.** Register `0069`–`0072` in `drizzle/meta/_journal.json` so `migrate()` applies them.

**Verified the exact prod-upgrade path locally** (full schema pushed, `__drizzle_migrations` seeded at `0068`, the post-0068 objects dropped to mimic prod):
- `migrate()` applies **only** `0069`–`0072`, creates every object (4 reschedule cols, `Profile.bufferMinutes`, `OneOnOneReview`, `OneOnOneWaitlist`, all 5 FK constraints), and records them.
- Re-running `migrate()` is a clean **no-op** (idempotent — every `.sql` is `IF NOT EXISTS`).
- Composes safely with #928's `ENSURE_TABLES_SQL` (belt-and-suspenders; both idempotent, order-independent).

Also observed (pre-existing, **not** touched here): the chain fails when run *from scratch* against an empty DB (a legacy migration drops `TutorApplication` before it exists). Prod never runs from scratch — `__drizzle_migrations` sits at `0068` — so this is inert for the deploy. Flagging it as a known issue. Journal only; no snapshot files (runtime `migrate()` doesn't read them).

## 2. UX: hide "Book 1-on-1" for non-students

A tutor/parent/admin viewing a tutor page saw a Book button that could only 403 (`Only students can request…`). Now it's hidden for logged-in non-students, and logged-out visitors are routed to sign in (instead of the misleading "select a time slot" toast).

## Scope / safety
- No money-movement code.
- `tsc` clean, page lint-clean, prettier clean, journal JSON validated.

body:
## 改动内容

本 PR 作为 #131 的总解决 PR，保持 Draft 状态逐步推进，完成后再标记 Ready for Review。

当前已完成：
- [x] 社团注册：新增 `GET /api/clubs/advisor-candidates`，恢复注册申请弹窗“指导老师（可选）”下拉选择，并随申请表提交 `advisorUserId`。
- [x] 社团注册：注册申请 DTO、审核池列表、展开详情和审核弹窗展示拟选指导老师，让申请人与审核人都能确认该信息。
- [x] 社团注册：复用后端现有教师/指导老师判定逻辑，避免候选列表和提交校验口径不一致。
- [x] 社团注册：支持已退回申请修改后重新提交，重交后重新进入待审核并保留上次退回意见。
- [x] 社团注册：管理员审核池支持按社团名/申请人关键字与提交日期范围筛选。
- [x] 我的社团：普通社团档案只展示日常基础信息，注册材料、申请理由和审核意见移入折叠的审批记录。
- [x] 我的社团：修复“我的社团身份”表格操作列被错误限制在成员管理工作台的问题，让查看/退出入口在身份 tab 内可见。
- [x] 成员管理：新增“待分组”快速筛选、待分组统计，并将空部门/小组显示为“待分配”，便于定位招新录取后仍需补分组的成员。
- [x] 成员管理：当前成员列表支持多选后批量设置部门/小组，减少待分组成员逐个维护。
- [x] 成员管理：当前成员列表支持多选后批量设置职务，并将部门/小组/职位缺失统一归为待补资料。
- [x] 成员考核：恢复“奖项分”文案，保持与评奖评优来源同名。
- [x] 数据库样例：新增 `005_sample_member_terms.sql`，为计算机协会、摄影社、羽毛球协会补充当前成员、干部职务和历史任期，并补齐摄影社现任负责人。
- [x] 成员考核：后端按活动签到/签退、项目任务、学习记录、评优评奖记录自动生成参与分、任务分、学习分和奖项分。
- [x] 成员考核：新增 `GET /api/clubs/{clubId}/evaluations/score-preview`，用于保存前预览系统生成分、总分和等级。
- [x] 成员考核：前端考核弹窗将四项分数改为只读展示，负责人和指导老师只需确认并保存公示状态/说明。
- [x] 评奖评优/成员考核：页面补充草稿、确认、公示以及已公示奖项分进入考核的流程说明。
- [x] 本地联调：统一登录/会话/权限检查的可用账号状态口径，`active` 种子账号不再被误判为禁用。
- [x] 本地联调：前端遇到失效 token 的 401 响应时自动清理登录态，并返回登录页，减少停在页面内反复“请求错误”的情况。
- [x] API 契约：已在 rebase 到当前 `dev` 后重新生成并提交前后端 API 代码。
- [x] 冗余清理：移除 `ClubList.vue` 中已被隐藏的旧成员考核 tab、表单、请求和样式，保留独立成员考核页面作为唯一入口。
- [x] 成员考核：新增按学期批量生成考核草稿，当前有效成员可先自动建草稿，已公示记录不会被覆盖。
- [x] 成员考核：负责人和指导老师可在系统生成分基础上微调参与分、任务分、学习分、奖项分，再确认公示。
- [x] 成员考核：考核结果支持按部门、小组、等级筛选，并按总分、分项、成员、学期、记录时间升降序排序。
- [x] CodeRabbit 复查：补齐考核分数字段可空契约、申请筛选参数示例和联系电话字段说明。
- [x] CodeRabbit 复查：批量成员操作支持部分成功提示，失效会话清理去重，申请日期按业务时区过滤。
- [x] CodeRabbit 复查：批量生成考核草稿改为集合化算分查询，减少按成员逐个查询。

后续在本 PR 继续完成：
- [x] 我的社团：继续整理学生、社团负责人、管理员视角入口，减少同一页面多角色混杂带来的困惑。
- [x] 成员管理：继续优化部门/小组/职务维护流程，减少录取后还要重复补资料的手工步骤。
- [x] 评奖评优：继续梳理公示、确认和考核联动，减少同类字段反复维护。
- [x] 成员考核：继续按「生成草稿、人工微调、确认公示、筛选排序」的完整流程优化页面。
- [x] 冗余清理：清理隐藏旧入口、重复按钮/标签、难以理解的状态文案和无效操作入口。

## 改动原因

#131 来自对“我的社团、社团注册、成员管理、评奖评优、成员考核”的真实业务场景走查。当前最明显的回归是：社团注册申请模型与后端逻辑仍保留 `advisorUserId`，但前端申请表单缺少指导老师选择入口，导致学生无法在创建社团时绑定指导老师。本 PR 先恢复该主路径，再逐步补齐整个 Issue 中的体验问题。

---

## 关联 Issue

Closes #131

## 审查关注点

- 指导老师候选接口的登录态、账号状态和教师身份过滤是否符合业务预期。
- 注册申请弹窗、审核池列表、展开详情、审核弹窗中指导老师信息是否形成闭环。
- “我的社团身份”里的查看/退出入口是否符合学生视角直觉，负责人保护是否仍然有效。
- 成员待分组筛选是否能准确覆盖部门或小组缺失的录取成员。
- 成员考核四项分数的自动生成规则是否符合现有业务数据含义。
- 批量生成考核草稿是否只允许系统管理员、社团负责人和指导老师操作，且不会覆盖已公示记录。
- 手动微调分数后，总分和等级是否按保存后的四项分数重新计算。
- 新增成员任期样例是否能支撑真实的负责人、干部、社员、历史换届演示。
- 登录/会话/权限检查对 `active`、`normal`、`enabled` 状态的口径是否符合既有种子数据和业务语义。
- 前端失效 token 自动清理后，是否会正确回到登录页并保留原访问路径。
- API 契约变更后，生成代码由 `gen-api-code.yml` 自动补齐，手写代码不直接修改生成目录。

## UI 改动

| 改动前 | 改动后 |
|--------|--------|
| 社团注册弹窗没有指导老师选择项 | 社团类别后新增可搜索、可清空的“指导老师（可选）”下拉框 |
| 已退回申请只能查看，不能基于原内容修改 | 我的申请列表提供“修改后重交”，表单带回原申请内容和上次退回意见 |
| 审核池只能按状态筛选 | 审核池增加社团名/申请人关键字和提交日期范围筛选 |
| 普通社团档案直接混入申请材料、申请理由和审核意见 | 日常档案只保留基础运营信息，注册审批记录折叠展示 |
| 申请审核时只能看到社团与意见 | 审核池、展开详情、审核弹窗均展示拟选指导老师 |
| “我的社团身份”tab 内看不到操作列 | 身份 tab 内可直接查看成员页或退出当前成员身份 |
| 招新录取后的未分组成员只能显示为 `-` | 成员列表可筛选“待分组”，空部门/小组显示“待分配” |
| 待分组成员需要逐个打开编辑 | 当前成员列表可多选后批量设置部门/小组 |
| 职位缺失成员需要逐个编辑任期 | 当前成员列表可多选后批量设置职务，负责人唯一职务保留逐人确认 |
| 成员考核分数需要负责人逐条录入或确认 | 可按学期批量生成全员草稿，四项分数支持微调、重新生成后再保存公示 |
| 评奖评优和成员考核只显示公示状态按钮 | 页面顶部展示草稿、确认、公示和考核联动流程，表单提示未公示可见范围 |
| 三个重点社团成员样例偏少 | 计算机协会、摄影社、羽毛球协会均补充当前任期和历史任期 |
| 本地重启后旧 token 可能反复触发请求错误 | 401 会清理失效登录态并回到登录页 |
| `ClubList.vue` 保留不可见的旧成员考核实现 | 删除隐藏旧 tab 和旧表单逻辑，成员考核统一从独立页面进入 |
| 考核结果只能按学期、状态和关键词查找 | 支持部门、小组、等级筛选和总分、分项、成员、学期、记录时间升降序排序 |

## 测试说明

当前阶段已验证：
- 已验证 CodeRabbit 评审修复：`python -c "import pathlib,yaml; yaml.safe_load(pathlib.Path('api/openapi.yaml').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))"`、`pnpm.cmd run format:ci`、`pnpm.cmd run build`、`dotnet build backend\ClubHub.Api.csproj --configuration Release --no-restore`、`git diff --check` 均通过；保留既有 `Microsoft.OpenApi` NU1903、生成模型 nullable、`@vueuse/core` Rolldown annotation 和 chunk size warning。
- 已同步当前 `dev` 并解决 PR 分支冲突。
- `dotnet build --configuration Release --no-restore` 通过；保留既有 `Microsoft.OpenApi` NU1903 漏洞警告和生成模型 nullable 警告。
- `dotnet format backend/ClubHub.Api.csproj --verify-no-changes --exclude backend/Models/** --verbosity minimal` 通过。
- `pnpm.cmd run format:ci` 通过。

- `git diff --check` 通过。
- 本地运行态已验证：`http://localhost:5173/` 可访问，`http://localhost:5173/api/health` 通过前端代理返回 healthy。
- 本地联调已验证：`http://localhost:5173/api/auth/login` 使用 `zhao_rui / 123456` 返回 200 且包含 token。
- 已在开发库执行 `database/seeds/005_sample_member_terms.sql`；落库后计算机协会 11 条任期（7 当前、4 历史），摄影社 10 条任期（5 当前、5 历史），羽毛球协会 14 条任期（7 当前、7 历史），摄影社负责人为林可欣。
- rebase 到当前 `dev` 后已重新生成并提交 API 代码同步提交 `49663db`。
- 已验证退回后重交改动：`dotnet build --configuration Release --no-restore`、`dotnet format backend/ClubHub.Api.csproj --verify-no-changes --exclude backend/Models/** --verbosity minimal`、`pnpm.cmd run format:ci`、`pnpm.cmd run build`、`git diff --check` 均通过。
- 已验证审核池筛选改动：`dotnet build --configuration Release --no-restore`、`dotnet format backend/ClubHub.Api.csproj --verify-no-changes --exclude backend/Models/** --verbosity minimal`、`pnpm.cmd run format:ci`、`pnpm.cmd run build`、`git diff --check` 均通过。
- 已验证社团档案展示调整：`pnpm.cmd run format:ci`、`pnpm.cmd run build`、`git diff --check` 均通过。

- 已验证成员考核生成、微调、筛选排序页面改动：`pnpm.cmd run format:ci`、`pnpm.cmd run build`、`git diff --check` 均通过。
- 自动生成 API 代码提交 `82f023f` 已拉回本地；随后复跑 `dotnet build backend\ClubHub.Api.csproj --configuration Release --no-restore`、`pnpm.cmd run format:ci`、`pnpm.cmd run build`、`git diff --check` 均通过。

后续每完成一个阶段，会同步更新本节测试说明和上方进度 checklist。

---

body:
### Motivation
- Provide an authenticated admin UI to manage only the MP3 playlist shown on `medien.html` while preserving the existing hard-coded fallback and player UX.  
- Implement a progressive enhancement so the public site can load a validated `data/media-audio.json` and replace the fallback playlist only on successful validation.  
- Keep filesystem/assets handling conservative: no DB, no external services, protect legacy MP3s and reuse existing auth/CSRF conventions.

### Description
- Added `data/media-audio.json` containing the six migrated tracks with preserved titles, subtitles, durations, seeds, order, stable `id`s and `managedUpload: false`.  
- Created `JS/media-audio-render.js` which fetches `data/media-audio.json`, validates the entire structure and each field, constructs DOM nodes (no `innerHTML`), replaces the playlist only on successful validation, resets the `<audio>` element, dispatches `media-audio:rendered`, and calls `window.AOS.refreshHard()` when available.  
- Updated `JS/media-audio-player.js` to support reinitialization without duplicate handlers using an IIFE-scoped `WeakMap` and `AbortController` per player and listening for `media-audio:rendered`.  
- Extended `admin/media.php` with a German `Audio-Playlist bearbeiten` section that lists existing tracks (title, subtitle, displayed duration, read-only MP3 path, order, remove checkbox and optional `<audio>` preview) and provides an upload subform for new MP3s with German help text.  
- Added `admin/save-media-audio.php` to handle authenticated, CSRF-protected saves: it validates existing JSON, validates posted fields and IDs, enforces at-least-one-track, performs safe MP3 upload to `assets/MP3/medien/` (size limit 25 MB, MIME/type/signature checks), generates safe filenames and stable IDs/seeds for uploads, creates a backup in `data/backups/` before writing, writes JSON atomically with locking, and only deletes previously managed files (in `assets/MP3/medien/`) after successful JSON write.  
- Modified `medien.html` minimally to add the playlist hook `data-media-audio-playlist` to the existing `<ol>` and included `JS/media-audio-render.js` after `JS/media-audio-player.js` while preserving all six hard-coded tracks as fallback.

### Testing
- Ran PHP syntax checks: `php -l admin/save-media-audio.php` (passed) and `php -l admin/media.php` (passed).  
- Checked JavaScript syntax: `node --check JS/media-audio-player.js` (passed) and `node --check JS/media-audio-render.js` (passed).  
- Executed a local `python3` verification script that confirmed the fallback markup still contains 6 `data-media-wave-track` entries, `data/media-audio.json` contains the same 6 tracks with preserved fields and `managedUpload:false`, the six MP3 files exist on disk, the renderer performs safe `replaceChildren` and dispatches `media-audio:rendered`, and the player includes reinitialization hooks and cleanup logic (passed).  
- Not performed here: interactive browser playback tests, authenticated form POST/real multipart uploads, and runtime checks for upload rejection (renamed PHP/non-MP3 files) and managed-file deletion, because those require an HTTP server, browser and authenticated upload actions outside this non-interactive environment.

author: sentry[bot]
body:
This PR addresses ECENCY-NEXT-1GHH, where `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'window.webkit.messageHandlers')` errors were leaking into Sentry.

The root cause was that the existing `beforeSend` filter (added for ECENCY-NEXT-1GE4) to suppress these errors relied on `stackStr.includes("sendDataToNative")`. However, when the code was minified, `sendDataToNative` was renamed (e.g., to `O`), causing the filter to miss these known environment-mismatch errors in non-WKWebView browsers (like Instagram's in-app browser on iOS).

This fix relaxes the `beforeSend` filter in `apps/web/src/utils/sentry-before-send.ts` to suppress any `TypeError` whose message contains `"window.webkit.messageHandlers"`, regardless of the function name in the stack trace. This is safe because any such error is consistently an environment mismatch, not an application bug.

The corresponding tests in `apps/web/src/specs/utils/sentry-before-send.spec.ts` have been updated to reflect this new behavior, including coverage for minified function names.

Fixes [ECENCY-NEXT-1GHH](https://ecency.sentry.io/issues/133720556/?seerDrawer=true)

author: sarthak195
body:
## What

Plug reservations for the first prospective client's use case (a private society/office group sharing one charger): group members book a future `[start_at, end_at)` window on a plug; **during that window only the holder can start a session**; everyone with plug access sees the upcoming schedule. **FREE in v1 — no coin hold**, no money movement anywhere in the lifecycle.

## Backend

- **Model:** `Reservation` + `ReservationStatus` enum (`booked → cancelled | fulfilled | expired`) at the tail of `models.py`. `tenant_id` denormalized plug→gateway→tenant (mirrors `charging_sessions`); nullable `session_id` linked when FULFILLED; composite index `(plug_id, start_at)` + `user_id`/`tenant_id` indexes.
- **Migration:** `backend/migrations/versions/0014_reservations.py`, `down_revision = "0013_auth_holds"`, guarded/idempotent DDL in the 0013/0011 style. ⚠️ **Merge-train note:** other parallel branches are also minting `0014_*` revisions chained on `0013_auth_holds` — this one needs the usual renumber/re-chain at merge time. It only creates the self-contained `reservations` table + `reservation_status` enum, so it is trivially reorderable.
- **Endpoints** (`routers/reservations.py`, registered after the original eight in `main.py`):
  - `POST /api/reservations` — plug access rule (ungrouped ∪ public group ∪ joined private group, extracted to `services/reservations.py user_can_access_plug`), plug not MAINTENANCE (409; OFFLINE stays bookable — liveness still gates at start time), window rules (400), per-user cap (409), `[start,end)` overlap vs BOOKED (409) — cap under a **user-row lock**, overlap under a **plug-row lock** (user→plug order, same as session start, so concurrent bookings serialize). Confirmation notification on success.
  - `GET /api/reservations/my` — `{upcoming, history(≤20)}` with plug names.
  - `POST /api/reservations/{id}/cancel` — owner, or cpo/admin **of the owning tenant** (anyone else 404, existence not leaked); operator cancel notifies the driver.
  - `GET /api/plugs/{plug_id}/reservations` — the schedule (holder names + `is_mine`) for anyone with plug access; lives in `reservations.py` so `plugs.py` only gained the response fields.
  - `GET /api/cpo/reservations` — tenant-scoped list at the tail of `cpo.py` (status/upcoming filters, audit-style pagination). Backend/API only — no CPO-portal page yet.
- **Session-start gate** (inside the plug-locked section of `sessions.py`): **lazy no-show expiry FIRST** (`expire_lapsed_reservations`, shared by the gate, the overlap check, and every list endpoint — an expired hold never blocks anyone with **no background sweep**), then a covering BOOKED window → 409 `"Plug is reserved until <end>"` for a non-holder; the holder's start flips it FULFILLED + links `session_id` in the same commit as the plug claim (and reverts it to BOOKED if the MQTT publish fails).
- **Plug APIs:** `reserved_now`, `reserved_now_by_me`, `reserved_until`, `next_reservation` on detail **and** list — the list batches all plugs into **one grouped query** (endpoint stays N+1-free).

## Policy defaults shipped (env-tunable, `services/reservations.py`)

| Env | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `RESERVATION_MAX_HOURS` | `4` | longest bookable window |
| `RESERVATION_MAX_ADVANCE_DAYS` | `7` | how far ahead a window may start (also the schedule horizon) |
| `MAX_UPCOMING_RESERVATIONS_PER_USER` | `2` | cap of BOOKED-with-future-end per user (409 past it) |
| `RESERVATION_NO_SHOW_GRACE_MIN` | `15` | minutes after `start_at` an unfulfilled hold lazily flips EXPIRED |

Fixed (not env): 15-min minimum duration; 2-min past-start grace so "book starting now" survives submit latency. All env reads use the `or "x"` empty-string guard (the GST_RATE_PCT compose lesson).

## Frontend (driver Home)

- Plug cards: **"Reserved until HH:MM"** badge (viewer-local time, distinct from occupied); the holder sees **"Reserved for you"** and the card stays startable, while a plug inside someone else's window stops inviting the start click.
- **"Reserve"** action per card → `ReserveModal`: date + start time + 30 min/1 h/2 h/4 h presets → `POST /api/reservations` (ISO strings); the plug's upcoming windows are listed in the modal so members book around each other; 409s (slot taken / cap) render inline.
- **"Your reservations"** strip: upcoming bookings with plug name, window, cancel.
- Plain `.jsx` (TD#14), shared `utils/reservationTime.js` for local-time formatting.

## Tests

- Backend: `backend/tests/test_reservations.py` — booking success + tenant denormalization + notification, all five window-rule 400s, +grace acceptance, cap 409 (and cancelled/past rows not counting), overlap 409 in three shapes + back-to-back edges legal, private-group 403 (member OK), MAINTENANCE 409, start-gate 409 for non-holder, holder fulfil + session link, lazy expiry frees the gate (and the overlap check) after grace while still blocking inside it, cancel by owner / tenant CPO (driver notified) / cross-tenant CPO 404 / terminal 409, my-list split, plug schedule (+403), grouped list fields, CPO tenant scoping. DB-gated (skip locally, run in CI). `test_session_start_plug_status.py`'s mocked-execute script gained the gate's two new queries.
- Local runs: backend `205 passed, 105 skipped` (exit 0; skips are the usual no-local-Postgres policy); frontend `85 passed` across 14 files (exit 0); eslint clean on touched files.

## Docs

`docs/API_REFERENCE.md` (new section, plug/session row updates, CPO row, env table), `docs/DATA_MODEL.md` (enum + `reservations` table), `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md` (backend + frontend rows, 2026-07-12), `docs/MARKET_GAP_ANALYSIS.md` §5 "Reserve / book a charger ahead" flipped ✅ — **"Scheduled / delayed start" deliberately stays ❌** (a reservation holds the window; it never switches the plug on).

## Follow-ups (noted, not blocking)

- Optional `SessionReaperService` piggyback: periodic expiry sweep + a "your reservation just started" nudge (lazy expiry already guarantees correctness without it).
- CPO-portal page for `GET /api/cpo/reservations` (endpoint only today).
- v1 doesn't force-stop a walk-up session that's still running when a reserved window begins — the holder sees "in use" until it ends.

author: ayushin
body:
## What this is

The framework DRY refactor: every concept in `angee.base` gets exactly one owner, the remaining ontology proposals (P1–P5) land in their leanest Django-native shapes, and the ratified service-account principal model closes the actor-species question. 17 commits, each gated by independent architecture + Django reviews.

## Base reconciliation (slices 1–4)

- **One impl owner** — `impl_types.py` + `registry.py` + `ImplClassField` merged into `angee.base.impl`; the fields↔impl duck-probe cycle is gone; `AngeeModel.impl_field` is the public seam; the 4× addon resolve ritual deleted.
- **One identity owner** — `SqidField` owns the public-id codec end-to-end (encode + decode + unbound-codec contract); `SqidPublicIdentity` is a thin adapter for models Angee can't put a field on; loose helpers survive only at dynamic-model boundaries, each with a documented why.
- **Declarations in base, interpretation in compose** — the composer walks the declared emission seams generically (pinned by a synthetic-mixin test); `emission.py` stays in base by import-direction law.
- **Fields declare their projection** — `angee_widget`/`angee_scalar_hint`/`angee_currency_field` replace isinstance-probing in core; **`MoneyField` moves home to `angee.money`** (with `RoundingMode` — the addon owns its default mode, uom-sibling precedent); core carries no money knowledge.

## Lean ontology P1–P5 (slices 5–9)

- **P1 — agents are principals**: `Agent.principal_subject()` on `rebac.SubjectRef`; the MCP verifier stops borrowing the credential owner's identity (fail-closed on ambiguity); the `agent` zed relation ships *with* its m2m tuple writer; end-to-end tested through the real verifier.
- **P2 — `RecordRef`**: one contenttypes reference primitive (storage/messaging/workflows/tags adopt; encodes public ids without fetching; scoping-neutral).
- **P3 — declared two-axis state**: `Integration.status` splits into `lifecycle` + `runtime_status` (deterministic data migration, `error → active+error`); `Agent` lifecycle runs on a declared `@transition` graph; `StateTransitions` gains `action_specs`, `force_state`, `not_allowed`; parent-Integration lifecycle control returns as admin action mutations.
- **P4 — catalogue trait**: `catalogue`/`catalogue_tier` class markers + system check + loader tier validation, carried across composer emission (the guard caught real manifest drift on landing).
- **P5 — one change signal**: `change_published` (django.dispatch) with `publish_change` owning the observation decision; GraphQL broadcast and workflow triggers are receivers; publishers wire at app `ready()` (workers publish without schema imports); feed membership is a loud contract (`Trigger.clean` + system check).

## Service-account principals (the layered-principal rule)

Agents act through **non-login rows in the one user table** (`iam.User.kind`, `Agent.user` O2O), so every attribution FK — `created_by`, `history_user`, `Revision.user` — keeps a single vocabulary across actor species, while authorization keeps REBAC species intact. One login-capability predicate gates password auth, session reload, and both OIDC paths; service-user lifecycle rides `post_delete` (cascade/bulk safe). Doctrine in `docs/glossary.md` + `docs/backend/guidelines.md`: *at the database layer only, user = service account = actor = principal — the layers link, never merge.*

## Breaking changes (for consumers)

- `ImplClassField` imports/deconstructs from `angee.base.impl`; `MoneyField` from `angee.money.fields` — committed runtime migrations referencing old dotted paths must be regenerated or path-edited (schema-identical).
- `Integration.status` → `lifecycle` + `runtime_status` (SDL drift on the integration family; data-migration mapping documented in the migration).
- Regenerated example runtime migrations orphan existing dev DBs → backed-up dev-DB reset (see Pitfalls).
- The consumer follow-up is already done for arpee (`ang-ee/arpee-angee` branch `refactor/framework-dry-followup`).

## Hygiene fixed along the way

Pre-existing reds surfaced by the per-slice gates, each fixed at its owner: threaded-record delete cascade authorization (deny-path pinned), stale channel-capabilities assertion, imap import order, the last mypy error, value-field-type registration ordering (consumer-exposed), and `HierarchyMixin.is_within` (restoring a consumer helper at the owning level). ruff and mypy went red-on-main → fully green.

## Verification

Every slice landed with: ruff ✓, `mypy angee addons` ✓ (300 files), full pytest ✓ (1,319 passing, +117 over main), example MCP module ✓, `angee build` byte-identical (except intentional slices), `makemigrations --check` ✓, fresh-DB migrate ✓, `rebac sync --check` ✓, `schema --check` ✓, frontend codegen/typecheck/tests ✓ (two pre-existing failures verified on main and recorded). Live `angee dev` boots the full stack clean end-to-end. Consumer acceptance: arpee `manage.py check` + `angee build` pass against this branch.

Known pre-existing (not addressed here, recorded): `@angee/tags` typecheck (tags not composed into the example), 4 `@angee/app` ResourceList tests (21 failing on main).

author: ezcobar
body:
## Three deploy defects, preview service unreachable

**1 — no gateway route.** `/api/v1/previews/*` had no Kong route, so the viewer could never fetch a thumbnail/page. Added the route to **both** `deploy/gateway/routes.yaml` and `kong.yaml` (auth `required`, same content class as `/api/v1/documents`) so **archtest C1 (the gateway↔kong mirror) passes** rather than being bypassed. The public prefix also matches `/api/v1/previews/internal/*`, so the gateway request-transformer now **strips `X-Service-Key`** — an external caller can't reach the internal stamping endpoints (fail-closed at the preview key check); in-cluster callers hit preview directly, bypassing the gateway.

**2 — S3 creds mis-keyed.** Helm `commonEnv` injected `SEDOC_MINIO_*`, but the Python services read `SEDOC_S3_*` (pydantic `env_prefix=SEDOC_` + `s3_*` fields) — so preview/intelligence booted with a **credential-less boto3 client** in cluster. Canonical is `SEDOC_S3_*` (compose + ansible inject it; Go `pkg/config` binds both but *prefers* S3_*). Changed the chart to emit `SEDOC_S3_*`. Added a Helm golden asserting `SEDOC_S3_*` present / `SEDOC_MINIO_*` absent.

**3 — service key never provisioned.** Neither the preview service (`SEDOC_SERVICE_API_KEY` gates its internal watermark endpoints) nor its document-service caller (`SEDOC_SERVICE_API_KEY` + `SEDOC_PREVIEW_URL` for the `PreviewClient`) had these set — the watermark call was disabled/401. Provisioned both via `commonEnv` (from a secret, optional) + compose; `SEDOC_PREVIEW_URL` points document at the preview API directly.

## Also fixed while wiring the above
- **The Helm chart never rendered at all** — `sedoc.fullname`/`sedoc.name` helpers were referenced by `templates/gateway/*` but undefined. Added the standard definitions (unblocks `helm template`/install *and* the golden).
- **`python-multipart` missing** from preview requirements → the internal `/watermark/pdf` (multipart) endpoint raised `RuntimeError` on every download/print burn-in. Added it.
- **Compose had no preview HTTP container** (only the celery worker), and the worker lacked S3 creds. Added a `preview` uvicorn service (the Kong upstream) + creds; gave the worker its creds.

## Tests (DoD)
- **archtest C1** (both directions) passes with the new route.
- **Helm golden** (`deploy/helm/sedoc/tests/preview-env-golden.sh`): the preview deployment renders `SEDOC_S3_*` + `SEDOC_SERVICE_API_KEY`, no `SEDOC_MINIO_*`.
- **Preview pytest** (`test_internal_watermark_auth.py`, 4/4): internal watermark → 401 without/wrong key, **200 + valid stamped PDF** with the key, fail-closed when the server key is unset.
- **Deploy-shaped smoke** (`scripts/preview-gateway-smoke.sh`): against the compose stack, fetch a preview page **through the gateway** (302 → presigned URL) + the internal watermark path (200 with key / 401 without).
- New CI job `preview-deploy-checks` runs the helm golden + watermark pytest.

## Scope note
The Helm gateway ConfigMap (`templates/gateway/configmap.yaml`) is a pre-existing stub — it mirrors none of the real routes (only a health route). The archtest-governed source of truth is the compose `kong.yaml`/`routes.yaml`, which this PR updates; wiring the full Helm gateway config is a separate, larger defect I've left untouched.

author: iroha924
body:
## Summary

Adds `tests/hooks/session-start-status.bats` — 13 bats cases covering every branch of `hooks/session-start-status.sh`. Test-only; no production code changes.

## Motivation / Context

Closes #159. `hooks/session-start-status.sh` is one of 13 hook handlers shipping without dedicated bats coverage. It is the hook a user meets first — on every `startup` / `resume` it decides whether to inject an `additionalContext` line naming the active feature, its vehicle, its phase, and the next command to run. A silent regression here is invisible in CI and costs the user their orientation at the exact moment they have none.

## Approach

Covered the handler by branch rather than by line, in three groups:

**Silence (nameless-butler stance).** No `.mumei/current`; an empty one; a whitespace-only one; a `.mumei/current` naming a feature with no `state.json` under either vehicle. Each must exit 0 with empty stdout *and* empty stderr.

**The emitted context.** Spec vehicle; plan vehicle; both vehicles present (spec wins — the handler checks `specs/` first, and that precedence was previously unpinned); malformed `state.json` (the `jq ... || echo "unknown"` fallbacks must yield `phase=unknown` / `current_wave=0` rather than a crash or a partial line).

**Next-step hints.** `phase=review` + `pending_review=true` → `/mumei:peruse`; `phase=review` + `pending_review=false` → no hint (the negative case is the one that actually pins the `if`); `phase=done` → `/mumei:shelve <feature>`; an in-progress phase → no hint at all.

Plus the `MUMEI_BYPASS=1` escape hatch, which `_lib/anchor.sh` short-circuits before the handler body runs.

**On helper reuse:** the spec vehicle comes free from `test_helper`'s `_init_feature`. The plan vehicle has no shared helper, and I did not add one to `test_helper.bash` — this is the only hook that branches on vehicle, so a local `_init_plan_feature` in this file is the KISS answer. If a second hook ever needs it, that is the time to promote it.

**Mutation-checked, not just green.** Assertions that pass against a broken handler are worse than no assertions, so I verified detection by mutating the hook and confirming the suite goes red:

| Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Drop the `phase=done` → shelve hint | `not ok 11` |
| Break the `specs/` vehicle branch | `not ok 5, 7, 8, 11` |
| Delete the `[[ -z "$STATE_PATH" ]] && exit 0` guard | `not ok 4` |
| Delete the `[[ -z "$FEATURE" ]] && exit 0` guard | **still green** |

The last row is a real finding, and it is not a hole in the test: with `FEATURE` empty, neither `specs/<empty>/state.json` nor `plans/<empty>/state.json` exists, so the `STATE_PATH` guard already exits 0. That line is defense-in-depth, unobservable from outside the handler. I left it alone — #159 is scoped test-only, and a redundant guard in a hook that must never crash is not worth a production diff.

## Affected components

- [ ] hook (`hooks/*.sh`, `hooks/_lib/*.sh`)
- [ ] agent (`agents/*.md`)
- [ ] skill (`skills/**/SKILL.md`)
- [ ] detector (`hooks/_lib/detectors.sh` / `hooks/pre-review-detector.sh`)
- [ ] plugin manifest (`.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`)
- [ ] CI (`.github/workflows/*`)
- [x] tests (`tests/**/*.bats`)
- [ ] docs (`README*.md`, `PRIVACY.md`, `docs/`)
- [ ] dev-only (`.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md`) — not shipped to plugin users

## Test plan

```sh
bats tests/hooks/session-start-status.bats   # 13/13
task validate                                # lint + full suite: 919 ok, 0 not ok
```

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] **Conventional Commits** subject (`test:`).
- [x] No `Co-Authored-By` trailer.
- [x] Single-line subject; PR body holds the long description (this template).
- [x] `bats -r tests/` passes locally on macOS.
- [x] `task lint` passes locally.
- [x] If the change alters external behavior, network egress, or distribution layout: N/A — test-only, and `tests/` is not in the plugin tarball.
- [x] If the change introduces a new design decision or revises an existing one: the only judgment call (keep `_init_plan_feature` local rather than promoting it into `test_helper.bash`) is recorded under Approach.
- [x] **Ratchet principle**: N/A — no new hook rule, agent, skill, or Hook ID.
- [x] Distributable artifacts stay in **English**.
- [x] No `--no-verify` or `--force` push to `main` is used.
- [x] No secrets, `.env`, credentials, or private keys are added.

## Breaking change?

- [ ] Yes (describe migration above and bump version accordingly)
- [x] No

author: vicentereig
body:
## Summary

- rewrite README, 34 published articles, the external Medium draft, and reader-facing documentation using the project’s economical-writing rubric
- align the documentation with current DSPy.rb APIs and remove stale examples, unsupported benchmarks, obsolete retry behavior, and nonexistent Memory/serializer APIs
- frame DSPy.rb around typed tasks, modules, Ruby programs, bounded agents, tools, evaluation, and optimization
- distinguish deterministic workflows from model-directed agent loops and use `harness` only for concrete runtime responsibilities
- replace the unqualified “Ruby port of Stanford DSPy” claim with a Ruby-native implementation positioning
- repair internal links for the `/dspy.rb` deployment base path and regenerate article OG images

## Positioning

The review reached two bounded conclusions:

1. Workflows, agents, and harnesses are different layers rather than successive generations. Ruby owns deterministic control flow; an agent delegates bounded action choices to a model; the harness is the application-owned runtime envelope around either one.
2. DSPy.rb began as a port but now evolves independently through Sorbet types, Ruby-native provider packages, toolsets, optimizers, persistence, and runtime behavior. The new high-level line is:

> DSPy.rb brings DSPy’s signature, module, agent, and optimizer model to Ruby, with Sorbet types and Ruby-native integrations.

Primary-source research and the adversarial conclusions are recorded in:

- `docs/editorial/dspy-agent-positioning.md`
- `docs/editorial/dspy-port-positioning.md`

## Editorial Method

- section-level McCloskey pass
- whole-document structure and repetition pass
- website voice reference for narrative articles
- technical verification against current code, specs, and git history
- independent adversarial reviews for meaning drift, lost qualifications, generic AI prose, invented aphorisms, and document convergence
- final link, navigation, frontmatter, and generated-site audit

The reusable private `vicente-writing-style` skill was developed and validated separately as part of the tracked epic.

## Verification

- production Bridgetown build passes under Ruby 3.4.5
- all generated internal links resolve under `/dspy.rb`
- `git diff --check` passes
- focused article and API suites passed across the batches, including runs of 386, 191, 165, 161, 133, 117, and 65 examples with zero failures
- Ruby fences, frontmatter, Liquid structure, provider installation paths, navigation, storage, registry, Evals, agent history, and union discriminator examples were checked
- final independent release audit reported no remaining blockers

## Residual Limits

- provider model identifiers were not checked against live provider catalogs
- intentionally partial examples were not all executed against live LLMs
- historical incidents and benchmark observations remain authorial evidence where raw artifacts no longer exist

Closes the editorial epic tracked in Beads as `dspy.rb-8mf`.

author: robobun
body:
## Repro

```js
const CUSTOM = Symbol.for("nodejs.util.inspect.custom");
let calls = 0;
const o = { plain: 1, [CUSTOM]() { calls++; return "HOOK-OUTPUT"; } };

calls = 0; console.dir(o, { customInspect: false });
console.log(calls); // node: 0   bun: 1
calls = 0; console.dir(o);
console.log(calls); // node: 0   bun: 1 (dir defaults customInspect to false in Node)
calls = 0; Bun.inspect(o, { customInspect: false });
console.log(calls); // bun: 1, output is "HOOK-OUTPUT"
```

`customInspect: false` exists so that callers can inspect untrusted values without running their code. Bun's JS-ported `util.inspect` and `new Console(stream).dir` already honor it; only the native formatter (global `console.dir`, `Bun.inspect`) was affected.

## Cause

`FormatOptions` in `src/jsc/ConsoleObject.rs` reads `depth`, `colors`, `sorted`, and `compact` from the options object but never reads `customInspect`. The `Formatter` struct already has a `disable_inspect_custom` flag (used internally to break recursion when a hook returns its own receiver), but nothing wires the user-facing option into it. The top-level `Tag::get` calls in `format2` also run with `TagOptions::empty()`, so the hook lookup always fires regardless of the flag.

The native `console.dir` handler reads `depth`/`colors` from its second argument but not `customInspect`, and does not default it to `false`.

## Fix

- Add `disable_inspect_custom` to `FormatOptions` and parse `customInspect` in `FormatOptions::from_js` (used by `Bun.inspect` / `Bun.inspect.table`).
- Thread it into the `Formatter` in `format2` and pass `TagOptions::DISABLE_INSPECT_CUSTOM` to the top-level `Tag::get_advanced` calls when set. Nested values already consult `formatter.disable_inspect_custom` via `tag_opts()`.
- Make the native `console.dir` default `customInspect` to `false` and read the option from its second argument, matching Node.
- Add `customInspect?: boolean` to `BunInspectOptions`.

## Verification

New `describe("customInspect option")` in `test/js/bun/util/inspect.test.js`:

- `Bun.inspect(o, {customInspect:false})`: hook not called, object rendered normally (top-level and nested).
- `Bun.inspect(o)` / `Bun.inspect(o, {customInspect:true})`: hook called (unchanged default).
- Spawned `console.dir`: default → 0 calls, `{customInspect:false}` → 0 calls, `{customInspect:true}` → 1 call, nested with `false` → 0 calls.

```
USE_SYSTEM_BUN=1 bun test test/js/bun/util/inspect.test.js -t "customInspect option"  → 2 fail, 1 pass
bun bd test test/js/bun/util/inspect.test.js                                          → 76 pass
bun bd test test/js/web/console/console-log.test.ts                                   → 4 pass
bun bd test test/js/node/console/console.test.ts                                      → 7 pass
```

author: k0b3n4irb
body:
Closes #88.

## Problem
`luna-gui` showed a **black screen** for ROMs whose internal checksum is blank/invalid — most of the PeterLemon homebrew test corpus. Layout auto-detection refuses to guess LoROM vs HiROM without a valid checksum (`crates/luna-cartridge/src/lib.rs` — `checksum ^ complement == 0xFFFF`), and the GUI had no override, unlike the CLI's `--force-mapper`.

## What lands
- **luna-api**: `Emulator::load_rom_forced(path, mapper)` — the path-based sibling of `load_rom_bytes_forced` (reads the file, strips a copier header, searches firmware like `load_rom`, forces the mapper). Unit-tested (`load_rom_forced_from_path_bypasses_autodetect`).
- **luna-gui**:
  - On a detection failure, an inline **"couldn't detect the mapper — load as LoROM / HiROM / ExHiROM / SA-1?"** prompt loads the ROM in **one click** (no re-Open) — the pending path is remembered and retried.
  - A **File ▸ Force mapper** submenu pre-sets a sticky default (for opening a whole test corpus), also auto-retrying a pending load.
  - Auto-detect stays the default; a menu-bar hint + `mapper: …` indicator show the state.

## Validation
- Maintainer-validated in the GUI: `WaveHDMA.sfc` (checksum-invalid) → black → prompt → click LoROM → the HDMA wave renders. Cancel dismisses cleanly.
- Full gate green: workspace build (debug + release), `cargo test`, `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy --all-features -D warnings`. New API unit test passes.

Motivation: opening PeterLemon / homebrew test ROMs directly in the GUI (came up while pulling the HDMA-wave demo as a reference for a new OpenSNES example).

author: perly6185-lab
body:
Capability-review item ① (回溯能力), redone cleanly on current main after a concurrent-terminal session garbled the first attempt (fake commit, missing web files). The retention archive (#742) wrote cap-evicted rows to `<stateDir>/archive/*.jsonl` but only ever **wrote** — an audit could grep the file by hand, nothing read it back. This closes that upward audit loop for recovery actions.

- `retentionArchive.readArchive(collection, {filter, limit})` — parses the append-only file, **orders by `archivedAt`** (a single eviction batch is written newest-first, so raw file order would misrank within a batch; the stable sort preserves batch order on ties), applies a row filter, bounds the result, and **tolerates a torn final line** (crash mid-append).
- `GET /api/applications/:id/recovery-archive?limit=N` — scoped to one application behind the existing `denyForeignApplication` tenancy guard plus a `findApplication` existence check (404 on unknown); read-only.
- Inspector: a collapsed **"Archived recovery actions"** list that fetches on open.

## Product Flow
- Role flow: auditor reconstructing a recovery decision evicted from the live 200-row window
- Scenario: a recovery action from weeks ago rolled past the cap — the inspector's Archived list (or one GET) returns the full row with its eviction timestamp instead of "it never happened"
- Frequency: low (reads only during audits; writes already happen at cap overflow)
- Owner surface: Applications inspector recovery area; `GET /api/applications/:id/recovery-archive`
- Usability task: answer "what happened to recovery action X?" after the window rolled past it
- What not to show: other applications' archived rows, a throw on a missing/torn file, or a query before the list is opened
- Partial acceptance or follow-up: acceptance below; a tail-read (vs full-file) is the follow-up if archives outgrow memory

## Verification
- apps/server: full suite green (exit code 0). New `retention-archive.test.mjs` case: two eviction batches read back most-recently-archived first, filter by row field, limit bound, torn line skipped, missing file → empty. New `application-recovery-archive.test.mjs` (endpoint, real HTTP): returns only this application's rows newest-first, `limit` bounds, app B gets only its row, unknown application → 404.
- apps/web: 23 files / 110 tests pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Acceptance: an evicted recovery action is recoverable per application, scoped and ordered, with unknown apps rejected.
- Security review: read-only; the same `denyForeignApplication` guard as every per-application route plus an existence check; the archive lives in the state directory (same trust domain that already persists these rows); rows carry no token material.
- Visual QA: the inspector addition is a collapsed `<details>` reusing existing muted-panel styling. Desktop and mobile viewport screenshots were **not** captured — this headless sandbox has no browser (standing limitation); additive to the inspector's existing responsive stack.

## Risk
Low: additive read path behind the existing guard; the write path and in-memory behavior are untouched.

Closes #762

author: vreich-ui
body:
## What this does

The first build session anchored to `PRODUCT_VISION.md` ("History is a first-class feature"): `/changes` becomes the attributed, immutable change ledger over the `changes.list/get/compare/restore` tools that shipped in S1. **UI only — no backend changes.**

- **Who/what/when/why at a glance.** Each row carries an actor chip (human / agent / system — the UI never assumes a human authored a change), a friendly title + entity ("Updated prompt · Research Agent"), the recorded reason, and a deterministic UTC timestamp. Calm visual language per the vision: quiet rows with subtle separators instead of stacked cards; color only where it carries meaning (attribution).
- **Progressive disclosure, selection reveals.** Expanding a row opens detail in place — attribution facts, run correlation, and a lazily-fetched field-level diff via `changes.compare`, cached per revision pair so most rows never load one. Timestamp-only churn is filtered out of the field chips and stated honestly ("plus timestamps" / "only timestamps changed"), as are the first-revision and non-structural cases. No JSON dumps, no schema walls.
- **Restore extends history, never rewrites it.** An explicit confirmation step states the append-only contract before `changes.restore` runs; on success the ledger reloads so the new `node.restored` event visibly lands at the top — the proof in the UI itself. Deletions restore from the parent revision, since the node no longer exists in the resulting one.
- **Filters + paging.** Actor-kind and operation filters map straight onto the server's filter args; cursor-based "Load older changes"; a sequence guard prevents a slow earlier request from clobbering a newer filter's results.
- **Overview Layer-2 awareness** (vision ▸ Attention hierarchy): recent changes made by agents or the system surface as an awareness item with per-actor counts and the latest event cited, deep-linking into the ledger. Human-only activity stays quiet — the supervisor's own edits are not news.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` · root suite **299 passed** (12 new ledger-model tests: presentation, filter args, diff range/summary incl. timestamp filtering, restore gating incl. the delete case, recent-changes attribution; plus 2 overview attention tests) · ui suite **21 passed** (4 new RTL tests: attributed rows + filter refetch, expand-in-place with cached lazy diff, restore confirmation + append-only status, cursor paging) · `npm run ui:build`.
- Live Playwright drive, **17 checks passed** against seeded agent/ui/human-attributed history: newest-first attributed rows with no raw JSON; actor filter narrows server-side; expanded detail answers who/why with `prompt` field chip and no `updatedAt` noise; restore confirmed → recorded as `node.restored` with `ui` source at the top of the ledger; Overview awareness cites agent activity and navigates to `/changes`; dark theme recolors chips via tokens; no horizontal scroll at 420 px.

## Deferred (intentional)

- History mode on the canvas (timeline scrubbing) and the configuration surface's History section — the S6 completion slice after S4. Node-scoped ledger filtering from the canvas rail is a natural follow-up once S4 touches selection.

author: nawaz-git
body:
## What this hardens

Grouped plainly:

- **Test infrastructure for the Electron side** — a Vitest harness (config, an `electron` module mock, co-located `*.test.ts` files) so the TypeScript main/renderer helpers finally have unit coverage. 84 tests today, plus a recipe for adding more.
- **Engine language / update defaults** — the bundled engine now defaults to auto-detect transcription language and English protocol output, and no longer polls GitHub for updates on headless hosts.
- **Failed-meeting visibility + retry** — a pipeline failure now writes an error sidecar next to the recording, surfaces the meeting as a *Failed* row with its error message, and offers a one-click **Retry** that re-imports the original audio. Previously a failed meeting silently vanished (silent data loss).
- **Atomic meeting writes + per-meeting locks + exact-suffix deletes + copy-based export** — every metadata/transcript write goes through write-to-temp-then-rename (no torn files if the app crashes mid-write); concurrent edits to one meeting serialize behind a per-meeting lock; sidecar discovery and delete match an exact filename-suffix grammar so a meeting can never claim or delete a sibling's media; exporting recorded audio/video copies the file instead of buffering the whole thing into memory.
- **Probe / watcher hygiene** — stopping the Chrome meeting-probe now clears its cached snapshot (no phantom "meeting detected" after a meeting is paused); the imported-folder watcher is rebuilt when the output folder changes; a recursive filesystem watch on a huge user-picked tree (Home/Documents/Desktop/Downloads) falls back to non-recursive.
- **Permission-verdict accuracy** — the engine writes its permission verdict as JSON under Application Support instead of world-readable `/tmp`, the onboarding reader prefers the fresh JSON and ignores a stale one, and a `broken` verdict maps to `denied`.
- **IPC validation + renderer sandbox** — main-process IPC handlers validate their inputs (meeting-id traversal guard, an open-path resolver, a spawn-path allow-list, output-folder validation) and the renderer now runs with `sandbox: true`.
- **Model memory lifecycle** — the ASR model lazy-loads on headless launch, unloads after an idle period to shrink idle RAM, and is kept resident (prewarmed) while a recording is in progress.

## Review hardening applied

After an adversarial review, four follow-up fixes landed on top:

- **Phantom-signal guard** — the Chrome probe can suspend for seconds inside its scripting call; on resume it could re-light a meeting that had been stopped mid-call. It now carries a generation epoch, and any probe tick whose epoch changed bails before writing a snapshot or signal.
- **Retry lifecycle** — the error sidecar is cleared only when a retry *succeeds*, not at kickoff, so a re-failed retry stays visible; a duplicate retry of the same meeting is rejected; and the per-meeting lock covers only validate + kickoff, never the whole import.
- **Model-load cancellation** — a model load cancelled by an unload can no longer resurrect the model: a cancelled load lands unloaded, the idle-unload fuse never fires during recording, and a failing final job still arms the fuse.
- **Verdict cadence** — the engine refreshes its permission verdict on a throttled idle cadence (never mid-call), and the reader treats a stale retained log as absent, so a dead engine can't out-rank live system state.

## Testing performed

- **84 Vitest tests pass locally** (Node 24; the CI job runs them on Node 22, verified compatible).
- **Engine XCTests run on this PR's CI for the first time.** This Mac has no Xcode, so the added Swift tests (pipeline queue, app-state gating, watch-loop cadence, permission-verdict file, error sidecar) have never executed on a runner until now — they run in the macOS `engine-tests` job.
- **All three Swift build variants compile clean** — debug, release, and the sandboxed App Store variant (`swift build` + `-c release` + `-c release -DAPPSTORE`).
- Electron `npm run typecheck` (node + web) and `npm run build` are green.

## CI note

This PR includes the same root CI workflow commit that the CI-bootstrap PR (#1) and the capture-stability PR (#2) carry. On a rebase-merge it de-duplicates automatically as an identical patch, so whichever of those merges first brings the workflow in and this PR's copy simply drops out. On top of it, this PR adds one delta it owns: a **blocking `npm run test` step** in the `electron-checks` job. The bootstrap workflow typechecks and builds the Electron app but never runs the unit suite — without this step the Vitest tests would exist but never gate a PR.

**Recommended merge order:** #1 / #2 → diarization → UX → this (hardening merges last and rebases over each).

## Risk / rollback

- All changes are **additive** — new files, new fields, new steps — chosen so the last-in-line rebase over the capture, diarization, and UX branches stays trivial.
- **Riskiest change:** the renderer `sandbox: true` flip. It needs the manual renderer smoke listed below (can't be exercised in a headless shell). Rollback is a one-line revert to `sandbox: false`.
- The permission-verdict file moved off `/tmp`; the reader keeps a one-release `/tmp` fallback so a still-installed older engine build keeps working. No data migration — the verdict is recomputed on each check.
- Idle model-unload is guarded to never fire during a recording; if it ever misbehaves the idle timer can be disabled without touching the transcription path.
- Whole-PR rollback is simply not merging — no on-disk format is destructively changed.

## Follow-ups

**Deferred work that needs other branches merged first** (it touches regions the capture and diarization branches own, so it lands after those merge):

- Streamed recording finalize (removes the large stop-time memory spike) and crash-salvage of a partial recording — both layer on top of the capture branch's already-shipped async-stop rework.
- Quit contract, "probe says gone vs. actually gone" plus split/resume handling, destructive-action guards with truthful tray state, a sleep assertion, disk-full honesty, and mic-start retry — all sit in capture-owned recording-state regions.
- A settings bridge and an import FIFO — ride on the diarization branch's widened engine-config wire.
- A "notifications muted" onboarding banner — the data is already plumbed and tested; only the banner copy remains, deferred because that surface is being reworked elsewhere.

author: comicbit
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in, authenticated Hermes-to-Hermes integration for the official Agent2Agent Protocol 1.0. A Hermes instance can expose a task-oriented A2A endpoint and contact named peers through `hermes a2a`, including card discovery, send/get/list/cancel, and explicit context continuation.

The integration follows Hermes' narrow-waist model: the agent uses a plugin-local CLI skill instead of gaining a permanent model tool, and the official SDK is isolated behind the optional `a2a` extra.

## Why / integration gap

Hermes' existing platform path is designed around messaging delivery. A standards-compliant A2A endpoint additionally needs synchronous request/response dispatch, protocol task ownership and cancellation, and a host-enforced tool boundary. This PR adds those generic gateway contracts and consumes them from the A2A platform rather than introducing an A2A-specific bypass in the agent core.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Security hardening
- [x] Documentation update
- [x] Tests
- [x] Plugin-local skill

## Changes Made

- Add an official `a2a-sdk==1.1.0` server/client plugin with Agent Card and JSON-RPC task lifecycle support.
- Add profile-scoped named peers, inbound principals, dedicated credentials, and context state through `hermes a2a`.
- Add generic platform request dispatch, canonical session interruption, bounded two-phase teardown, and platform-scoped agent tool policies.
- Package an A2A-specific CLI skill and user/CLI documentation.

## Security and compatibility

- The listener binds to loopback; remote ingress requires a configured HTTPS URL through a private overlay or trusted reverse proxy.
- Inbound principals and outbound peers use dedicated credentials; `API_SERVER_KEY` and arbitrary request URLs are rejected.
- Credentials stay in a profile-local, permission-restricted store rather than config or environment files.
- A2A disables gateway slash commands and inbound local context-reference expansion.
- The platform uses an exact explicit tool allowlist; the default `configured` policy preserves existing platform behavior.
- Streaming, push notifications, and extended cards are not exposed.

## Validation

- 161 focused A2A and lifecycle tests passed locally.
- 704 gateway/plugin/tool-policy tests passed locally; 1 skipped.
- Official client/server interoperability passed locally.
- Wheel/sdist packaging, lockfile, Ruff, compilation, and diff checks passed.
- The exact pushed SHA also passed 161 focused tests and official interoperability on Linux/Norbert.

This is intentionally a draft while it is rebased onto current `main`; the branch base is 67 commits behind and overlaps recent upstream edits in four files.

author: ddehilster
body:
## Summary

Adds **`languages/English/en-roots.kbb`** — the inverse of `en-full.kbb`. Where `en-full.kbb` is keyed by surface word with each inflected reading pointing back via `root=<lemma>`, this table makes the **root/lemma the parent concept** and its **conjugations/plurals the children**, each carrying its morphological features. This is the shape a text generator wants: look up a lemma, walk its children, pick the surface form matching the desired features.

```
roots
  go:
    goes:
      m01: pos=noun number=plural
      m02: pos=verb vform=pres3sg tense=present person=3 number=singular
    going: pos=verb vform=ger
    gone: pos=verb vform=pastpart
    went: pos=verb vform=past tense=past
```

- **58,299 roots / 92,691 inflected readings.**
- Irregulars gather correctly: `went→go`, `mice→mouse`, `children→child`, `feet→foot`.
- Format mirrors `en-full.kbb` exactly (2-space indent, space-separated attrs, `m01/m02` for multi-reading forms, single readings inlined) — loads with the same parser. The redundant `root=` attribute is dropped from children (the parent *is* the root).

## Adjective comparatives / superlatives

`en-full.kbb` encodes **no degree information** (comparatives like `bigger`/`happier` are bare `pos=adj` with no link). The generator derives these links morphologically and keeps only forms **attested as adjectives** in the dictionary — it never invents a surface form:

- **3,386 degree links**, e.g. `good→better/best`, `big→bigger/biggest`, `happy→happier/happiest`, `large→larger/largest`, `far→farther/further/farthest/furthest`, `little→less/lesser/least/littler/littlest`.
- Handles the `-e`, consonant+`-y→-ier`, and CVC-doubling spelling rules, plus a small suppletive table (`good/bad/far/little`).
- Children are tagged `pos=adj degree=comparative|superlative`.

## Tooling

`python/kbb_roots.py` regenerates the whole table (including degree derivation):

```
python kbb_roots.py en-full.kbb en-roots.kbb
```

## Note

Follow-up to #189 (already merged), which added the other English KBB lookup tables.

body:
## What

Two docs improvements you asked for:

1. **Current-decision TL;DRs.** ADR **0008** (7 amendments) and **0009** (9) had grown so amended that the *present* decision was scattered across the original + N amendments — a reader had to do amendment-archaeology to answer "what do we actually do now." Each now opens with a **"Current decision (as amended)"** header stating the present state in one place; the amendments stay below as the reasoning trail (the *why*).

2. **CLAUDE.md — "assess architectural fit, always."** Issues, PRs, and reviews must weigh a change against the ADRs, not just local correctness: does it round-trip **all** ADR-0011 surfaces (recognise + emit + declare — no recognition-only debt, epic #574), fit the ADR-0008 compiler waist, conform to the ADR-0013 recogniser contract, and sit right in the DAG? A locally-correct but off-pattern change *is* tech debt — flag it in the issue/PR/review, not after merge. Plus a rule: past ~3–4 amendments, prefer a **superseding** ADR over amendment N+1 (0009 is the cautionary tale).

Docs-only. No content deleted — the TL;DRs summarise, they don't replace the amendment history.

author: edithatogo
body:
🎯 **What:** Replaced the use of `self.random.randrange` (which relies on Python's built-in insecure PRNG) with `secrets.randbelow` in the initial placement of agents in the `InnovationModel`.
⚠️ **Risk:** The built-in random module is predictable and insecure for cryptographically sensitive operations. Although this is primarily an Agent-Based Model, utilizing insecure randomness could theoretically allow an attacker to predict the random distribution of agents if the initial state coordinates were somehow exposed/manipulated.
🛡️ **Solution:** Used `secrets.randbelow` which pulls from the OS's cryptographically secure random number generator instead of a predictable PRNG, mitigating the vulnerability.

author: pnrxa
body:
Fixes #352.

## What broke

The Commander's Bundle product page (tcg 648686) lost its card sections: "In the box" (Arcane Signet, Sol Ring, Swiftfoot Boots — tle 315–317) and "Chance to be in the box" (the 2-random-of-10 pool — tle 305–314), leaving only a bare **1× Commander's Bundle** line in "What's in the box".

## Root cause

MTGJSON switched this product from `contents: null` (our curated fallback filled it) to a partial description:

- a `deck` reference `{name: "Commander's Bundle", set: "tla"}` that exists in **no** MTGJSON deck data — it resolves to zero cards and renders as the bare textual line;
- the 9 Play + 1 Collector boosters (linked), whose sealed recursion gives the product `booster` membership rows.

Those booster rows make the product count as "described by MTGJSON", so the fallback's *only-when-upstream-emitted-zero-rows* gate made our correct curated entry step aside entirely — the regression.

## The fix: supplement, don't replace

Upstream's data is **kept as-is** — "What's in the box" still renders MTGJSON's composition, including the "1× Commander's Bundle" deck line and the textual land packs. A fallback entry can now be flagged `"supplement": true`: its membership rows merge **alongside** upstream's even when the product is covered, carrying the axis upstream is missing (the dangling deck's cards; the land packs at card level). Properties:

- **Add-only**: upstream rows are never touched; the production-code change is a single gate condition in `merge_fallback`.
- **Self-retires per card**: when MTGJSON ships the real deck, rows they author identically dedup away via the `(product, card, membership, foil)` row set / unique key — the same pattern as the SLD bonus-pool pass from #350. The `variable` pool rows stay valuable regardless (an MTGJSON deck can't express "2 random of 10"), and the land rows stay (upstream keeps bundle land packs textual).
- The entry's authored `components` remain gated to only-when-upstream-empty — a safety net if upstream ever regresses to `contents: null`.

Result on the bundle page: **In the box** = the 3 staples + the 10 land printings · **Chance to be in the box** = the pool of 10 · boosters and box contents exactly as MTGJSON describes.

## Land packs (new)

Per Wizards' ["Collecting Avatar: The Last Airbender"](https://magic.wizards.com/en/news/feature/collecting-avatar-the-last-airbender), each 15-card land pack (one traditional-foil, one nonfoil) contains 5 full-art **Appa** lands (tla 287–291) + 10 default-frame basics (tla 282–286), and — per the article's explicit correction — **no** Avatar's Journey lands (292–296) despite the packaging. Those 10 printings are `contains` rows in both finishes.

## Verification

- `cargo check` + `cargo test`: **715 passed, 0 failed** (19 ignored = env-gated PG/Redis), on current main (post-#350/#351 `ingest/` split).
- New tests: supplement merges alongside a covered product (upstream rows untouched, duplicates dedup), plus a shipped-data end-to-end regression test simulating the exact new upstream shape (validated against the live TLA.json) asserting memberships gain the staples/pool/lands while upstream's booster rows and its deck-line composition stay verbatim; shipped-data pins for the flag + all 20 land rows.
- All referenced printings verified present in the catalog (names + finishes) against the dev DB.
- Two rounds of multi-agent adversarial review (opus): the earlier replace-based design's one confirmed finding led to this simpler rework; the final supplement diff came back with **zero findings**.

## Notes

- No migration; the fallback content-hash change forces the sealed-contents rebuild automatically on the next sync.
- The Commander's Bundle **Case** (648694) shows no guaranteed/pool cards — unchanged from before the regression; can be a follow-up if wanted.
- Pre-existing repo-wide rustfmt version drift left untouched.

author: chertov
body:
## What changed

- Added contextual `using` and `await using` declarations, including classic `for` and `for-of` heads and their static errors.
- Added immutable resource bindings and bytecode/runtime registration.
- Added ordered scope-owned sync/async resource stacks with LIFO disposal and correct `SuppressedError` nesting.
- Added suspendable disposal across functions, resumed async functions, async generators, lexical blocks, try bodies, classic loops, and each `for-of` iteration.
- Added an engine-compatible `deepEqual.js` Test262 harness without enabling unsupported tagged-template execution.
- Tightened lexical binding, Annex B duplicate-function, class-name, and `for-of` head/body conflict early errors.
- Added direct integration tests for normal and abrupt sync cleanup, initializer failures, mixed async cleanup, nested blocks, and per-iteration disposal.

## Why

The engine already exposed `DisposableStack` and `AsyncDisposableStack`, but explicit resource management syntax could not use those semantics. This connects parser, binding layout, bytecode control flow, Promise continuations, GC roots, and scope teardown without global state or blocking async disposal.

## Noteworthy decisions

- Every declaration owns one intrinsic stack entry so mixed `using` / `await using` declarations preserve exact declaration order.
- Async scope exit is represented as a Promise reaction plus parked bytecode completion, preserving return/throw/break completion while disposal suspends.
- Script-goal top-level resource declarations remain syntax errors. The four focused residual variants are module-only top-level cases and require a future module source-goal API.
- The Annex B duplicate declaration exception applies only to ordinary functions in sloppy blocks, not async/generator declarations or switch clauses.

## Validation

- `RSQJS_FAST_RUNNER=1 ./scripts/check-fast.sh`
- `./scripts/check-test262-focused.sh language/statements/using`: 150/152 variants, 76/78 files; only module-goal cases fail.
- `./scripts/check-test262-focused.sh language/statements/await-using`: 182/184 variants, 92/94 files; only module-goal cases fail.
- Exact regression slice: 65/65 variants passed.
- `cargo test --test resource_management_syntax`: 5 passed.
- Exact-tree correctness CI: [run 29195548765](https://github.com/surveria/rs-quickjs/actions/runs/29195548765), 76,708/76,708 expected passes preserved, 76,708 full-corpus variants passed, 25,870 failed.
- Correctness artifact: `rsqjs-correctness-<tree-sha>` from run 29195548765.

body:
## What changed
CodeRabbit (on #274/#275) caught a real consumer break my earlier CI fix had papered over: the generated app's config defaults to **sqlite**, but the dependency rework slimmed both the `standard` extra and the scaffold dependency to `arvel[standard]` — which carries no database driver. A real consumer's `arvel new` + `uv sync` app crashed `migrate` with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sqlalchemy'`. The e2e smoke missed it because it runs scaffolds inside the dev environment; my #274 test fix then pinned the broken template output as if it were the intended contract.

- The skeleton now emits `dependencies = ["arvel[standard,sqlite]"]` — `standard` itself stays deliberately slim.
- `test_console_new` re-pins the *working* contract, with the rationale in a comment.
- Also applies CodeRabbit's #273 nit: `test_media_library` clears its class-level model connections before disposing the resolver.

## How it was verified (real consumer path, both directions)
In a scratch dir with a **bare venv** (no dev extras):
- scaffold + install `arvel[standard]` only → `migrate` crashes `ModuleNotFoundError: sqlalchemy` (the exact break).
- scaffold + install `arvel[standard,sqlite]` (what the template now emits) → **`migrated 10 migration(s)`**, clean shutdown.
- Full gate suite + e2e smoke PASS.
